Aryan Republican Army.description: White nationalist terrorist gang that robbed 22 banks in the Midwest from 1994 to 1996. Founded in 1992 by Donna Langan and Richard Lee Guthrie Jr., the group stockpiled weapons for a race war and allegedly conspired with Timothy McVeigh. Members were arrested in 1996 after informants cooperated with the FBI.

Asano-gumi.description: The Asano-gumi is a yakuza group based in Okayama, Japan, formed in 1945 as the Oyama-ikka and restarted as the Asano-gumi in 1952. It has been involved in conflicts with the Yamaguchi-gumi and Kyodo-kai. Since 1996, it has been a member of the anti-Yamaguchi federation Gosha-kai. The group has approximately 40 members.

Ashkenazum.description: Organized crime group active in Argentina in the early 20th century, founded by Simon Rubinstein as a splinter from Zwi Migdal. Specialized in sex trafficking of Eastern European Jewish girls and silk smuggling. Operated in Buenos Aires with up to 700 agents.

Ashok Mahto gang.description: Indian criminal gang active in Bihar, led by Ashok Mahto and Pintu Mahto. Responsible for the 2005 killing of MP Rajo Singh and numerous caste-related murders in the late 1990s. Engaged in a long-running rivalry with the Akhilesh Singh gang, rooted in caste conflict between Koeris and Bhumihars. The gang operated primarily in Nawada, Nalanda, and Sheikhpura districts.

Asian Boyz.description: The Asian Boyz are a street gang based in Southern California, founded in the late 1980s by Cambodian refugees to protect themselves from other gangs. The gang has 2,000 to 5,000 active members, primarily Southeast Asian, and is involved in drug trafficking, robbery, assault, and homicide. They are active in 28 cities across 14 U.S. states and have ties to the Crips.

Aston Villa Hardcore.description: Football hooligan firm associated with Aston Villa FC, based in Birmingham, England. Active since circa 1993, following earlier firms the Steamers, C-Crew and Villa Youth. Known for clashes with rival firms such as Birmingham City's Zulu Warriors and Chelsea Headhunters. Members have been involved in multiple violent incidents and received banning orders.

Atlantic Guards.description: The Atlantic Guards were a 19th-century American street gang active in New York City from the 1840s to the 1860s. They were one of the original Bowery gangs, known for nativist vigilante activities and street fighting against Irish American gangs like the Dead Rabbits. They wore a red stripe on their trousers as a uniform and were allied with the Bowery Boys. The gang participated in the Dead Rabbits Riot of 1857.

Atomwaffen Division.description: International far-right extremist and neo-Nazi network formed in 2015 and based in the Southern United States. It expanded across the US and several other countries, described as one of the most violent neo-Nazi movements of the 21st century. Members have been responsible for murders, bombings, and planned terrorist attacks. Designated as a terrorist group by multiple governments including the UK and Canada.

Autodefensas Campesinas de Casanare.description: Colombian regional paramilitary group founded in 1979 by Héctor José Buitrago Rodríguez. Initially engaged in land dispossession, drug trafficking, and extortion, later also using oil royalties and land holdings for financing. After Buitrago's capture in 1997, his son 'Martín Llanos' took control. The group fought a war with the AUC-affiliated Bloque Centauros and is still active.

Autodefensas Unidas de Colombia.description: Colombian far-right paramilitary, drug trafficking, and counterinsurgent organization active from 1997 to 2006. Formed on April 18, 1997, as a coalition of paramilitary groups to combat leftist guerrillas such as FARC-EP and ELN. Responsible for numerous human rights abuses, including massacres, forced displacement, and assassinations. Designated as a terrorist organization by Colombia, the EU, and the US until 2014. Demobilized in 2006, with some members later forming successor criminal groups.

Avenues (gang).description: The Avenues is a Mexican/Mexican American criminal street gang based in Los Angeles County, California. Originally a social club founded by the Flores brothers in the 1940s, it evolved into a violent criminal organization involved in drug trafficking, murder, and hate crimes. The gang is under the control of the Mexican Mafia in prison and has an estimated 800 members. It remains active as of the present day.

Axe Gang.description: The Axe Gang was a militant organisation active in Shanghai and surrounding areas of the Republic of China during the early 20th century. Originating among Anhui migrant workers, it evolved from labour mobilisation into a faction involved in political violence and assassinations amid the Warlord Era and early Nationalist period. Its most prominent leader was Wang Yaqiao. The group declined after Wang's assassination in 1936.

Azuma-gumi.description: The Azuma-gumi is a yakuza organization based in Osaka, Japan. It was registered as a designated yakuza group under the Organized Crime Countermeasures Law in August 1993. The group has an estimated 50 active members and maintains its headquarters in Nishinari, Osaka.

Azusa 13.description: Azusa 13 is a Mexican American street gang based in Azusa, California, founded in the 1960s. It is one of the most aggressive Sureño gangs, with around 400 active members. The gang is affiliated with the Mexican Mafia and engages in drug trafficking, extortion, and hate crimes, including a campaign of ethnic cleansing against African Americans. Many members have been indicted and convicted since 2011 for terrorizing African American residents.

Bacchus Motorcycle Club.description: Canadian outlaw motorcycle club founded in 1972 in Albert County, New Brunswick. It is the third largest Canadian one-percenter motorcycle club with seventeen chapters across five provinces. The club has been involved in drug trafficking and has expanded through patching over other clubs.

Bacon Brothers.description: The Bacon brothers are a trio of gangsters from Abbotsford, British Columbia, Canada, involved in drug trafficking and firearms offenses. They are implicated in multiple homicides in the Fraser Valley and Greater Vancouver area. The brothers rose from a middle-class background to become prominent figures in organized crime. Jonathan Bacon was murdered in 2011.

Badr Organization.description: Iraqi Shia Islamist political party and paramilitary organization, formed in 1982 as the military wing of the Supreme Council for Islamic Revolution in Iraq (SCIRI). Based in Iran during the Iran–Iraq War, it fought the Ba'athist regime of Saddam Hussein. After the 2003 US-led invasion, it integrated into Iraqi security forces and later became a political party. It is part of the Popular Mobilization Forces and has been active against ISIL.

country_links.evidence_quote: The organization was formed in Iran in 1982 as the military wing of the Supreme Council for Islamic Revolution in Iraq . It was based in Iran for two decades during the rule of Saddam Hussein and led by Iranian officers.

Bahala Na Gang.description: The Bahala Na Gang is a Filipino street gang founded in the early 1940s in Sampaloc, Manila, by Divino Talastas. It originated as a protective group against rival gangs and later expanded into criminal activities including drug and weapons trafficking. The gang spread to the United States and remains active, with alliances including Nuestra Familia.

country_links.evidence_quote: The Bahala Na Gang spread into Filipino immigrant communities in the United States, especially California .
country_links.context: The Bahala Na Gang spread into Filipino immigrant communities in the United States, especially California, with sets emerging in multiple cities.

Bailey Boys.description: Street gang based in Buffalo, New York, founded around 2011 and named after Bailey Avenue. Known for murder, robbery, drug trafficking, and racketeering. The gang gained notoriety after a 2012 shooting in Martin Luther King Jr. Park. Its leader Kenneth Pettway Jr. was arrested in 2018 on federal drug and RICO charges.

Bakassi Boys.description: Nigerian youth vigilante group that operated mainly in southeastern and south-southern Nigeria from 1998 to 2006. They targeted armed robbers, ritual killers, and kidnappers, often using machetes and guns, and were accused of extrajudicial killings. They claimed magical immunity to bullets, known as Odeshi. The group later rebranded as Anambra Vigilante Services.

Bala na Cara.description: Brazilian criminal organization based in Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul, founded in the early 2000s. Known for extreme violence, including executions with multiple shots to the face. Engages in drug trafficking, robberies, and murders. Allied with Comando Vermelho and active in southern Brazil, Uruguay, and Argentina.

Baltimore Crew.description: The Baltimore Crew was an Italian-American organized crime group based in Baltimore, Maryland, active from the 1920s to the 1990s. Originally independent, it became a faction of the Gambino crime family in 1955. The group was involved in gambling, extortion, loan sharking, drug trafficking, and murder. It was led by the Corbi family for much of its existence.

Bamboo Union.description: The Bamboo Union is the largest of Taiwan's three main criminal Triads, with roughly 20,000 members. Formed in 1957 by waishengren children in Taipei, it evolved from street-fighting to profiteering, engaging in protection, extortion, drug trafficking, and contract killings. The gang has historic ties to the Kuomintang and operates transnationally, with a presence in the United States, China, and other countries.

Banda della Comasina.description: Italian criminal group active in the 1970s in robberies, kidnappings, and weapons trafficking in the Comasina area of northern Milan. Controlled by Renato Vallanzasca, it was often at odds with the Turatello Crew. The group's most famous action was the kidnapping of Emanuela Trapani. It was active until 1987.

Banda della Magliana.description: The Banda della Magliana was a mafia-type criminal organization based in Rome, Italy, active from the late 1970s until 1999. It unified the fragmented local underworld under a single structure, engaging in kidnappings, gambling, drug trafficking, and robberies. The group had connections with other Italian criminal organizations, Masonic lodges, far-right terrorists, and intelligence services. It was involved in several high-profile Italian historical events, including the Moro case and the disappearance of Emanuela Orlandi.

In Denmark, the club has ten chapters and about 150 members involved in drug dealing, extortion, fraud, weapons trafficking, and violent crimes. The Danish Bandidos originated from the Morticians club, which rebranded as Undertakers and patched over by Bandidos in 1993. They were key participants in the Nordic Biker War (1994-1997) against the Hells Angels.

Barrio Azteca.description: Barrio Azteca is a Mexican-American criminal organization originating in El Paso, Texas, founded in 1986 as a prison gang. It has grown into a multinational criminal enterprise with thousands of members in the US and Mexico, primarily involved in drug trafficking, murder, and other organized crime. The group is allied with the Juárez Cartel and La Línea, and is known for its violent cross-border operations.

country_links.evidence_quote: The leader of Barrio Azteca, Arturo Gallegos Castrellón, better known for his nickname El Farmero, ordered the execution of two American consulate workers and a Mexican with ties to the agency in Ciudad Juárez on 13 March 2010.

country_links.context: Barrio Azteca operates in Mexico, carrying out attacks and controlling drug trafficking routes in Ciudad Juárez.

Barriox13.description: Barriox13 is a highly active Sureños street gang based in South Los Angeles, founded in the early 1970s near El Segundo Boulevard and San Pedro Street. The gang is divided into West Side and East Side factions, with over 5,000 members loyal to the Mexican Mafia. It is involved in narcotics, homicide, drug and human trafficking, and has expanded into Southern California and Mexico.

country_links.evidence_quote: expanded its influence to regions across Southern California, including Norwalk, Long Beach, San Bernardino, and Riverside, as well as across the border into Tijuana, Rosarito, and Tecate, Mexico.
country_links.context: The gang has expanded its influence across the border into Tijuana, Rosarito, and Tecate, Mexico.

Barrow Gang.description: The Barrow Gang was an American criminal group active from 1932 to 1934, led by Clyde Barrow and including Bonnie Parker. They robbed banks, stores, and gas stations across the Central United States during the Great Depression, killing at least nine police officers. The gang gained national notoriety during the 'public enemy era'.

Basilischi.description: Italian criminal organization founded in 1994 in Potenza, Basilicata, aiming to become the fifth mafia in southern Italy after Cosa Nostra, Camorra, 'Ndrangheta, and Sacra Corona Unita. It controlled illicit activities in the region but was significantly downsized after all its leaders were arrested by April 1999. Since then, the area's organized crime has been dominated by 'Ndrangheta clans from Rosarno.

Batavia Street Gang.description: New York independent street gang based in the Fourth Ward during the 1890s. Affiliated with the Eastman Gang, they were rivals of the Cherry Hill Gang. Known for a jewelry store robbery to fund costumes for a ball. Five members were arrested and tried in the incident.

Baxter Street Dudes.description: The Baxter Street Dudes was a New York City teenage street gang active in the 1870s, consisting of former newsboys and bootblacks. Founded by Baby-Face Willie, they operated the Grand Duke's Theatre from a basement on Baxter Street, which became their headquarters and a popular underworld hangout. The gang wrote and performed plays, musicals, and variety shows, and engaged in tax evasion, thievery, and charity.

Once called 'the most dangerous men in Europe' by the British Home Office. Currently led by Abdullah Baybaşin.

It trafficked cocaine, heroin, and marijuana, and engaged in human smuggling, money laundering, extortion, kidnapping, and murder. The cartel infiltrated Mexican government agencies and Interpol. It was declared disbanded in 2011 after the arrest of its last major lieutenant, though remnants continued fighting until 2017.

Benson Syndicate.description: The Benson Syndicate was a 19th-century criminal organization in the western United States that fraudulently executed or fabricated cadastral land surveys for the U.S. General Land Office. Led by John A. Benson, it operated from the mid-1870s to 1898, primarily in California with headquarters in San Francisco. The syndicate infiltrated government positions, including California Surveyors General, to award contracts and approve fraudulent surveys, affecting nearly 20 million acres. Its downfall began in 1885 when ground inspections were instituted.

Bergin Hunt and Fish Club.description: The Bergin Hunt and Fish Club was a former hangout of the Gambino crime family in Queens, New York. Despite its name, it was not a legitimate hunting or fishing club but a front for criminal activities such as truck hijacking and loansharking. The club consisted of two connected brick-front stores located at 98-04 101st Avenue in Ozone Park, Queens.

Known for armed robberies, drug trafficking, and extreme violence. Described as one of the largest and most sophisticated criminal conspiracies in Canada.

Bing Kong Tong.description: The Bing Kong Tong was one of the most powerful Tongs in San Francisco's Chinatown during the early 20th century. It was involved in violent Tong wars, particularly against the Hop Sing and Suey Sing Tongs. The organization was weakened by a decade-long war and state authorities, eventually emerging as a trade union, though suspected of remaining ties to organized crime.

Birmingham Boys.description: The Birmingham Boys were a street gang active in England from the 1910s to the 1930s, founded by Billy Kimber. They controlled racecourses in the Midlands and North, later expanding to London. They lost control of South East racecourses to the Sabini gang after the Epsom Road Battle. The gang engaged in bookmaking, assault, extortion, and other crimes.

Black Axe.description: The Black Axe is an international confraternity originating from Nigeria, founded in 1977 at the University of Benin. Originally a Pan-African student movement, it evolved into a criminal organization involved in cybercrime, human trafficking, drug trafficking, election fraud, and violence. The group has been described as a mafia-style gang and has been linked to the 1999 Obafemi Awolowo University massacre. Despite the Neo-Black Movement of Africa publicly distancing itself in 2024, the two are often considered synonymous.

country_links.evidence_quote: In 2016, almost two dozen Black Axe members were arrested in Italy for 'mafia conspiracy, drug trafficking, exploitation of prostitution and violent crimes.' A year later, more Black Axe members were suspected in other sex trafficking activities in Italy.

Black Cobra.description: Black Cobra is one of the largest immigrant street gangs in Denmark, founded in 2000 in Roskilde. With approximately 100 members, it operates in major Danish cities and has expanded into Sweden and Norway. The gang is involved in drug trafficking, robbery, extortion, and murder, and is known for its distinctive black and white shirts with a cobra emblem. It controls a youth gang called the Black Scorpions.

Black Diamond Riders Motorcycle Club.description: Canadian outlaw biker gang based in Toronto, founded in 1953 by Harry Paul Barnes. Known for extreme violence in the 1950s-1960s, including the 'Battle of Pebblestone' in 1962. Declined after conflict with Satan's Choice Motorcycle Club in the mid-1960s. Still active in the Greater Toronto area.

Black Disciples.description: The Black Disciples is an African American street gang founded in Chicago, Illinois in 1966 by David Barksdale. Originally formed as the Devil's Disciples, it later merged with the Gangster Disciples to form the Black Gangster Disciples Nation before splitting again. The gang is involved in various criminal activities including drug trafficking, murder, and racketeering, and remains active with thousands of members across multiple US states.

Black Dragons.description: Chinese-American criminal organization and street gang formed in 1980 by Chinese immigrants in Lincoln Heights, Los Angeles. Operated in Los Angeles and San Gabriel Valley, involved in both organized crime (extortion, prostitution, money laundering, narcotics, counterfeiting) and street-level crime (murder, robbery, home invasion). At its peak had over 100 core members. Dismantled in 2002-2003 after FBI's Operation Back Door, but reportedly revived around 2020.

Black Flag Army.description: The Black Flag Army was a splinter remnant of bandit and mercenary groups recruited from ethnic Zhuang and former Taiping soldiers, founded in the 1860s by Liu Yongfu. Based in northern Vietnam, they fought against French colonial forces and other bandits. The army was officially disbanded in 1885 but remnants continued guerrilla warfare.

Black Guerrilla Family.description: African American prison gang, street gang, and political organization founded in 1966 by George Jackson, George 'Big Jake' Lewis, and W.L. Nolen at San Quentin State Prison in California. It is a Marxist-Leninist revolutionary group promoting black power and prisoner dignity, involved in drug trafficking, burglary, and homicide. The BGF remains active with estimated 100-300 members and thousands of associates.

Formed in 1985 in Heidenheim an der Brenz by immigrants from Turkey, Italy, and former Yugoslavia. Engages in arms trafficking, drug trafficking, robbery, extortion, arson, prostitution, burglary, and vandalism. Claims to be a brotherhood rather than an outlaw motorcycle club or criminal organization.

Black Mafia.description: The Black Mafia was a Philadelphia-based African-American organized crime syndicate founded around 1969 by Samuel Christian. It controlled drug trafficking, extortion, and other rackets in Philadelphia and the Delaware Valley during the 1970s and early 1980s. The group was known for its use of intimidation and violence, with over 40 murders attributed to it. It became largely defunct by 1984, though a successor group, the Junior Black Mafia, operated until 1992.

Black Mafia Family.description: The Black Mafia Family (BMF) is a drug trafficking and money laundering organization founded in 1985 in Detroit, Michigan by brothers Demetrius and Terry Flenory. It distributed cocaine across the United States with ties to Mexican cartels and used a hip-hop record label as a front. The organization was dismantled by federal indictments in 2005, with the Flenory brothers sentenced to 30 years in prison.

Black P. Stones (Jungles).description: The Jungles faction of the Black P. Stones is a Bloods-affiliated street gang based in Baldwin Village, Los Angeles. Originating in the 1960s, it became one of the largest gangs in the city, involved in drug trafficking, weapons violations, robbery, assault, and murder. The gang has been targeted by FBI and LAPD investigations, including Operation Stone Cold in 2005.

Black Pistons Motorcycle Club.description: International outlaw motorcycle club founded in Neuwied, Germany in 2002. It serves as an official support club for the Outlaws Motorcycle Club, providing a recruitment source and conducting criminal activities on their behalf. The club has expanded throughout Europe, North America, and Asia, with over 70 chapters in the United States alone. Members are involved in drug trafficking, assault, extortion, and other crimes.

Black Spades.description: The Black Spades is a predominantly African-American street gang formed in the Bronxdale Houses in New York City during the late 1960s. It gained popularity in the 1970s and spread to other boroughs and states. In 2019, the gang rebranded as TBS New Direction, a community service group focusing on anti-violence and food distribution.

Black Tuna Gang.description: The Black Tuna Gang was a Miami-based drug smuggling organization in the 1970s, led by Robert Platshorn and Robert Meinster. They imported an estimated 500 tons of marijuana into the United States over 16 months. The gang was known for sophisticated methods, including radio code words and surveillance countermeasures. They were dismantled by a joint FBI-DEA operation, resulting in convictions of eight members.

Blekingegade Gang.description: Danish far-left criminal group active from 1972 to 1989. They committed robberies to finance the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP). The group was named after a street in Copenhagen where a weapons cache was discovered. They were known for extreme secrecy and brutality during heists.

Blood Family Mafia.description: Canadian street gang founded in 2006, active in Quebec, particularly in Quebec City, Côte-Nord, and Chaudière-Appalaches. Modelled after the Bloods and Central American maras, it engages in drug trafficking, torture, and murder. Known for conflict with the Hells Angels after refusing to pay a 10% tax. Current leader is David 'Pic' Turmel.

Blood Magic Gang.description: A gang of Russian serial killers organized in 2007 by 19-year-old Konstantin Shumkov in Irkutsk, Russia. The gang consisted of teenagers from dysfunctional families who murdered five elderly people, participated in one rape, and injured three others between January and June 2008. Members were sentenced to imprisonment in 2010.

Bloods.description: The Bloods are a predominantly African-American street gang founded in Los Angeles, California in 1972. They are known for their red attire and hand signs spelling 'Blood'. The gang consists of numerous subgroups called 'sets' and is engaged in drug trafficking, extortion, murder, robbery, and pimping. They have a long-standing rivalry with the Crips and have spread across the United States and Europe.

Bloody Tubs.description: The Bloody Tubs were a 19th-century gang of street thugs in Baltimore and Philadelphia, formed in the mid-1850s. They worked for Nativist Know Nothing politicians to commit election fraud, using violent tactics such as dunking opponents in slaughterhouse tubs. The gang reportedly planned to assassinate President-elect Abraham Lincoln in 1860. They were broken up by police after 1870 due to public outrage.

It emerged from the ERPAC and was active in the eastern plains of Colombia, particularly Meta department. The group was known for its brutality and had around 260 members. It was declared completely dismantled after the capture of its last leader in September 2017.

Born to Kill (gang).description: Born to Kill was a New York City-based street gang composed of first-generation Vietnamese immigrants, founded in 1988 by Tho Hoang "David" Thai. Active primarily in the 1980s and early 1990s, the gang engaged in drug trafficking, counterfeiting, extortion, and murder. Its main base of operations was Canal Street in Manhattan's Chinatown. The gang was largely dismantled by 1992 following arrests and prosecutions of its members.

Bottoms Gang.description: The Bottoms Gang was an American street gang based in St. Louis, Missouri, active from around 1905 to 1917. Founded by Frank Hussey and Anthony Foley, the gang engaged in voter intimidation, armed robbery, assault, illegal lottery, and murder. Its members were primarily Irish-American, and the gang was known for extreme violence and feuding with the larger Egan's Rats gang and the St. Louis Police Department. The gang ceased to exist by the time the United States entered World War I.

Bounty Hunter Watts Bloods.description: The Bounty Hunter Watts Bloods is a set of the Bloods gang alliance based in the Nickerson Gardens public housing projects in Watts, Los Angeles. Founded in 1969 by Gary Barker and Bobby Jack, it is known for its violent rivalry with the Grape Street Watts Crips. The gang has over 2,000 documented members and is involved in drug trafficking, robbery, and murder. A 2004 injunction limited members' movements.

Bowe Brothers.description: The Bowe Brothers were a criminal family in New York City during the early-to-mid-19th century, headed by Martin Bowe. The gang operated along the New York waterfront, engaging in theft, robbery, and fencing stolen goods. They were known as shooters, cutters, and thieves in the Fourth Ward, leading raids on dockyards and ships. The gang was active from around 1840 to 1860.

Bowery Boys.description: The Bowery Boys were a nativist, anti-Catholic, and anti-Irish criminal gang based in the Bowery neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, active from the 1830s to the 1860s. Founded by Mike Walsh and William Poole, the gang consisted of volunteer firemen and engaged in street fighting, knife fighting, assault, murder, robbery, arson, and rioting. They feuded with rival gangs such as the Dead Rabbits and were known for their distinctive uniform of a stovepipe hat, red shirt, and dark trousers tucked into boots.

Boyd Gang.description: The Boyd Gang was a Canadian criminal gang based in Toronto, Ontario, active in the late 1940s and early 1950s. Named after member Edwin Alonzo Boyd, the gang committed a series of bank robberies and jail breaks, gaining notoriety in the media. The gang was involved in the fatal shooting of a police detective in 1952. All members were eventually captured and the gang dissolved.

Bra Boys.description: The Bra Boys are a surf-culture gang founded and based in Maroubra, Sydney, Australia, in the 1990s. They are known for territorial violence, alleged links to organized crime, and community activism. The gang gained international attention with a 2007 documentary narrated by Russell Crowe. Members include the Abberton brothers and several professional athletes.

The club disbanded in 2006 after prominent members were indicted on racketeering and drug trafficking charges.

Cannonball Motorcycle Club.description: An outlaw motorcycle club founded in Helsinki, Finland in 1991 by Jari Uotila. It has eleven chapters in Finland and Estonia with over 200 members. Designated as an organized crime group by the Finnish National Bureau of Investigation. The club briefly disbanded in 2017 due to internal disputes but resumed operations.

Capriati clan.description: The Capriati clan is a criminal organization originating from Bari, Italy, active since the 1980s. Founded by Antonio Capriati, it is primarily involved in extortion and drug trafficking, operating mainly in the historic center of Bari. The clan has attempted to expand into other areas and infiltrate the economic fabric of the city. In 2023, a major operation dismantled its hierarchical structure, leading to numerous arrests.

Carecas do ABC.description: Brazilian skinhead group based in the ABC region of São Paulo, founded in 1987 as a dissident from Carecas do Subúrbio. The group accepts Afro-Brazilian members and declares itself nationalist and anti-communist, but uses swastikas and Nazi greetings. Members have been accused of several murders, including the beating death of Edson Néris da Silva. The group currently has 250 members and is less active than in the 1980s and 1990s.

Cartel de Buga.description: Colombian drug trafficking organization named by the DEA, led by Ramón Quintero Sanclemente and Duffay Gutiérrez. It was a rival of the Cali Cartel and operated primarily in the Valle del Cauca region. The group was involved in cocaine trafficking, money laundering, and other crimes. It was dismantled around 2012.

Cartel de la Costa.description: Colombian drug trafficking organization active from the 1980s to 1998, based in the Caribbean region of Colombia. It controlled drug trade routes to the Caribbean and Central America, initially operating autonomously and later as a franchise of the Medellín and Cali cartels. The group was led by José Rafael Abello Silva and later Alberto Orlández Gamboa. It dissolved in 1998 due to arrests, deaths, and the incursion of the AUC paramilitary group.

Cartel de La Guajira.description: Colombian-Venezuelan criminal organization based in Maicao, Colombia, operating in the La Guajira peninsula and the Venezuelan state of Zulia. Specializes in smuggling, drug trafficking, arms trafficking, extortion, kidnapping, and murder. Founded in Maicao, Colombia, and maintains alliances with the Cartel de los Soles.

Cartel de Medellín.description: The Medellín Cartel was a loose coalition of Colombian drug trafficking organizations based in Medellín, Colombia, that played a central role in the international cocaine trade during the late 1970s and 1980s. It was founded by Pablo Escobar, Carlos Lehder, Gonzalo Rodríguez Gacha, and the Ochoa brothers. The network was known for its violence, including terrorism and assassinations, and was designated a terrorist group by the United States. It was dismantled in the early 1990s following the death of Escobar.

Cartel del Dorado.description: Colombian criminal organization active from 1970 to 2010, based in Bogotá. It supplied narcotics to the Medellín Cartel and later became one of the world's largest after the decline of the Medellín and Cali cartels. Led by Justo Pastor Perafán and later Luis Caicedo, it engaged in drug trafficking, money laundering, extortion, kidnapping, human trafficking, and arms trafficking. The organization was dismantled after Caicedo's arrest in 2010.

Cartel del Norte del Valle.description: Colombian drug trafficking organization based in northern Valle del Cauca, active from the 1980s to 2008. It emerged after the fragmentation of the Cali Cartel in the mid-1990s and was known for its violence and internal betrayals. The cartel was led by Orlando Henao Montoya until his death in 1998, after which it split into factions led by Diego Montoya Sánchez and Wilber Alirio Varela. It was eventually dismantled, though small dissident groups remain active.

country_links.evidence_quote: the Norte del Valle cartel exported more than 1.2 million pounds – or 500 metric tons – of cocaine worth in excess of $10 billion from Colombia to Mexico and ultimately to the United States for resale.

Catania Mafia family.description: The Catania Mafia family is a crime family of the Sicilian Cosa Nostra that dominates organized crime in Catania and its province. Founded around 1925 by Antonino Saitta, it evolved into a powerful and violent faction under leaders like Giuseppe Calderone and Benedetto Santapaola. The organization is involved in extortion, drug trafficking, and infiltration of legitimate businesses, and remains active today under the Santapaola-Ercolano clan.

country_links.evidence_quote: Investigations by Italian anti-mafia authorities... revealed that the Santapaola Mafia family has played a central role in transnational criminal activities, with Malta emerging as a strategic hub for its illicit operations.
country_links.context: The Santapaola Mafia family uses Malta as a hub for money laundering and illegal online gambling operations.

aliases: Cash Been Long / Brothers For Life
CBL/BFL.description: American street gang based in Buffalo, New York, founded in 2009 in the Towne Gardens Housing Complex. Engages in drug trafficking (heroin, fentanyl, cocaine, crack, marijuana) and weapons racketeering. Involved in turf wars with rival gangs, including the Ronnie Gang. Members have been convicted under RICO statutes.

Cedar Block Piru.description: The Cedar Block Piru is a set of the Piru gang alliance, part of the larger Bloods gang alliance, formed around 1980 in the west side of Compton, California. It gained notability for its connection to rapper The Game, who has referenced the gang in his songs. The gang was involved in the 1992 murder of Allen King and his three children. Its territory includes multiple cities across the United States.

Cesarano clan.description: The Cesarano clan is a Camorra clan based in Castellammare di Stabia, Italy, founded in the 1980s by Ferdinando Cesarano. It operates in the Ponte Persica region and Pompei, engaging in extortion, racketeering, usury, and drug trafficking. The clan has been led by Nicola Esposito and currently by Luigi Di Martino. Ferdinando Cesarano was sentenced to life imprisonment in 2000.

country_links.evidence_quote: provenienti prevalentemente dai Paesi Bassi
country_links.context: The clan sources flowers, bulbs, and pottery from the Netherlands for its transport monopoly.

Chaldean mafia.description: The Chaldean mafia is a collective of criminal organizations composed of Chaldeans that emerged in the United States during the 1980s. It is active primarily in Detroit, as well as San Diego and Phoenix. The groups are involved in murder, arson, weapons trafficking, narcotics trafficking, money laundering, fraud, theft, counterfeiting, racketeering, alien smuggling, assault, kidnapping, and armed robbery. The organization was founded by Louis Akrawi, known as the 'Godfather of the Chaldean Mafia', who fled Iraq in 1968.

country_links.evidence_quote: In Detroit, Chaldean criminals are involved in distributing Canadian MDMA...
country_links.context: The Chaldean mafia distributes Canadian MDMA in Detroit.

Chambers Brothers.description: The Chambers Brothers were a criminal organization based in Detroit, Michigan, that dominated crack cocaine distribution in the city during the mid-1980s. Founded by four brothers from Marianna, Arkansas, the gang controlled over 50% of Detroit's crack trade, operating around 700 crack houses and generating $3 million daily. They were dismantled after a joint DEA and Detroit Police investigation led to their arrest in 1988 and conviction in 1989.

Chapare Cartel.description: Bolivian criminal organization dedicated to drug trafficking and human trafficking, operating in the Chapare region. It emerged from the merger of six coca growers' federations in the Chapare region, with origins dating back to 1964. The cartel is alleged to have strong connections with the Movement for Socialism political party and former president Evo Morales. Its current structure is unknown.

country_links.evidence_quote: In 2012, the Brazilian magazine Veja accused Evo Morales and his then minister Juan Ramón Quintana, of providing raw material for the production of drugs that were destined for Brazil
country_links.context: The cartel's raw material was destined for Brazil, and cartel members were arrested in Brazil for drug trafficking.

Charles Martel Group.description: French far-right anti-Arab militant group active from 1973 to 1987. Formed by veterans of the Organisation armée secrète, it targeted Algerian properties, businesses, and government offices in France. The group claimed responsibility for several bombings, including the 1973 Algerian consulate bombing in Marseille. Its status is inactive, with no members ever arrested.

Charlestown Gang.description: Irish American organized crime gang based in Charlestown, Boston, headed by the McLaughlin brothers. Active from the 1950s until 1966, the gang controlled gambling and loan sharking on the docks and carried out contract killings for the Patriarca and Genovese crime families. They were destroyed in a gang war with the Winter Hill Gang, resulting in the deaths or imprisonment of its leaders.

Charlton Street Gang.description: The Charlton Street Gang was a group of river pirates active on the Hudson River in New York City during the mid-19th century. They raided small cargo ships and later moved upriver, stealing a sloop in 1869 under leader Sadie the Goat. The gang engaged in kidnapping for ransom and flew the Jolly Roger flag. They dissolved by the end of the 1860s after conflicts with vigilantes.

Chechen mafia.description: One of the largest ethnic organized crime groups in the former Soviet Union, based in the North Caucasus and Moscow. Founded in the 1980s by Nikolay Suleimanov, it uses Chechen tribal structures (teip) and the abrek concept. Active in money laundering, racketeering, arms and drug trafficking, and cybercrime, with ties to Chechen separatism. Still active as of the present.

Chee Kung Tong.description: Chinese secret society established in 1880, with roots in 18th-century Fujian, China. It promoted Chinese values, customs, and democracy, and supported Sun Yat-sen's revolution. The organization spread to the United States and Canada, with headquarters in San Francisco. It remains active today.

country_links.evidence_quote: Additionally, there came to be a branch located in Victoria on Canada's Vancouver Island.
country_links.context: The organization established a branch in Victoria, Canada, and later had many lodges in British Columbia.

country_links.evidence_quote: The fraternity founded its headquarters in San Francisco in the United States.
country_links.context: The organization founded its headquarters in San Francisco and has an active presence there.

Cheetham Hill Gang.description: Organised crime group based in Cheetham, Manchester, England, established by the early 1980s. Engaged in drug trafficking, weapon trafficking, armed robbery, and other crimes. Known for turf wars with Moss Side and Salford gangs, and for controlling Manchester's club scene. At its peak between the late 1980s and early 2000s, still active as of present.

Cherry Hill Gang.description: The Cherry Hill Gang was a New York street gang formed in the 1890s, known as the 'dandies' of the underworld for their dress suits and metal-weighted walking sticks. They robbed wealthy victims and were considered the most vicious gang in the city by the early 20th century. Their main rivals were the Whyos, and internal feuds led to sub-gangs forming.

Chiapas–Guatemala Cartel.description: Mexican drug cartel active in Chiapas and Guatemala, founded in 2022 as a splinter group of the Sinaloa Cartel. It emerged after a power struggle and defection to the Jalisco New Generation Cartel. The group is involved in drug trafficking across the Guatemala-Mexico border and has published execution videos. Its founder was killed in 2025.

country_links.evidence_quote: In Guatemala, the cartel is primarily involved in illegal drug trafficking through the Guatemala–Mexico border, specifically the Chiapas- Huehuetenango land border.
country_links.context: The cartel operates in Guatemala, collaborating with local criminal groups and trafficking drugs across the border.

Chicago Outfit.description: Italian American Mafia crime family based in Chicago, Illinois, originating in the city's South Side in the early 1910s. Rose to power in the 1920s under Johnny Torrio and Al Capone during Prohibition. Involved in loansharking, illegal gambling, extortion, political corruption, and murder. Considered one of the most violent Mafia families in the U.S., with over 1,000 murders since the 1920s. Still active but in decline since the late 20th century.

country_links.evidence_quote: Giudice operated an illegal bookmaking business ... and allegedly operated a professional sporting business from Costa Rica ...
country_links.context: The Chicago Outfit operates an illegal sports gambling business through an online company based in Costa Rica.

Chicanos Motorcycle Club.description: International outlaw motorcycle club founded in Pritzwalk, Germany on 23 August 2003. Acts as a support club for the Bandidos. Operates chapters in multiple countries including Germany, Netherlands, Norway, Russia, Serbia, Sweden, Ukraine, and UAE. Known for violent conflicts with Hells Angels and other groups.

country_links.evidence_quote: An investigation into the Limburg Bandidos chapter in January 2016 revealed that an associated Chicanos branch, which was founded by the Bandidos' vice-president, provided recruits and engaged in threats, drug offenses and violent crimes on the Bandidos' behalf.
country_links.context: The Chicanos have a branch in the Netherlands that provides recruits and engages in threats, drug offenses, and violent crimes for the Bandidos.

Chichesters.description: The Chichesters were an Irish-American street gang based in the Five Points area of New York City, founded by John Chichester in the 1820s. They engaged in theft, illegal gambling, and robbery, and were allies of the Dead Rabbits against the Bowery Boys. The gang lasted for over 50 years before being absorbed by the Whyos after the American Civil War in 1865.

Chijon family.description: South Korean gang active from 1993 to 1994, founded by Kim Gi-hwan and six other former convicts and unemployed workers. The gang targeted wealthy individuals and engaged in murder, extortion, kidnapping, cannibalism, and rape. It was dismantled after a series of arrests.

Chosen Few Motorcycle Club.description: The Chosen Few Motorcycle Club is the first mixed-race 1%er outlaw motorcycle club, founded around 1959 in Los Angeles, California by Lionel Ricks and others. It has chapters across the United States and internationally in the Philippines. The club is known for its outlaw status and diverse membership.

Clan Abbinante.description: The Clan Abbinante is a Camorra organization operating in the northern area of Naples, specifically in the municipality of Marano di Napoli. Founded by Raffaele Abbinante, it was originally affiliated with the Nuvoletta clan and later became a trusted group of Paolo Di Lauro. The clan is involved in drug trafficking and cigarette smuggling, and has been engaged in violent feuds with rival clans. Key members include Raffaele, Guido, and Antonio Abbinante.

Clan Ascione.description: The Clan Ascione is a Camorra organization originating and operating in the Ercolano area of Italy. It emerged in the 1980s, defeating the Esposito clan in a local feud. The clan is involved in racketeering and other criminal activities. Its current status is unclear from the text.

Clan Cappello.description: The Clan Cappello is a Mafia organization and family originating from the province of Catania, Sicily, named after boss Salvatore Cappello. It is considered, together with the Catania family of Nitto Santapaola, the most powerful Mafia clan in eastern Sicily. The clan emerged from the earlier Ferlito-Pillera group and rose to prominence in the 1980s under Salvatore Cappello.

Clan Cava.description: The Clan Cava is a Camorra organization based in Quindici, province of Avellino, Italy. It has been involved in a bloody feud with the rival Graziano clan for over thirty years. The clan operates in the Vallo di Lauro, Baianese, Nolano, and other areas of Campania, engaging in extortion, contract rigging, usury, and drug trafficking. Despite state crackdowns, it remains one of the most influential clans in the province of Avellino.

Clan D'Alessandro.description: Camorra clan operating in the southern province of Naples, Italy, particularly in Castellammare di Stabia and the Scanzano district. Founded in the mid-1970s, it is involved in drug trafficking, money laundering, extortion, and murder. The clan has alliances with other Camorra and 'Ndrangheta groups and has expanded into Emilia-Romagna.

Clan De Luca Bossa.description: Camorra clan operating in the eastern suburbs of Naples, specifically Ponticelli and Cercola. Founded by Antonio De Luca Bossa, known as 'o sicco, born in 1971. The clan was hostile to the Fusco-Ponticelli and Sarno clans, engaging in a bloody war for territorial control. After the arrest of its founder and the killing of his successor Giuseppe Mignano, the clan was eliminated by the Sarno clan.

Clan dei Barcellonesi.description: Mafia clan originating from Barcellona Pozzo di Gotto, Sicily. Active since the second half of the 20th century, it was involved in the 1986 maxi-trial in Messina. The clan's structure is described as chaotic with shifting alliances, and it has connections with other mafia groups including the Santapaola family of Catania and Calabrian and Neapolitan organizations.

Clan dei Casalesi.description: The Clan dei Casalesi is one of the most powerful Camorra clans and criminal organizations in Italy. It was created by Antonio Bardellino and originated in the municipalities of San Cipriano d'Aversa and Casal di Principe in the second half of the 20th century. The clan is active in Spain, Switzerland, and Romania, involved in cocaine trafficking, prostitution, construction, and money laundering.

Clan dei Casamonica.description: The Clan dei Casamonica is a Romani mafia organization based in Rome, Italy, originating from Abruzzo and Molise. Founded in the late 1930s by Luciano Casamonica and Adelaide Spada, it evolved from semi-nomadic horse traders into a structured criminal group. The clan controls various illegal activities in Rome and Lazio, with ties to the Banda della Magliana. It remains active today.

Clan dei catanesi.description: The Clan dei catanesi was the Turin branch of the Catania-based Cursoti clan, active in the 1970s and early 1980s. It controlled gambling, prostitution, and heroin trafficking in Turin, supplied by the Milanese band of Angelo Epaminonda. The clan was dismantled by mass arrests in 1984 following the collaboration of several members, including boss Francesco Miano.

Clan dei Cursoti.description: Italian criminal organization originating from the Antico Corso area of Catania, Sicily. Active since the 1970s, it operated in northern Italy, especially Milan and Turin. The clan is divided into two factions, historically in conflict: the Milanese faction and the Catania faction. It was formed to counter the power of the Catania Mafia families led by Giuseppe Calderone and Benedetto Santapaola.

Clan dei marsigliesi.description: Italian-French criminal organization founded in Rome in 1973, operating between France and Italy during the early 1970s. Engaged in drug trafficking and lucrative kidnappings, becoming the first organized crime group to exert territorial control in Rome. It was composed of French ex-convicts from the Marseille milieu, linked to the French Connection.

Clan del Golfo.description: Colombian narcoparamilitary and terrorist organization that emerged after the demobilization of the United Self-Defense Forces of Colombia (AUC) between 2003 and 2006. It is considered the largest, most dangerous, and best-structured criminal group in Colombia, involved in drug trafficking, massacres, extortion, kidnapping, and other crimes. The group operates in hundreds of municipalities across Colombia and has an estimated 9,000 to 14,000 members. Its former leader Dairo Antonio Úsuga David (alias Otoniel) was captured in October 2021.

Clan Di Biasi.description: The Di Biasi clan, also known as 'i Faiano', was a Camorra organization operating in the Quartieri Spagnoli area of Naples, Italy. It emerged in the 1980s as a longa manus of the Giuliano clan. The clan was involved in drug trafficking and had a violent rivalry with the Russo clan, leading to multiple murders. In July 2008, a major police operation led to the arrest of several members, and the clan is now considered defunct.

Clan Di Cosola.description: Italian criminal organization based in Bari, founded in the 1980s by Antonio Di Cosola. Operates in the Carbonara, Ceglie del Campo, and Loseto neighborhoods. Involved in drug trafficking, extortion, and weapons possession. Weakened after the boss's collaboration with authorities.

Clan Di Lauro.description: The Clan Di Lauro is a Camorra organization based in the northern neighborhoods of Naples, Italy, founded by Paolo Di Lauro in 1982. At its peak in the 1990s and early 2000s, it earned over €500,000 daily from drug sales, making Secondigliano the largest open-air drug market in Europe. The clan was involved in a violent internal feud in 2004, leading to the Scissionisti di Secondigliano split. Its power declined after the arrest of Paolo Di Lauro in 2005.

country_links.evidence_quote: The Di Lauro clan funneled the money into real estate, buying dozens of flats in Naples, shops in France and the Netherlands... The clan also produces counterfeit clothes in the Netherlands.
country_links.context: The Di Lauro clan bought shops in the Netherlands and produces counterfeit clothes there.

Clan Fabbrocino.description: The Fabbrocino clan is a Camorra mafia-type criminal organization originating from the area between Ottaviano, San Gennaro Vesuviano, and San Giuseppe Vesuviano in Italy. It was founded by Mario Fabbrocino after breaking away from Michele Zaza's group. The clan controls a vast territory in the Vesuvian area and is involved in diverse criminal activities including extortion, vote-buying, and money laundering through legitimate businesses. Mario Fabbrocino was sentenced to life imprisonment for the murder of Roberto Cutolo.

Clan Galasso di Poggiomarino.description: The Clan Galasso di Poggiomarino was a Camorra organization operating in the hinterland east of Naples, based in Poggiomarino. Led by Pasquale Galasso and his brother Martino, it was considered one of the most powerful and ferocious clans in Camorra history, controlling neighboring municipalities and most public contracts in the province of Naples. The clan declined in the 1990s after Pasquale Galasso's arrest in 1992 and subsequent collaboration with justice.

Clan Gallo-Cavalieri.description: The Clan Gallo-Cavalieri is a Camorra clan based in Torre Annunziata, Italy, founded in the mid-1970s by Enrico Gallo and Pasquale Gallo. It is considered one of the richest, most powerful, and most violent Camorra clans. The clan was historically opposed to the Gionta clan, leading to a bloody feud. After Enrico Gallo's death in 1985, Pasquale Gallo led the clan in a war against Valentino Gionta, which ended through the intervention of Salvatore Riina.

country_links.evidence_quote: A metà degli anni ‘90 i Cavalieri spostarono i loro affari in Spagna e Paesi Bassi gestendo il traffico della marijuana, cocaina ed eroina...
country_links.context: The clan moved its drug trafficking operations to the Netherlands.

country_links.context: The clan moved its drug trafficking operations to Spain.

Clan Gionta.description: The Clan Gionta is a Camorra criminal organization based in Torre Annunziata, Italy. It emerged in the early 1980s under boss Valentino Gionta, engaging in cigarette smuggling, heroin trafficking, and control of the fish market. The clan was known for its violent conflicts with other Camorra groups and was heavily targeted by law enforcement, leading to the arrest of Valentino Gionta in 1985. Despite setbacks, the clan remains active with leadership passing to various members.

country_links.evidence_quote: Tra le accuse vi è il traffico dai Paesi Bassi di cocaina, hashish, marijuana .
country_links.context: The clan traffics cocaine, hashish, and marijuana from the Netherlands.

Clan Giuliano.description: The Clan Giuliano is a Camorra organization based in central Naples, founded by Pio Vittorio Giuliano in the 1950s. It was one of the most powerful criminal groups in Campania from the 1970s to the 1990s, involved in cigarette smuggling, drug trafficking, and counterfeiting. The clan operated in neighborhoods such as Forcella, San Gaetano, Maddalena, Piazza Garibaldi, and Piazza Mercato. Several family members became pentiti (collaborators with justice), leading to its decline.

Clan Graziano.description: The Clan Graziano is a Camorra clan originating from Quindici, Italy. It has been involved in a long-standing conflict with the rival Clan Cava since the 1980s, initially over post-earthquake reconstruction funds. The clan was part of the larger 'Clan dei Quindiciari' before splitting. It is known for the 2002 'Strage delle donne' massacre of three women from the Cava family.

Clan Lago.description: Camorra clan based in Pianura, a western suburb of Naples, Italy. Active primarily in the cement cycle, illegal building, extortion rackets, drug trafficking, and murders. Founded by Pietro Lago, who was arrested in 2004 and died in prison in 2014. The clan is now largely dismantled following arrests of key members.

Clan Licciardi.description: The Clan Licciardi is a powerful Camorra syndicate based in the Secondigliano district of Naples, Italy. Founded in the mid-1980s by Gennaro Licciardi, it transformed the area into a strategic hub for drug storage and trafficking. After Gennaro's death, leadership passed to his siblings, notably Maria Licciardi. The clan is part of the Alleanza di Secondigliano cartel and has been involved in internal conflicts and large-scale drug trafficking.

country_links.context: The clan is active in the Netherlands in the counterfeit goods sector.

Clan Lubrano-Ligato.description: Italian Camorra organization operating in Pignataro Maggiore, Caserta province. Founded in 1965 by Vincenzo Lubrano, it maintained close ties with the Nuvoletta clan and Cosa Nostra, including Totò Riina. The Ligato faction became dominant after the decline of the original Lubrano leadership. As of recent investigations, only the Ligato faction remains active.

Clan Magliulo.description: The Clan Magliulo was a Camorra syndicate based in Afragola, Italy, operating also in lower Lazio and Caserta. It was considered one of the most powerful Camorra families. Founded by Mario Magliulo, brother-in-law of Casalesi boss Antonio Bardellino, the clan was involved in construction contracts, control of shopping centers, drug trafficking, and a bloody feud with the Moccia clan. It suffered major asset seizures in 1990.

Clan Mariano.description: Italian Camorra criminal organization originating from the Quartieri Spagnoli in Naples. Founded in the 1980s by brothers Salvatore, Ciro, and Marco Mariano, former followers of the Giuliano brothers. It fought wars with the Faiano clan and the Secondigliano Alliance for control of the Quartieri Spagnoli.

Clan Matrone.description: The Clan Matrone is a Camorra criminal organization based in Scafati, Salerno, Italy. Founded in the 1970s, it aligned with the Nuova Famiglia against Raffaele Cutolo's Nuova Camorra Organizzata. The clan exerted near-total territorial control, often substituting for the state, and was involved in drug trafficking, extortion, and violent enforcement. Following the 2012 arrest of boss Francesco Matrone, the group became largely disarticulated, though a faction led by Giuseppe Buonocore attempted to revive its dominance until being dismantled in 2018.

Clan Mazzarella.description: The Clan Mazzarella is a Camorra criminal organization operating in several neighborhoods of Naples, Italy. Historically considered one of the most powerful Camorra clans, it was founded by the Zaza family in the 1940s and later came under the control of the Mazzarella brothers. Currently, it is divided into several branches, each with its own regent.

country_links.evidence_quote: L'ultimo capo del ramo Zaza, Salvatore Zaza, era coinvolto in un ampio piano di traffico internazionale di cocaina dal Perù verso l'Europa, con l'intenzione di acquisire il controllo totale del porto di Callao
country_links.context: The Zaza branch of the Mazzarella clan was involved in international cocaine trafficking from Peru to Europe.

country_links.context: The clan, operating from Barcelona, was involved in cocaine trafficking from Peru to Europe, aiming to control the Port of Callao.

Clan Mercante-Diomede.description: Italian criminal organization based in Bari, founded by a confederation of the Mercante and Diomede families. Active in drug trafficking and other illicit activities in several Bari neighborhoods. Known for the 'Strage di San Valentino' in 2000, a failed attack on a rival clan. The organization has been involved in violent turf wars.

Clan Misso.description: Camorra clan operating in the Rione Sanità district of Naples, Italy. Founded in the 1980s by Giuseppe Misso, known as 'o nasone. Specialized in bank robberies, postal office heists, and armored truck thefts, as well as usury, counterfeiting, and gold trafficking. Engaged in violent feuds with rival clans, including a split led by Salvatore Torino in 2005.

Clan Nuvoletta.description: Italian mafia clan based in Marano di Napoli, founded in the 1960s by the Nuvoletta brothers Angelo, Lorenzo, and Ciro. It was one of the most powerful clans between the 1970s and 1990s, involved in cigarette smuggling and heroin trafficking, with strong ties to Sicilian Cosa Nostra. After the deaths of its historical leaders in the 1990s-2000s, it was replaced by the Polverino and Orlando clans.

Clan Pariante.description: The Clan Pariante is a Camorra criminal organization operating in the western suburbs of Naples, specifically in the municipalities of Bacoli and Monte di Procida. Founded by Rosario Pariante, it was originally part of the Di Lauro clan before splitting in 2004, triggering the First Scampia feud. The clan is involved in drug trafficking and extortion. As of 2017, the regent is Genny Pariante, son of Rosario.

Clan Pecoraro-Renna.description: The Pecoraro-Renna clan is a Camorra clan originating from Battipaglia, Italy. Founded by Giovanni Pecoraro after his release from prison, it fought against the Cutolo and De Feo clans in the Sele Plain. After Giovanni's murder in 1988, his brothers Alfonso and Francesco took over, leading a bloody feud. The clan is involved in drug trafficking, extortion, usury, prostitution, and tax evasion, with operations in the Sele Plain and surrounding areas.

Clan Russo dei Quartieri Spagnoli.description: Camorra clan operating in the Quartieri Spagnoli neighborhood of Naples, Italy. Founded by Domenico Russo, known as 'Mimì dei cani', and later led by his sons. Engaged in drug trafficking, extortion, and a violent feud with the Di Biasi clan. The clan emerged victorious and continues to exert control over the area.

Clan Russo di Nola.description: The Clan Russo di Nola is a Camorra organization operating in Nola, Italy, founded by brothers Pasquale and Salvatore Russo in the 1980s. Originally lieutenants of Carmine Alfieri, they replaced the Alfieri clan after his downfall. Despite arrests of its leaders, the clan remains active and has expanded into new territories, forming alliances with other Camorra clans.

Clan Sacco-Bocchetti.description: The Clan Sacco-Bocchetti is a Camorra organization active in the northeastern suburbs of Naples, specifically in the San Pietro a Patierno and Secondigliano districts. It was named after Gennaro Sacco and Gaetano Bocchetti, the latter being a proponent of the Secondigliano Alliance. Gennaro Sacco was killed in a Camorra attack in 2009, and Mario Bocchetti was arrested in 2017. The clan is involved in drug trafficking and extortion.

Clan Sarno.description: Camorra clan based in Naples, Italy, formed in the early 1980s by the Sarno brothers (Ciro, Vincenzo, Luciano, Giuseppe, Pasquale). It emerged after the dissolution of the Nuova Famiglia and engaged in conflicts with the Alleanza di Secondigliano and the De Luca Bossa clan. The clan later allied with the Mazzarella and Misso families to form a dominant cartel in Naples.

Clan Serino.description: The Clan Serino is a Camorra organization originating from Sarno, Salerno, Italy. Founded by Aniello Serino, known as 'O' Pope', it was influential for over twenty years and affiliated with the Nuova Famiglia. The clan engaged in extortion, usury, drug trafficking, and video poker businesses, and infiltrated local government. As of 2019, it remains active but weakened.

Clan Vangone-Limelli.description: Camorra clan based in Trecase, Boscoreale and Boscotrecase, controlling arms and drug trafficking in the Vesuvian area and abroad. Originating from a split from the Gionta clan in the late 1970s-early 1980s, it is considered one of the richest, most powerful and ferocious Camorra clans. Its regent, Giuseppe Gallo, is a major international cocaine broker with direct contacts with South American cartels.

Clerkenwell crime syndicate.description: English criminal organization based in Clerkenwell, London, founded in the 1980s by Terry Adams and his brothers Tommy and Patrick. Allegedly one of the most powerful in the UK, involved in drug trafficking, extortion, gold bullion hijacking, and security fraud. Linked to 25 gangland murders and connections with South American drug cartels. Influence reportedly decreased from 2000 onwards.

Cleveland crime family.description: Italian American Mafia crime family based in Cleveland, Ohio, formed during the 1900s. Under boss John T. Scalish (1945-1976), it exerted influence over the Teamsters and skimmed Las Vegas casino revenue. Membership peaked at 60 made men in the 1950s. After a gang war in the late 1970s and subsequent convictions, the family weakened but remains active in illegal gambling and loansharking.

Colacurcio Organization.description: The Colacurcio Organization was a criminal group based in Seattle, Washington, founded in the 1950s by Frank Colacurcio. It operated strip clubs and vending machines as fronts for racketeering, prostitution, and money laundering. The organization was dismantled after a series of indictments in 2009-2010, culminating in Colacurcio Sr.'s death in 2010 and his son's conviction.

College Kidnappers.description: A Chicago-based group of University of Illinois alumni who kidnapped wealthy mobsters for ransom, active in the early 1930s. Led by Theodore 'Handsome Jack' Klutas, the group consisted of ten members. They targeted mobsters because they were unlikely to go to police and could pay ransoms.

Colombo crime family.description: The Colombo crime family is an Italian American Mafia crime family and one of the Five Families of New York City. Founded in 1928 by Joe Profaci, it is the youngest of the Five Families and has a history of instability and infighting, including three internal wars. The family engages in racketeering, gambling, loansharking, extortion, drug trafficking, and other criminal activities. It remains active, though weakened by leadership turnover and prosecutions.

Colorado crime family.description: Italian-American Mafia crime family based in Pueblo and Denver, Colorado. Originated as a bootlegging organization under the Carlino brothers in the 1920s, later taken over by Giuseppe Roma and evolved into the Denver branch of La Cosa Nostra. Engaged in extortion, loan sharking, drug trafficking, and other rackets. Believed defunct by the 2000s after the death of Clarence Smaldone.

Columbia Point Dawgs.description: Criminal organization and street gang based in Boston, Massachusetts, founded in 1988. Involved in murder, drug trafficking, and violence, with one of the largest drug operations in New England. Known for wearing Philadelphia Phillies or Pittsburgh Pirates hats and driving expensive vehicles. In 2015, 48 members were arrested in a major gang takedown.

Comanchero Motorcycle Club.description: The Comanchero Motorcycle Club is an outlaw motorcycle gang based in Australia, with chapters in Southeast Asia and New Zealand. Founded in 1968 by William George 'Jock' Ross in Sydney, the club is known for its violent history, including the 1984 Milperra massacre. The Comancheros are involved in drug trafficking and have been engaged in ongoing conflicts with rival clubs such as the Hells Angels and Bandidos.

Comando Vermelho.description: One of the two largest criminal organizations in Brazil, founded in 1979 at the Cândido Mendes prison on Ilha Grande, Rio de Janeiro. It originated from the Falange Vermelha and was created by Rogério Lemgruber. The group is heavily involved in drug trafficking and operates in multiple Brazilian states and several South American countries. It is designated as a terrorist organization by Argentina, Paraguay, and the United States.

Combat 18.description: Combat 18 is a neo-Nazi terrorist organization founded in 1992 in the United Kingdom. It originated as a stewarding group for the British National Party but later split and became openly violent. The group has been linked to murders of immigrants, dissidents, and German politician Walter Lübcke. It has been banned in Canada and Germany and is still active.

Commisso 'ndrina.description: The Commisso 'ndrina is a powerful clan of the 'Ndrangheta based in Siderno, Calabria, Italy, with a branch in the Greater Toronto Area, Canada. Founded in the 1930s by Antonio Macrì, it is involved in international drug trafficking, racketeering, money laundering, and extortion. The clan emerged as a dominant force in Siderno after the First 'Ndrangheta war and has been active in conflicts with rival clans such as the Costa 'ndrina.

Compton Executioners.description: The Compton Executioners is a deputy gang within the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department (LASD), based at the Compton station. Founded by former 2000 Boys member Andy Toone, its members share a distinctive calf tattoo. The gang is involved in police corruption and has been linked to the Lynwood Vikings. In July 2021, Congresswoman Maxine Waters called for a Department of Justice inquiry into the gang.

Continentals.description: The Continentals were a Chinese American street gang prominent in New York City's Chinatown in the early 1960s. Founded in 1961 by American-born Chinese high school students to protect Chinese students from attacks by other ethnic groups. The gang engaged primarily in non-violent crimes such as vandalism and had up to 100 members. It was active only from 1961 to 1964, succeeded by more violent gangs like the Ghost Shadows and Flying Dragons.

Contini clan.description: The Contini clan is a powerful Neapolitan Camorra clan operating in Naples, Italy, founded in the early 1980s by Edoardo Contini. It is a founding member of the Secondigliano Alliance and is active in drug trafficking, extortion, and money laundering. The clan has a strong presence in Europe, including Spain, the Netherlands, and Eastern Europe. It is considered one of the most powerful Camorra groups due to its lack of internal splits and informants.

Corleonesi.description: The Corleonesi was an alliance of Mafia families within the Sicilian Mafia, formed in the 1970s. Led by Luciano Leggio, Salvatore Riina, Bernardo Provenzano, and others, it took over the Sicilian Mafia Commission and imposed a dictatorship over Cosa Nostra. The coalition waged the Second Mafia War from 1978–1983 and dominated until 2006.

Cornbread Mafia.description: The Cornbread Mafia was a group of Kentucky men who operated the largest domestic marijuana production operation in U.S. history, based in central Kentucky. Founded in the late 1970s by Joe Keith Bickett and others, the group grew marijuana across 30 farms in 10 states. The term was first publicly used by federal prosecutors in 1989 after a massive bust. The group was known for its code of silence, which prevented a Continuing Criminal Enterprise prosecution.

Cortesi brothers.description: The Cortesi brothers were four Italian-descended siblings who operated as gangsters in London in the early 20th century. They engaged in protection racketeering of gamblers and bookmakers, and were rivals of the Sabini family. The brothers were involved in a violent confrontation at the Fratellanza Social Club in 1922, leading to arrests and convictions. The group was active from the 1900s until the deaths of the brothers between 1938 and 1972.

Cossacks Motorcycle Club.description: American outlaw motorcycle club founded in Tyler, Texas in 1969 by six bikers. One of the largest outlaw biker groups in Texas, known for conflicts with the Bandidos Motorcycle Club, including the 2015 Waco shootout. Has chapters in Texas, Ohio, Indiana, and Virginia.

Cotroni crime family.description: The Cotroni crime family was an Italian Canadian crime family based in Montreal, Quebec, established in the 1940s by Vincenzo Cotroni. It was considered a branch of the Bonanno crime family of New York City. The family controlled territory in southern Quebec and Ontario, engaging in racketeering, drug trafficking, and other illegal activities. An internal war in the late 1970s led to the rise of the Sicilian Rizzuto faction, and the family became defunct by the 2000s.

country_links.evidence_quote: Frank Cotroni was sentenced to seven years in prison after he and his son pleaded guilty to plotting to import 180 kilograms of cocaine from Colombia.

County Road Cutters.description: The County Road Cutters are a hooligan firm associated with Premier League football club Everton F.C. They were one of the largest hooligan firms in England during the 1980s and early 1990s. The firm is known for adopting casual clothing and designer garments in the 1970s and has been involved in high-profile clashes, including the 2005 'Battle of Everton Valley' with Manchester United's Red Army.

Cowboy Mafia.description: The Cowboy Mafia was a nickname for a group of marijuana smugglers operating in the United States during the 1970s. Based in Texas, they imported over 106 tons of marijuana from Colombia using shrimp boats. The group was arrested in 1978 and 26 members were convicted in 1979. Rex Cauble, considered the headman, was sentenced to 95 years.

country_links.evidence_quote: the group made six trips from Colombia to Texas
country_links.context: The group made six trips from Colombia to Texas to import marijuana.

Crazy Butch Gang.description: American juvenile street gang active in New York City's Lower East Side during the late 19th century, known for pickpocketing and sneak thievery. Founded by Simon Erenstoft ("Crazy Butch") around 1890, the gang was allied with the Eastman Gang and broke up after Butch's death in a gunfight.

Crazy Dragons.description: The Crazy Dragons are a street gang active in the Prairie provinces of Canada, founded in Edmonton, Alberta as a successor to the Vietnamese Trang gang. The gang is involved in drug trafficking, gunrunning, and violent crimes. It has expanded from Alberta into Saskatchewan and has become more ethnically diverse over time.

country_links.context: The Crazy Dragons import cocaine from Los Angeles.

Crips.description: The Crips are a primarily African-American alliance of street gangs based in Southern California, founded in Los Angeles in 1969 by Raymond Washington and Stanley Williams. They are one of the largest and most violent street gang associations in the United States, with an estimated 30,000 to 35,000 members in 2008. Members are involved in murders, robberies, and drug dealing, and have a long-standing rivalry with the Bloods.

Culver City Boys.description: Mexican-American street gang from Mar Vista, Los Angeles, California, founded in the 1960s. Engages in murder, drug trafficking, extortion, assault, auto theft, and robbery. Under a civil injunction enforced by the LAPD, but remains active.

Cuntrera-Caruana Mafia clan.description: The Cuntrera-Caruana Mafia clan was a Sicilian Mafia clan originating from Siculiana, Sicily, founded in the 1950s. It held a key position in international drug trafficking and money laundering for Cosa Nostra during the 1980s and 1990s, with operations extending to Canada and Venezuela. The clan was described by Italian prosecutors as an 'international holding' providing drug-trafficking routes and money-laundering channels. It was considered defunct by the 2000s.

It is involved in drug trafficking, particularly fentanyl and methamphetamine, and operates primarily in the border municipality of Caborca. The group is in conflict with Los Chapitos and La Mayiza over territory and drug routes. Despite the arrest of its founder in 2022, the organization remains active under new leadership.

Originally a cocaine trafficking group for Colombian cartels, it later specialized in methamphetamine. The cartel was dismantled in 2005 and some members joined the Jalisco New Generation Cartel.

Cártel de Jalisco Nueva Generación.description: Mexican criminal organization dedicated to drug trafficking and arms trafficking, designated as a foreign terrorist organization by the United States and Argentina. Founded in 2007 as an armed wing under the name Los Mata Zetas, it became independent in 2010 and emerged publicly in September 2011. Led by Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes (El Mencho) from 2009 until his death in 2026, it is considered one of the most dangerous criminal groups in Mexico and a rival of the Sinaloa Cartel.

Based in Guerrero and Morelos, it engaged in drug trafficking, extortion, kidnapping, and other crimes. The group was active until around 2022, when it was dismantled.

Cártel de Santa Rosa de Lima.description: Mexican criminal organization originating in Santa Rosa de Lima, Guanajuato, founded in 2014 by José Antonio Yépez Ortiz alias 'El Marro'. Known primarily for fuel theft (huachicoleo) and drug trafficking, it has been in violent conflict with the Jalisco New Generation Cartel. Despite leadership arrests, the group remains active.

Cártel de Tepalcatepec.description: Mexican criminal organization dedicated to drug trafficking, based in Tepalcatepec, Michoacán. Founded in 2018 by Juan José Farías Álvarez alias 'El Abuelo'. Known for violent confrontations with the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) and for using tactics such as explosive-laden drones and roadblocks. Currently operates under the protection of Carteles Unidos.

Cártel de Tláhuac.description: Mexican criminal group founded in 2012 by Felipe de Jesús Pérez Luna, alias El Ojos, operating primarily in Tláhuac, Iztapalapa, Milpa Alta, Xochimilco, and the State of Mexico. It emerged from splinter groups of the Beltrán Leyva Cartel and engages in drug trafficking, homicide, extortion, kidnapping, vehicle theft, fuel theft, and human trafficking. The group is currently led by relatives of El Ojos and remains active.

Cártel del Noreste.description: Mexican criminal and terrorist organization formed in 2015 after a split from Los Zetas following the capture of Omar Treviño Morales. Based in Nuevo Laredo, Tamaulipas, it engages in drug trafficking, kidnapping, extortion, human trafficking, money laundering, and murder. Designated as a foreign terrorist organization by the U.S. State Department in February 2025. Controls territory in several Mexican states and has operational presence in the United States, Guatemala, Honduras, and Colombia.

Cártel Independiente de Sonora.description: Mexican criminal federation dedicated to drug trafficking, extortion, money laundering, and other illegal activities. Originally formed as Gente Nueva, the armed wing of the Sinaloa Cartel, it became independent in 2023 after internal disputes with Los Chapitos. Based in Sonora, it operates in Chihuahua, Sonora, and Sinaloa, and is currently active.

Cárteles Unidos.description: Mexican criminal organization formed in 2010 to expel Los Zetas from Michoacán and Jalisco. Composed of members from various cartels including Tepalcatepec, Los Viagras, Sinaloa, La Familia Michoacana, Gulf, and Knights Templar. Known for drug trafficking in the Tierra Caliente region and ongoing conflict with CJNG. Designated as a foreign terrorist organization by the U.S. State Department in February 2025.

D'Aquila crime family.description: One of the earliest crime families in New York City, based in Manhattan's Little Italy. Founded by Salvatore D'Aquila in the 1910s after breaking off from the Morello family and absorbing remnants of the Brooklyn Camorra. Active in racketeering, extortion, and murder until D'Aquila's murder in 1928, after which the family was taken over by Manfredi Mineo and eventually became part of the modern Gambino crime family.

D-Block Boys.description: American criminal street gang based in Algiers, New Orleans, Louisiana, formed by teenagers from the DeGaulle Manor Public Housing Complex and Fischer Projects. Active from 2004 to 2017, involved in drug trafficking, multiple murders, and violent crimes. The gang was tracked by NOPD since the mid-2000s and listed as a threat by the FBI in 2011.

D-Company.description: Organized crime syndicate founded and controlled by Dawood Ibrahim, based in India. Established in the 1970s by Shabir Ibrahim Kaskar and Dawood Ibrahim. Involved in drug trafficking, extortion, murder, and terrorism, including the 1993 Bombay bombings and logistics for the 2008 Mumbai attacks. Designated as a Global Terrorist Organization by the U.S. Treasury.

D.C. Blacks.description: The D.C. Blacks is an African-American prison gang in the United States whose members are from Washington D.C. They are allied with the Black Guerrilla Family and rival the Aryan Brotherhood. Formed due to the concentration of D.C. inmates in federal facilities, they are one of the largest prison gangs within penitentiaries but smaller than gangs like the Bloods and Crips.
