Dallas crime family.description: The Dallas crime family, also known as the Civello crime family, was an Italian-American Mafia crime family based in Dallas, Texas. Founded around 1910 by Carlo Piranio, it operated primarily in the Dallas metropolitan area and throughout Texas, Oklahoma, and Arkansas. The family was involved in racketeering, loansharking, drug trafficking, and other criminal activities. It became defunct in the 1990s.

DarkMarket.description: DarkMarket was an English-language cybercrime forum created by Renukanth Subramaniam in London. It facilitated the buying and selling of stolen identities and credit card data, with 2,500 users at its peak. The forum was infiltrated by FBI agent J. Keith Mularski, leading to over 60 arrests worldwide. It was shut down in 2008, and Subramaniam was sentenced to nearly five years in prison in 2010.

Daybreak Boys.description: The Daybreak Boys was a New York City street gang formed in the late 1840s. Active along the waterfront, they were known for unprovoked murder, sabotage, and theft. By 1852, they were suspected of 20 to 40 murders and stealing $200,000 in goods. The gang was broken up by police in 1859 after several gunfights.

Dead Man Incorporated.description: Dead Man Incorporated (DMI) is a predominantly white organized crime enterprise founded in the late 1990s in the Maryland Department of Corrections by Perry Roark, James Sweeney, and Brian Jordan. Initially allied with the Black Guerrilla Family, the gang expanded into drug trafficking, murder, and other crimes. It operates in prisons and streets across Maryland, Virginia, and West Virginia, with an estimated 370 members. Internal divisions have emerged over ideology and direction.

Dead Rabbits.description: Irish American criminal street gang active in Lower Manhattan from the 1830s to 1860s. They were founded by disgruntled members of the Roach Guards and were known for their rivalry with the Bowery Boys. The gang engaged in street fighting, assault, murder, and rioting, and supported Tammany Hall politicians. Their symbol was a dead rabbit on a pike.

mentioned_in.title: Bandidos MC criminal allegations and incidents in Australia

DeCavalcante crime family.description: The DeCavalcante crime family is an Italian-American Mafia crime family operating primarily in North Jersey, particularly in Elizabeth, Newark, Linden, and West New York. Founded around the 1900s by Phil Amari, it is considered by some to be the 'Sixth Family' due to its strong ties with New York's Five Families. The family engages in racketeering, gambling, drug trafficking, extortion, and other illicit activities. It maintains alliances with several other Mafia families, including the Gambino and Philadelphia families.

Decepticons (gang).description: The Decepticons were a Brooklyn street gang active from the mid-1980s into the early 1990s. Named after the antagonists of the Transformers franchise, they were known for flash-mob style attacks and muggings. The gang originated in Brooklyn and expanded across New York City, with offshoots in Queens and the Bronx. Some former members later became notable in hip-hop music.

Detroit Partnership.description: The Detroit Partnership is an Italian American Mafia crime family based in Detroit, Michigan, founded around 1908 by Pietro Mirabile. It operates primarily in the Greater Detroit area, with additional territory in Ohio, Ontario, and Las Vegas. The family has been involved in racketeering, gambling, loan-sharking, labor racketeering, narcotics trafficking, and other illegal activities. Despite RICO prosecutions in the 1990s, the organization remains active in the 21st century.

Devil's Disciples Motorcycle Club (Canad.description: Canadian outlaw motorcycle club based in Greater Montreal, founded in late 1965. It was briefly the most powerful motorcycle gang in Montreal before disbanding in January 1976 after a biker war with the Popeyes. The club engaged in drug trafficking, intimidation, assault, and murder, and was known for its assassination attempt on singer Johnny Hallyday.

Dinner Set Gang.description: A gang of thieves active in the late 1960s and 1970s, known for burglarizing wealthy Americans' homes while the victims were at dinner. Based in the United States, the gang was led by brothers-in-law Peter Salerno and Dominick Latella. They stole millions in jewels, targeting families like the DuPonts and Flaglers. The gang avoided violence and carried no weapons.

Dirty Dozen Motorcycle Club.description: The Dirty Dozen Motorcycle Club was an outlaw motorcycle club based in Arizona, founded in 1964 by twelve founding members. It became the largest and most violent motorcycle gang in the state, involved in drug trafficking, arms trafficking, prostitution, assault, and murder. The club merged with the Hells Angels in 1997.

Dixon Bloods.description: Street gang based in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, founded in 2006. Involved in drug and weapons trafficking, operating from a highrise complex on Dixon Road. Dismantled in 2013 after Project Traveller, with 43 members arrested. Still considered active.

DLASTHR.description: Assyrian criminal organization active in southwestern Sydney, Australia, originating from the Assyrian Kings gang. Involved in drug trafficking, murders, and public shootings. Resurrected in the early 2000s under the name DLASTHR after the original gang dissolved following the murder of off-duty police officer David Carty in 1997.

Dnipropetrovsk Mafia.description: A group of Ukrainian oligarchs, politicians, and organized crime figures, and formerly Soviet politicians, based in Dnipro (formerly Dnipropetrovsk). It emerged after the Great Purge and was firmly established in the 1950s-1960s under Leonid Brezhnev. The group wielded powerful influence in Ukraine and was involved in black market activities. It declined after Brezhnev's death and Gorbachev's rise.

Doddington gang.description: Primarily Afro-Caribbean street gang based in Moss Side, Manchester, United Kingdom. Originated from the Pepperhill Crew in the 1980s and named after Dodington Close. Engaged in drug trafficking, weapon trafficking, robbery, kidnapping, and murder. Known for rivalries with the Cheetham Hill Gang and Gooch Close Gang, contributing to the 'Gunchester' era. Still active as of the 2000s.

Doghmush clan.description: A Palestinian clan from the Gaza Strip known for its long-running rivalry with Hamas. Involved in extortion, smuggling, arms dealing, and killings. Members have been affiliated with Fatah, Hamas, Popular Resistance Committees, and Al-Qaeda. The clan was behind the 2007 kidnapping of British journalist Alan Johnston.

Dojin-kai.description: The Dojin-kai is a yakuza organization headquartered in Kurume, Fukuoka, Japan, founded in 1971 by Isoji Koga. It is a designated yakuza syndicate with approximately 310 members, known for its militant nature and large-scale drug trafficking, particularly methamphetamine. The group has been involved in violent conflicts with other yakuza groups, including the Yamaguchi-gumi and its own splinter group, Kyushu Seido-kai.

Dominicans Don't Play.description: Dominicans Don't Play (DDP) is a Dominican-American street gang formed in Manhattan, New York, in 1991. Known for using machetes and knives, they are involved in drug trafficking, robbery, extortion, and murder. The gang operates across New York City, New Jersey, and internationally, with ties to Colombian cartels for cocaine distribution.

Downtown Gang.description: The Downtown Gang was a criminal organization based in Galveston, Texas, founded around 1920 by Johnny Jack Nounes. It dominated organized crime in Galveston during Prohibition, engaging in bootlegging, gambling, and other illegal activities. The gang had connections with the Chicago Outfit and New York mobsters. Formed in the late 1860s by Little Freddie, Mike Kurtz, and Johnny Irving, it grew to around 300 members. The gang operated in Manhattan's Bowery area, using staged street fights to pickpocket crowds. Police crackdowns in 1877 led to its dissolution.

East Harlem Purple Gang.description: The East Harlem Purple Gang was an Italian-American organized crime group based in New York City, active from the early 1970s to the 1980s. It consisted of hit-men and heroin dealers who were semi-independent from the Italian-American Mafia but allied with several crime families, particularly the Genovese family. The gang dominated heroin distribution in East Harlem, Italian Harlem, and the Bronx. At its peak, it had about 30 members and 80 associates, and was considered an unofficial sixth family.

Eastman Gang.description: The Eastman Gang was a predominantly Jewish-American street gang that dominated parts of the New York City underworld from the late 1890s to the early 1910s. Founded by Monk Eastman, the gang operated in Manhattan's Lower East Side, engaging in armed robbery, theft, illegal gambling, extortion, prostitution, and opium peddling. It succeeded the Whyos as a prominent non-Irish gang and had strong political connections through Tammany Hall. The gang dissolved in the early 1910s.

Egan's Rats.description: American organized crime gang based in St. Louis, Missouri, active from 1890 to 1924. Founded by Thomas 'Snake' Kinney and Tom Egan, the gang engaged in bootlegging, labor slugging, voter intimidation, armed robbery, and murder. It was predominantly Irish-American but included Italian and Jewish members. The gang dissolved after key members were imprisoned for a mail robbery in 1924.

El Monte Flores.description: Mexican-American criminal street gang based in El Monte, California, founded in the 1940s or 1950s. It is the largest Hispanic gang in San Gabriel Valley and one of the oldest in Los Angeles County. The gang is involved in drug trafficking, robbery, murder, and other crimes, with thousands of active members. It is a Sureño gang allied with the Mexican Mafia.

Elephant and Castle Mob.description: The Elephant and Castle Mob was an independent street gang active in London's underworld during the interwar years. They were rivals of Charles Sabini and the Birmingham Boys, and were eventually forced out by Sabini with Sicilian mafiosi. The gang achieved dominance on race courses and in London's West End from the 1910s to the 1930s, led by the McDonald brothers. They disappeared by the end of World War II.

Elm Street Piru.description: The Elm Street Piru is a set of the Piru gang alliance, part of the larger Bloods alliance, originating in Compton, California. It has spread to other U.S. cities including Brooklyn, Atlanta, and Virginia. The gang has been involved in criminal activities such as recruiting high school students and conspiracy to murder a witness. It remains active as of the 2020s.

Errol Flynns.description: The Errol Flynns were a street gang founded on the lower east side of Detroit, Michigan, United States during the 1970s. They were known for their flamboyant dress and use of hand signs, and engaged in extortion, robbery, and drug trafficking. The gang collapsed in the 1980s due to the rise of crack cocaine and prosecution of leaders.

Escritório do Crime.description: Brazilian militia of elite hitmen operating in the west zone of Rio de Janeiro, founded in 2007. It originated from illegal real estate activities such as land grabbing, construction, and illegal sale and rental of properties, with its main activity being contract killings. The group is composed of military police officers and former police, commanded by former BOPE captain Adriano Nóbrega and PM major Ronald Paulo Alves Pereira. It is suspected of involvement in 19 unsolved homicides since 2002, including the assassination of councilwoman Marielle Franco.

ETA.description: ETA was an armed Basque nationalist and separatist organization active in Spain and France between 1959 and 2018. Founded in 1959 during Francoist Spain by Basque nationalist students, it evolved into a clandestine paramilitary group conducting assassinations, bombings, and kidnappings primarily in Spain. ETA killed over 800 people and was classified as a terrorist group by multiple countries. It announced a definitive end to armed activity in 2011 and formally dissolved in 2018.

Fatemi Circle.description: A clique of statesmen within the Government of Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, involved in corruption scandals in Iran. Known for embezzlement, money laundering, bribery, and fraud. Based in Tehran, founded around 2005. Allegedly led by Mohammad-Reza Rahimi.

Felony Lane Gang.description: Organized crime gang based in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, known for smash-and-grab thefts from parked cars to steal identification and cash fraudulent checks. FFF (gang).description: FFF was a gang centered in the San Fernando Valley during the 1980s, unique for its membership of White Americans from middle and upper middle class backgrounds. Five Points Gang.description: The Five Points Gang was a criminal street gang based in the Five Points of Lower Manhattan, New York City, during the late 19th and early 20th century. Formby Gang.description: Early Chicago juvenile street gang formed in the late 1890s by teenagers Jimmy Formby, Bill Dulfer, and David Kelly. The gang committed hundreds of burglaries and armed robberies, and later engaged in murder for hire. It dissolved in 1904 after its leaders were imprisoned.

Forming Kaos.description: Forming Kaos is a criminal street gang based in Costa Mesa, California, composed primarily of Mexican-American members. Originating as a party/tagger crew in the early 1990s, it evolved into a street gang by the late 1990s. The gang is affiliated with the Sureños and has documented ties to the Mexican Mafia. Its activities include drug trafficking, extortion, and violent crime.

Forty Elephants.description: An all-female London crime syndicate active from the late 19th century to the 1950s, specializing in shoplifting. Based in the Elephant and Castle area, they raided West End stores and sometimes posed as housemaids to rob homes. The gang was allied with the Elephant and Castle Mob and avoided police detection for decades.

Forty Thieves.description: The Forty Thieves were a New York City criminal street gang formed in 1825 by Edward Coleman, primarily composed of Irish immigrants and Irish Americans. Based in the Five Points neighborhood of Manhattan, they engaged in street fighting, assault, murder, and robbery. The gang dissolved by 1850, with members joining larger gangs or leaving.

Forty-Two Gang.description: The Forty-Two Gang was a teenage street gang in Chicago active from 1925 to 1934, founded by Italian-American youths in the 'Patch' and 'Little Hell' neighborhoods. It served as a recruitment pool for the Chicago Outfit, producing future mobsters like Sam Giancana. The gang engaged in vandalism, theft, burglary, and armed robbery, and was known for extreme violence. It disbanded after heavy losses from rival wars and arrests.

Foster gang.description: A South African criminal group active in 1914, led by William Henry Foster. The gang committed robberies and murders in Johannesburg and the Rand. After a police standoff, all members and Foster's wife committed suicide.

Four Corner Hustlers.description: American street gang founded in the West Garfield Park neighborhood of Chicago in the late 1960s by Walter 'King' Wheat and Freddy Gauge. Known for violence and drug trafficking, it is allied with the People Nation and Vice Lords. The gang operates in multiple U.S. cities and has over 9,000 members as of 2020.

Four Seas Gang.description: Taiwanese triad society founded in May 1954 by mainland Chinese refugees who fled with the KMT. Active in alien smuggling in Southern California, with estimated membership of 10,000 in Taiwan and branches in Los Angeles and Santa Ana. Uses grey as its color.

country_links.evidence_quote: Its members have extended their influence to cities in the southern region of California . Its American constituents are a branch off of the original Taiwan society. Four Seas Gang is active in alien smuggling in Southern California.
country_links.context: The Four Seas Gang has a branch in the United States and is active in alien smuggling in Southern California.

Fourth Reich.description: The Fourth Reich was a racist skinhead prison gang formed in Paparua Prison in Christchurch, New Zealand, in the early 1990s. It terrorized communities in Nelson and the West Coast of the South Island, engaging in violent crimes with racist and bigoted dimensions. The gang was perceived as a credible terrorist threat during the early 2000s. There is little evidence that it still exists.

Foxtrot (criminal network).description: Foxtrot is a Swedish criminal network that emerged in the late 2010s, primarily involved in narcotics distribution. Led by Rawa Majid, also known as the Kurdish Fox, the network has developed direct operational ties with Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security. It is linked to violent crimes including shootings, bombings, and attacks on Israeli and Jewish targets in Europe. The network recruits vulnerable individuals and has been a major concern for Swedish law enforcement.

country_links.evidence_quote: Foxtrot has developed direct operational ties with the Iranian government, specifically Iran’s Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS).
country_links.context: Foxtrot maintains direct operational ties with the Iranian government and carries out attacks on Israeli and Jewish targets across Europe under Iranian direction.

country_links.context: Foxtrot members, including the leader, have purchased Turkish citizenship and control the network from Turkey.

Frankfurt mafia.description: The Frankfurt mafia is a Macedonian crime group founded in the mid-1990s in Veles, North Macedonia, involved in heroin trafficking in Frankfurt, Germany, and Vienna, Austria. It controlled up to 90% of Frankfurt's drug trade and 19 of 24 blocks in Vienna's heroin market. Despite mass arrests in 2010 and 2013, the group remains active and has adapted its tactics.

Free Souls Motorcycle Club.description: Outlaw motorcycle club founded in Eugene, Oregon in 1969. Has chapters in Oregon, Washington, Germany, and Australia. Its center patch features an ankh over a motorcycle wheel on handlebars, with blue and white colors.

country_links.evidence_quote: Chapters exist in Oregon, Washington, Germany and Australia.

French Connection.description: The French Connection was a heroin smuggling network that operated from the 1930s to the 1970s, trafficking opium from Indochina and Turkey to France for refining, then to the United States and Canada. Based in Marseille, it was run by Corsican gangsters including Antoine Guérini and Paul Carbone. The network supplied the majority of heroin in the U.S. during its peak in the 1960s before being dismantled.

Fresno Bulldogs.description: Primarily Mexican American criminal street and prison gang based in Fresno, California, founded in 1984. One of the biggest drug gangs in Central California with an estimated 12,000 members. Engaged in drug trafficking, human trafficking, murder, and other crimes. Unaffiliated with Sureños or Norteños, and rivals with multiple prison gangs.

Friends Stand United.description: Anti-fascist, anti-racist, and anti-drug hardcore crew founded in the late 1980s by Elgin James in Boston, Massachusetts. Originally fought Neo-Nazis and racist groups in the punk scene, but later accused of unprovoked violence and intimidation. Classified by the FBI as a street gang.

Fruit Belt Gang.description: Street gang based in Buffalo, New York, founded in the 1960s-1970s in the Fruit Belt area. Primarily African American, it engages in drug trafficking, weapons smuggling, and murder. The gang is in direct opposition to the Central Park Gang and has been involved in ongoing violent conflicts.

Fruit Town Piru.description: The Fruit Town Piru is a set of the Piru gang alliance, part of the larger Bloods alliance, formed in the 1970s in Compton, California. Named after fruit-named streets in their neighborhood, the gang is primarily African-American and known for its rivalry with the Mob Piru Bloods. It has been involved in violent feuds and has affiliations with rappers such as Chris Brown and Soulja Boy.

Fucked For Life.description: Swedish criminal network founded by Daniel Maiorana in the late 1990s, originally named Tumba Lords. Based in Tumba, Stockholm, the group engages in car thefts, motorcycle thefts, armed robberies, and drug trafficking. Membership is estimated at around 40 individuals, with a core of 12 men.

Fuerza Anti-Unión.description: Mexican criminal organization originating from the Tepito neighborhood of Mexico City, founded around 2016. It emerged either as a self-defense group against the Unión Tepito or as a splinter faction led by Roberto Moyado. Engages in extortion, kidnapping, drug trafficking, and murder. Despite arrests of key leaders, the group remains active.

Fukuhaku-kai.description: The Fukuhaku-kai is a yakuza organization based in Fukuoka, Japan, founded in 1985 by Akira Umedu. It is a designated yakuza group with an estimated membership of 60. The group has been involved in conflicts with the Yamaguchi-gumi and other local syndicates over territory in the Nakasu red-light district.

Fullerton Boys.description: A Korean-American street gang based in Fullerton, California, founded in 1996. Members were originally from other gangs such as LVM, SZA, and Wah Ching. The gang emerged as a collective identity after other gangs disbanded in Fullerton.

Galatolo Mafia clan.description: The Galatolo Mafia clan was a criminal family originating from the Acquasanta neighborhood of Palermo, Sicily. One of the longest-running Mafia clans in the city, they held important positions throughout the 20th century and ruled the Resuttana mandamento in the early 21st century. They were involved in the violent Palermo wholesale market war in the 1950s and were devastated by internal betrayal. The clan was active from the 1950s until 2014.

Galloping Goose Motorcycle Club.description: Outlaw motorcycle club founded in 1942 in Los Angeles, California by Dick Hershberg. Initially an informal racing team, it chartered in 1946 and expanded across the Midwest and South. Considered a second-tier outlaw motorcycle gang by law enforcement, it has been involved in violent crimes and has support clubs.

Galloway Boys.description: The Galloway Boys are a gang based in Southern Ontario, Canada, originating in the Scarborough district of Toronto. Founded in the early 1980s, they expanded into Durham Region and Kawartha Lakes. They are involved in drug trafficking, robbery, extortion, murder, burglary, and racketeering, and have been linked to multiple gang-related violence incidents including the Danzig Street shooting.

Gambino crime family.description: The Gambino family is one of the Five Families of New York and one of the most powerful in the United States. Originating from the Black Hand gang led by Ignazio Lupo and Giuseppe Morello in East Harlem, it evolved under Salvatore D'Aquila and later Al Mineo. The family was formally established as one of the Five Families by Salvatore Maranzano after the Castellammarese War. It remains active in organized crime activities such as gambling and racketeering.

Gang de la Brise de Mer.description: Corsican criminal organization founded in the 1970s, based in Northern Corsica. Controls racketeering, slot machines, money laundering, night clubs, gambling, and casinos in Corsica, southern France, Paris, Italy, Africa, and Latin America. Known for violent robberies and conflicts with rival gangs. Estimated capital between 120 and 150 million euros.

Gang des postiches.description: A team of bank robbers that operated in Paris between 1981 and 1986, robbing around thirty banks. They wore false mustaches, beards, and wigs to disguise themselves. The gang was known for being respectful to hostages and gained public sympathy. Their total theft may have exceeded 30 million euros.

Gang des Tractions Avant.description: The Gang des Tractions Avant was a criminal gang in the Pigalle quarter of Paris, composed of former Carlingue militia members, lapsed police officers, and criminals from the French Resistance. Active in the mid-20th century, the gang was named after its preferred vehicle, the Citroën 11CV 'Traction'. Its methods influenced later gangs and inspired various cultural works.

Gang of Amazons.description: A family of serial killers from Stavropol, Russia, who committed a series of murders and robberies from 2007 to 2013. Founded by Inessa Tarverdiyeva and her husband Roman Podkopaev, the group included their daughters and other relatives. They were apprehended in 2013.

Gangster Disciples.description: The Gangster Disciples are an African-American street and prison gang founded in Chicago in 1966 by Larry Hoover and David Barksdale. Originally formed as the Black Gangster Disciple Nation, the group split in 1989 into the Gangster Disciple Nation and the Black Disciple Nation. The gang is involved in drug trafficking, assault, firearms violations, fraud, homicide, money laundering, and organized crime, with an estimated 30,000 members in Chicago and operations across the United States and internationally.

Garduña.description: The Garduña is a mythical secret criminal society said to have been founded in Spain in the late Middle Ages, around 1417, with statutes approved in Toledo in 1420. It was allegedly involved in robbery, kidnapping, arson, and murder-for-hire. However, historians consider it a fictional organization, with all references traced back to a 19th-century book. It is often cited as a foundational myth for Italian mafias like the Camorra, Mafia, and 'Ndrangheta.

GAS Gang.description: British street gang based in Brixton, South London, formed in the late 2000s. Known for drug trafficking, murder, theft, and money laundering. Considered one of the most dangerous gangs in South London by 2012, responsible for multiple murders and violent incidents. Membership declined in the early 2010s due to incarceration of leaders.

Gas House Gang.description: The Gas House Gang was a New York City street gang founded in the 1890s, based in the Gas House district of Manhattan. They controlled the area along Third Avenue from 11th to 18th Street, specializing in armed robbery, extortion, and operating brothels. The gang committed an estimated 30 to 40 robberies per night and dominated the district for over two decades until being absorbed by the Five Points Gang in 1910.

Gate Keepers Motorcycle Club.description: Canadian outlaw motorcycle club founded in 2013 in Musquodoboit Harbour, Nova Scotia. Operates as a support club for the Hells Angels in Canada, with chapters in Ontario and formerly Nova Scotia. Known for rapid expansion and rivalry with Bacchus Motorcycle Club.

Genovese crime family.description: The Genovese crime family is an Italian American Mafia crime family and one of the Five Families that dominate organized crime in New York City and New Jersey. Founded by Charles 'Lucky' Luciano in the 1930s, it is the oldest and largest of the Five Families. Known for its secrecy and white-collar rackets, it has been considered the most powerful Mafia family in the United States. The family is currently led by Liborio 'Barney' Bellomo.

aliases: New Jersey faction of the Genovese crime family
Genovese crime family New Jersey faction.description: The New Jersey faction of the Genovese crime family is a group of Italian-American mobsters controlling organized crime in New Jersey. It is divided into multiple crews involved in labor racketeering, illegal gambling, loansharking, and extortion. The faction has maintained a strong presence in Northern Jersey since the early Prohibition era. Notable members include Guarino 'Willie' Moretti, Gerardo 'Jerry' Catena, and Louis 'Bobby' Manna.

Genovese crime family Springfield factio.description: The Springfield faction of the Genovese crime family is a group of Italian-American mobsters controlling organized crime in Springfield, Massachusetts. It was founded in the 1920s and is led by a caporegime. The faction engages in racketeering, illegal gambling, loansharking, and extortion. It has been active since the 1920s and remains operational.

Gente Nueva.description: Gente Nueva is a large group of well-trained gunmen serving as an elite armed wing of the Sinaloa Cartel. Founded in 1995 in Sonora, Mexico, it was created to counter the Juárez Cartel's influence in northwestern Mexico. The group has been involved in drug trafficking, kidnapping, and murder, and has engaged in a prolonged turf war with the Juárez Cartel and its enforcer wing, La Línea. As of 2012, Gente Nueva and the Sinaloa Cartel had emerged victorious in the conflict.

George Street.description: George Street is a Bloods-affiliated street gang based in Belize City, Belize, allegedly formed in the late 1980s by US deportee Heathcliff Reyes. It is one of the country's earliest gangs and has been involved in violent conflicts with rival gangs. The gang's territory was estimated as among the largest in Belize in 2018, with membership ranging from 40 to 150. As of 2021, it remains one of the largest gangs in Belize.

Georgian mafia.description: The Georgian mafia is an organized crime network originating in Georgia, known for producing the largest number of 'thieves in law' in post-Soviet states. It controls and regulates many Russian-speaking mafia groups and is active in Russia and Europe. The organization has two major clans from Tbilisi and Kutaisi, with the Kutaisi Clan being particularly well represented. Its criminal activities include arms trafficking, extortion, money laundering, and murder.

country_links.context: The Georgian mafia operates in Spain through criminal groups involved in violent crimes, burglaries, and money laundering, with police operations in Barcelona and Madrid.

Ghee Hin Kongsi.description: The Ghee Hin Kongsi was a Chinese secret society in Singapore and Malaya, formed in 1820. It was part of the Hongmen overseas network and provided mutual aid for Chinese migrants, aiming to overthrow the Qing dynasty. The society was involved in violent conflicts with rival secret societies and was suppressed by colonial authorities from the 1890s.

Ghetto Boys.description: The Ghetto Boys is a street gang based in New Cross, Lewisham and Deptford, South London. Formed in the 1970s on the Woodpecker Estate, it is primarily composed of Black British members. The gang has been involved in drug trafficking, murder, assault, and robbery, and had a notable conflict with the Peckham Boys. By the mid-late 2000s, the gang declined and splintered, with offshoots like Shower and 814 emerging.

Ghetto Brothers.description: The Ghetto Brothers were a gang and music group founded in New York City's South Bronx in the late 1960s. They were involved in politics, particularly the Puerto Rican independence movement, and aimed to uplift young Latino and Black men. The gang spread to much of the Northeastern United States and later merged with the Savage Nomads to form Los Solidos in Connecticut.

Ghost Shadows.description: The Ghost Shadows was a Chinese American street gang prominent in New York City's Chinatown from the early 1970s to the mid 1990s. Formed in 1971 by immigrants from Taiwan and Hong Kong, it was affiliated with the On Leong Tong. The gang engaged in extortion, kidnapping, murder, racketeering, drug trafficking, and illegal gambling. It became defunct due to federal RICO crackdowns in the 1990s.

Gitans Moto Club.description: French-Canadian outlaw motorcycle gang based in Sherbrooke, Quebec, founded in 1967. Originally a street gang called the Vikings, it evolved into the Dirty Reich MC before becoming the Gitans MC in 1970. The gang controlled drug trafficking in Sherbrooke and integrated into the Hells Angels in 1984, forming the Sherbrooke charter.

Goda-ikka.description: The Goda-ikka is a yakuza group based in Yamaguchi, Japan, formed in 1948 as the Goda-gumi by Koichi Goda. It is the largest yakuza group in Yamaguchi Prefecture, with an estimated 30 members. The group was renamed Goda-ikka in 1968 and became a designated yakuza group in 1992. It is a member of the anti-Yamaguchi federation Gosha-kai.

Gooch Close Gang.description: Organised crime group based in Moss Side, South Manchester, England, founded in the late 1980s. Primarily involved in drug trafficking, weapon trafficking, robbery, and murder. Known for violent disputes with rival gangs such as the Doddington Gang and Moss Side Bloods. Still active as of the present.

Gopher Gang.description: The Gopher Gang was an early 20th-century New York street gang based in Hell's Kitchen, Manhattan. Formed in the 1890s from various local street gangs, it numbered around 500 members and controlled territory from Fourth to Forty-Second Street and Seventh to Eleventh Avenue. The gang engaged in burglary, armed robbery, assault, prostitution, and illegal gambling. It declined in the 1910s.

Goto-gumi.description: The Goto-gumi was a Japanese yakuza organization founded by Tadamasa Goto. Originally based in Fujinomiya, Shizuoka Prefecture, it moved to Tokyo in 1991 and became an affiliate of the Yamaguchi-gumi. The gang was involved in financial, real estate, construction, entertainment, and political activities, and was notorious for the assault on filmmaker Juzo Itami. It was dissolved in 2008 after Goto's expulsion from the Yamaguchi-gumi.

country_links.context: The Goto-gumi smuggled firearms from the Philippines, where they had connections with high-ranking military officers.

Grady Gang.description: The Grady Gang was a New York City sneak thief gang during the 1860s, organized by fence John D. 'Traveling Mike' Grady after the American Civil War. The gang operated in Broadway's 'Thieves Exchange' and was known for the robbery of $2 million from financier Rufus L. Lord in 1866. Most members retired by the end of the decade, but Grady continued as a fence.

Gran Grif.description: Gran Grif is the largest and most powerful criminal organization in the Artibonite department of Haiti, based in Savien. Founded around 2016 by former congressman Prophane Victor, it engages in murder, rape, mass abduction, forced child recruitment, and other violent abuses. The gang was responsible for 80% of reported civilian deaths in Artibonite in 2022 and perpetrated the 2024 Pont-Sondé attack that killed at least 115 people. It has been designated a terrorist organization by the Dominican Republic and the United States.

Grape Street Watts Crips.description: The Grape Street Watts Crips is a set of the Crips gang based in the Watts neighborhood of Los Angeles, founded in the 1970s. It is known for a violent and long-lasting feud with the Bounty Hunter Bloods. The gang operates in California, Tennessee, and New Jersey. It remains active as of the present.

Greco Mafia clan.description: Historically one of the most influential Mafia clans in Sicily, based in Ciaculli and Croceverde Giardini near Palermo. Founded in the late 19th century, the extended family played a key role in the Sicilian Cosa Nostra, with members serving as secretaries of the Sicilian Mafia Commission. Involved in citrus growing, cigarette smuggling, heroin trafficking, and money laundering. Declined in the 2000s but remains active with strong influence.

Green Gang.description: The Green Gang was a Chinese secret society and criminal triad organization prominent in Shanghai during the early to mid 20th century. It originated from the Luojiao Buddhist sect and grain transport boatmen along the Grand Canal. The gang engaged in criminal, social, and political activities, including opium trafficking. Key leaders included Du Yuesheng and Huang Jinrong.

country_links.evidence_quote: the Green Gang left Shanghai and in the early 1950s opened heroin refineries in Hong Kong.
country_links.context: The Green Gang opened heroin refineries in Hong Kong in the early 1950s.

Green Street Counts.description: A street gang based in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, active in the early 1950s. Their turf centered at 21st and Green Streets, and they specialized in armed robbery, kidnapping, and weapons dealings. The gang gained notoriety after member Joseph 'Blackie' Battel was sentenced to life for a robbery murder. A separate, unaffiliated group also operated under the same name in West Philadelphia.

Greenwich Village Crew.description: The Greenwich Village Crew is a crew within the Genovese crime family, active in the Greenwich Village area of Manhattan. Founded in the 1920s by Vito Genovese, it has been involved in racketeering, gambling, loan sharking, and extortion. The crew was historically led by Vincent Gigante, who became boss of the Genovese family. It remains active, though its current leadership is uncertain.

Gremium Motorcycle Club.description: German outlaw motorcycle club founded in 1972 in Mannheim. Claims to be the largest German MC since 1999, with chapters across Europe and a prospect chapter in Thailand. The club was banned in 1988 but the ban was lifted in 1992. Associated with organized crime including human trafficking, drug and weapons trafficking.

Grendon crime family.description: Irish organised crime syndicate based in Ireland, emerging in the late 20th century. Involved in drug trafficking, money laundering, firearms smuggling, extortion, and contract violence. Considered a top priority for dismantlement by Irish law enforcement. Concentrated operations within Ireland.

Grey Wolves.description: The Grey Wolves are a Turkish far-right ultranationalist and neo-fascist political movement and the youth wing of the Nationalist Movement Party (MHP). Founded by Colonel Alparslan Türkeş in the late 1960s, they engaged in urban guerrilla warfare during the late 1970s political violence in Turkey and are implicated in numerous massacres and assassinations. The organization has been banned in Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, and France, and is active in Turkey, Northern Cyprus, Western Europe, and Central Asia.

Founded in 1971 by twins Rashied and Rashaad Staggie, it evolved from a street gang into a structured criminal organization involved in drug trafficking, weapon trafficking, prostitution, contract killing, extortion, illegal diamond smuggling, and other crimes. Henry Street Gang.description: The Henry Street Gang was a Chicago street gang formed by Chris Merry in the early 1890s. Based in Chicago's Southwest Side, they committed armed robbery against local merchants and street peddlers, often posing as push cart vendors. They developed a robbery method called the 'kick in' and operated for several years until Merry was hanged for murdering his wife, after which the gang dissolved.

The gang has over 1,000 members and is involved in trafficking cocaine and marijuana from Mexico into the United States.

Hogan Gang.description: The Hogan Gang was a St. Louis-based criminal organization active during Prohibition, involved in bootlegging, labor slugging, voter intimidation, armed robbery, and murder. Founded around 1917 by Edward "Jelly Roll" Hogan, the gang was predominantly Irish-American but included Italian and Jewish members. They fought a violent gang war with Egan's Rats in the early 1920s and were active from the 1920s to the 1930s.

Honda-kai.description: The Honda-kai were a Japanese yakuza gang active in Kobe in the mid-20th century. They were a bakuto gang devoted to illegal gambling. After World War II, they allied with the Yamaguchi-gumi but were soon absorbed and ceased to be independent. An American Yamaguchi-gumi syndicate may have reused the name in the 2000s.

Honeymoon Gang.description: The Honeymoon Gang was a mid-19th century New York street gang based in the East Side's 18th Ward. Known for brutal attacks on passersby, they operated with impunity until 1853 when police Captain George W. Walling formed the Strong Arm Squad to suppress them. The gang was disbanded within two weeks, with members fleeing the district.

Honoured Society (Australia).description: The Honoured Society is a Calabrian 'ndrangheta criminal confederation active in Australia, founded around 1920 in Melbourne. It controls Italian-Australian organized crime along the East Coast, involved in racketeering, drug trafficking, and other illegal activities. The organization has been marked by internal power struggles and conflicts such as the Market Wars. It remains active with multiple 'ndrine (crime families) operating across Australia.

country_links.evidence_quote: The Honoured Society ... is a Calabrian 'ndrangheta criminal confederation, started in Melbourne and currently active in all of Australia.

Hook Gang.description: The Hook Gang was a street gang and river pirate group active in New York City in the 1860s and 1870s. Based in Corlear's Hook on the East River, the gang engaged in armed robbery, theft, hijacking, and river piracy. It was formed around 1866 and disbanded after police arrests in 1876.

HooNaRa.description: Far-right hooligan group based around German football club Chemnitzer FC, founded in the early 1990s by Thomas Haller. The group engaged in fights with other hooligan firms and was banned from the stadium in 2006. Officially dissolved in 2007, it continues as a loose network of 20-30 members.

Hop Sing Tong.description: The Hop Sing Tong is a Chinese American tong established in 1875. It operates multiple branches across the United States, including in cities such as San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Seattle. The organization is historically associated with Chinese immigrant communities and has been involved in both legitimate and illicit activities.

Hopi Boys.description: The Hopi Boys are an Afro-Curaçaoan criminal group based in the south-east region of Amsterdam, Netherlands. They are one of the most influential gangs in the Dutch capital, controlling rackets, drug dealing, and prostitution. The group is predominantly Afro-Curaçaoan and has allies such as the Green gang and rivals like the Kloekhorststraat Gang.

Hornec gang.description: The Hornec gang is a Gitanes criminal group from the Paris region, led by three brothers from Montreuil. It controls racketeering, drug dealing, and illegal slot machines in Paris, with connections to the Corsican mafia and Maghrebian gangs. The gang rose after the 1994 assassination of crime boss Claude Genova and became the most influential in Paris, but its influence declined after arrests in 2006.

Hudson Dusters.description: The Hudson Dusters were a New York City street gang formed in the late 1890s by Circular Jack, Kid Yorke, and Goo Goo Knox. Based in Manhattan's West Side, they controlled the Hudson River docks and engaged in burglary, armed robbery, and narcotics. The gang had ties to Tammany Hall and was known for cocaine-fueled violence. They were active until around 1917.

Imperial Klans of America.description: White supremacist, white nationalist, neo-Nazi paramilitary organization founded in 1996 by Ron Edwards in Dawson Springs, Kentucky. It was the second largest Klan group in the United States until the late 2000s, and briefly the largest in the early 2000s. The group has been weakened by legal judgments and Edwards' imprisonment, but remained active as of 2020 with only two chapters by 2012.

Inagawa-kai.description: The Inagawa-kai is the third largest yakuza group in Japan, based in the Kantō region. Founded in 1949 by Kakuji Inagawa in Atami, Shizuoka, it initially focused on illegal gambling and later expanded into drug trafficking, extortion, and prostitution. It was one of the first yakuza organizations to operate overseas and has an estimated 1,600 members.

Independent Cartel of Acapulco.description: The Independent Cartel of Acapulco was a Mexican criminal gang based in Acapulco, Guerrero, formed in 2010 as a split from the Beltrán-Leyva Cartel after the death of Arturo Beltrán Leyva. It engaged in drug trafficking, extortion, and murder, known for flaying victims' faces. The group was severely damaged by 2011 and faded from public view, with its territory taken over by rival La Barredora.

Independent Soldiers.description: Organized crime group based in British Columbia, Canada, formed in the early 1990s by Indo-Canadians. Initially known as the Sunset Boys, they became independent from the Punjabi mafia after 1998. Engaged in drug trafficking, murder, and other crimes across Canada and in prisons. Known for red and black colors and the Independent Soldiers clothing brand.

Jheri Curls.description: The Jheri Curls were a Dominican gang active in Washington Heights, Manhattan, New York City in the early 1990s. Named after the Jheri curl hairstyle, they ran a major cocaine trafficking operation based out of an apartment complex on W. 157th St. and Riverside Drive. Led by Rafael Martinez and his brothers, the gang was known for extreme violence, including the murder of a resident who cooperated with police. The gang was dismantled in October 1991 after undercover police operations led to arrests and lengthy prison sentences.

Joe Boys.description: The Joe Boys were a Chinese American youth gang founded in the 1960s in San Francisco's Chinatown by Joe Fong, a former Wah Ching member. They were involved in drug trafficking, extortion, robbery, and murder. The gang was active from 1969 to 1977 and had conflicts with the Wah Ching and Hop Sing Tong.

Originally a burglary ring, it later expanded into loansharking, illegal gambling, racketeering, and drug trafficking. The gang controlled Philadelphia's Irish-American underworld for much of the late 20th century and maintains ties with other organized crime groups.

Kadyrovites.description: Informal Chechnya-based detachments of Russian state security forces, effectively serving as Ramzan Kadyrov's private army. Founded in the late 1990s, they have been accused of widespread human rights abuses including torture and extrajudicial killings. They have participated in conflicts such as the Syrian Civil War and the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

Kansas City crime family.description: Italian American Mafia crime family based in Kansas City, Missouri, founded around 1912 by Sicilian mafiosi Joseph and Peter DiGiovanni. It expanded through bootlegging during Prohibition and later engaged in racketeering, gambling, loansharking, and drug trafficking. The family was led for decades by Nicholas Civella, who forged alliances with other families and used Teamsters to fund Las Vegas casinos. As of 2015, it had an estimated 12 made members and remains active.

Kantō-kai.description: The Kantō-kai was a Japanese underworld organization formed by Yoshio Kodama in 1964, intended as a secret national police force to advance far-right views. It drew most of its membership from the Kantō region. The group disbanded in January 1965 after only fifteen months, but was a crucial step in uniting post-war gangs into the modern yakuza.

Keane-Collopy gang.description: Criminal organisation based in Limerick City, Ireland, founded in the 1990s by Christy Keane. Major drug suppliers in the Mid-West region, heavily involved in the Limerick feud since 2000. Has been weakened in recent years with key figures dead or imprisoned.

Kelly Park Compton Crips.description: The Kelly Park Compton Crips are a set of the Crips gang alliance originating in Kelly Park, Compton, California. Known for its connection with rap group N.W.A, members include Eazy-E and MC Ren. The gang has been involved in violent conflicts with rival Piru sets, including the Lueders Park Piru. A police substation established in 1986 reduced criminal incidents in the area.

Kerryonians.description: The Kerryonians were an Irish-American street gang based in the Five Points area of New York City, active from the 1820s to the 1830s. Founded by recent immigrants from County Kerry, Ireland, they were among the earliest criminal gangs in the city, known for targeting British-descended New Yorkers and disrupting a performance by actor William Charles Macready in 1849. The gang was eventually absorbed into larger Five Points gangs such as the Dead Rabbits, Roach Guards, and Chichesters.

Keystone United.description: Neo-Nazi group based in Pennsylvania, founded in 2001 by five men from Harrisburg. Originally focused on uniting white power skinheads across Pennsylvania, it expanded to multiple chapters and became one of the largest single-state racist skinhead crews in the US. The group organizes white power concerts and family-oriented events, and changed its name from Keystone State Skinheads to Keystone United in 2008.

Khmer Rouge.description: The Khmer Rouge was a communist-led insurgent and later ruling party in Cambodia, founded in 1951. Under Pol Pot, it ruled Cambodia from 1975 to 1979, implementing radical agrarian collectivization and autarky that led to the Cambodian genocide, killing 1.5 to 2 million people. The group continued as an insurgency until its final dissolution in 1999.

Khumalo gang.description: The Khumalo gang was an armed group based in the Joe Slovo section of South Africa, led by Mbhekiseni Khumalo, founder of a small Zionist Christian sect. It was allied with the Inkatha Freedom Party. The group is described in the past tense, indicating it is no longer active.

Khánh Trắng.description: Khánh Trắng was a Vietnamese crime boss who operated in Hanoi during the 1990s. He used his position as President of the Dong Xuan Labor Union as a front for extortion, murder, and tax evasion. He controlled the Dong Xuan market area and led a gang of criminals. He was executed by firing squad in 1998.

Founded in 2003 in Ōtara as a spin-off of the Tribesmen gang by Josh Masters, a former vice-president of Tribesmen MC. King Cobras.description: The King Cobras are a prominent Pacific gang in New Zealand, founded by Samoans in Ponsonby in the 1950s, making them the oldest gang in the country. Initially restricted to Samoans, they have since accepted other Polynesians. The gang is known for violence, firearms possession, and involvement in drug dealing, including methamphetamine, cocaine, and marijuana. They have been involved in major drug cases and murders.

Kings Crew Motorcycle Club.description: Outlaw motorcycle club based in Western Canada, founded in Calgary, Alberta in 1977. Kipps Lane Crew.description: Canadian street gang founded in 2000 in London, Ontario. Operates in the Kipps Lane area of Northeast London, involved in drug trafficking, murder, assault, extortion, robbery, burglary, and grand theft. One of the largest gangs in London, monitored by the London Police Service and part of the 'Big Seven' street gangs in the city.

Kizuna-kai.description: The Kizuna-kai is a yakuza organization based in Hyogo, Japan, formed on April 30, 2017 by defectors from the Kobe Yamaguchi-gumi. It was originally named Ninkyo-dantai-Yamaguchi-gumi, then Ninkyo Yamaguchi-gumi, before adopting its current name in 2020. The group has about 50 members and 70 quasi-members, and is designated as a bōryokudan by the Hyogo Prefecture Public Safety Commission.

Knights Templar Cartel.description: Mexican drug cartel that emerged in Michoacán in March 2011 as a splinter group from La Familia Michoacana. Known for its pseudo-religious ideology, it engaged in drug trafficking, extortion, and other crimes. The cartel gained significant social influence and de facto control in some municipalities. It was designated as a Specially Designated Narcotics Trafficker by the U.S. Treasury in 2013.

Kobe Yamaguchi-gumi.description: The Kobe Yamaguchi-gumi is a yakuza organization based in Hyogo, Japan, formed in 2015 after breaking away from the Sixth Yamaguchi-gumi. It was founded by Kunio Inoue and initially had 2,800 members, but membership declined to around 140 by 2023 due to splits and disbandments. The group has been designated as a crime syndicate by authorities and is involved in various criminal activities.

Kodo-kai.description: The Kodo-kai is a yakuza criminal organization based in Nagoya, Japan, founded in 1984 by Shinobu Tsukasa. It is a secondary organization of the Sixth Yamaguchi-gumi, the largest yakuza syndicate in Japan, with an estimated membership of 4,000. The Kodo-kai is known for its defiant attitude toward police and its involvement in banking, real estate, securities, and show business. It is considered by the National Police Agency to be more like a mafia-type or terrorist organization.

Kokusui-kai.description: Tokyo-based yakuza organization founded in 1958 by Masaji Morita. Originally a revivalist monarchist anticommunist group, it temporarily disbanded in 1965 after crackdowns. Controls Tokyo's Ginza district and was historically part of the Kantō Hatsukakai federation before becoming an affiliate of the Yamaguchi-gumi in 2005.

Kompania Bello.description: Transnational Albanian-speaking cocaine-trafficking network that organized shipments from South America to Europe and coordinated wholesale distribution across EU member states. It was dismantled in 2020 after a five-year investigation codenamed Operation Los Blancos, resulting in over 100 arrests and seizures of nearly 4 tonnes of cocaine. The network negotiated directly with South American cartels and used encrypted communications and informal value transfer systems.

Kozakura-ikka.description: The Kozakura-ikka is a yakuza organization based in Kagoshima, Kyushu, Japan, with an estimated 40 active members. It was formed in 1948 by Seizo Osato. Its criminal activities include protection racketeering, drug trafficking, and unlawful involvement in public works.

Ku Klux Klan.description: American white supremacist and far-right hate group, founded in 1865 in Pulaski, Tennessee, by former Confederate soldiers. It has operated in three major iterations, using violence and intimidation to target African Americans, Jews, Catholics, and immigrants. The Klan is considered one of the earliest terrorist groups in the United States, with a history of lynching, political violence, and racial terror. Modern iterations are smaller but continue to promote white nationalism and anti-immigrant nativism.

Kudo-kai.description: The Kudo-kai is a yakuza group headquartered in Kitakyushu, Fukuoka, Japan, founded before WWII as a bakuto organization named Kudo-gumi by Genji Kudo. It is the largest yakuza group in the Kitakyushu area, known for its militant stance and conflicts with the Yamaguchi-gumi. The group has been designated as a particularly nefarious organization by the National Police Agency and was registered under the Organized Crime Countermeasures Law in 1992.

Kumi 415.description: Predominantly African-American prison gang formed in Folsom State Prison in the mid-1980s by inmates from the San Francisco Bay Area. The name combines the Swahili word for ten (kumi) with San Francisco's area code 415. Members often incorporate African symbols and Swahili language into their culture and tattoos. The gang operates in several California prisons and selected areas.

Kuratong Baleleng.description: Kuratong Baleleng is an organized crime syndicate in the Philippines, originally established in 1986 as an anti-communist vigilante group. It became one of the largest syndicates in the country, involved in kidnapping, drug trafficking, extortion, and other crimes. The group gained nationwide attention after a 1995 shootout with police in Quezon City. Despite the death of its first leader, the syndicate has scattered across provinces and some members have entered politics.

Kurdistan Workers' Party.description: Kurdish militant political organization and armed guerrilla group primarily based in mountainous Kurdish-majority regions of southeastern Turkey, northern Iraq, and northeastern Syria. Founded on 27 November 1978 in Ziyaret, Lice, by Abdullah Öcalan and others. Initially sought an independent Kurdish state, later shifted to seeking autonomy and cultural rights within Turkey. Designated as a terrorist organization by Turkey, the US, EU, and others. Declared a ceasefire in March 2025 and announced plans for dissolution.

Kyodo-kai.description: The Kyodo-kai is a yakuza group based in Hiroshima, Japan, formed in January 1969 by Kokichi Morita after the disbanding of its predecessor, the Takahashi-gumi. It is a designated yakuza group with an estimated 60 active members and is the second largest yakuza group in the Chugoku region. The group has been a member of the anti-Yamaguchi federation Gosha-kai since 1996.

Kyokuryū-kai.description: The Kyokuryū-kai is a yakuza criminal organization based on the Okinawa island of Japan, with an estimated membership of 210–270. It was formed in 1970 as the Okinawa-rengo Kyokuryu-kai by two gangs, the Naha Clan and the Koza Clan. It was Okinawa's largest organized crime group from 1983 until 1990 when a splinter group, the Okinawa Kyokuryu-kai, broke away. The group has been in conflict with the Yamaguchi-gumi and its official policy forbids drug trafficking.

Kyokuto-kai.description: The Kyokuto-kai is a yakuza organization based in Tokyo, Japan, founded by Aiji Sekiguchi. It was registered as a designated yakuza group under the Organized Crime Countermeasures Law in July 1993. In the early 2000s, it was involved in a feud with the rival Matsuba-kai, leading to shootings. As of the article, it has about 300 members and is led by Jin Takahashi.

Kyosei-kai.description: The Kyosei-kai is a yakuza group based in Hiroshima, Japan, formed in May 1964 by bakuto Tatsuo Yamamura from seven yakuza clans. Known for fierce conflicts with other groups, particularly the Yamaguchi-gumi, it has been a leading member of anti-Yamaguchi federations. The group has around 120 members and is led by Susumu Arase.

Kyushu Seido-kai.description: The Kyushu Seido-kai was a yakuza organization based in Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan, formed in 2006 as a splinter group from the Dojin-kai. It engaged in armed conflicts with its former parent syndicate, using automatic firearms and grenades, and was designated as a yakuza group in 2008. The group was involved in drug trafficking and loansharking, and dissolved in June 2013, later reorganizing under new names.

La Barredora.description: La Barredora is a Mexican criminal gang based in Tabasco, formed in 2008 as a split-off from the Beltrán-Leyva Cartel. It operates primarily in Acapulco and surrounding states, engaging in drug trafficking, money laundering, extortion, murder, kidnapping, arms trafficking, and illegal fuel extraction. The group is known for its rivalry with the Independent Cartel of Acapulco and links to the Sinaloa Cartel. Its leader, Hernán Bermúdez Requena, was captured in Paraguay in 2025.

La Corporación.description: Bolivian drug cartel founded in the 1970s by Roberto Suárez Gómez, known as the 'King of Cocaine'. It became one of the world's largest cocaine producers after the 1980 coup, receiving political protection from the military dictatorship. The cartel supplied the Medellín Cartel and was active until the early 1990s.

country_links.evidence_quote: Drugs were smuggled from the cocaine labs in the Bolivian Amazon to Colombia, selling at $9,000 per kilo.
country_links.context: The organization smuggled drugs from Bolivia to Colombia and was a major supplier to the Medellín Cartel.

country_links.context: The organization smuggled drugs into the United States and operated a major drug-trafficking operation in Southern California.

La Empresa.description: Colombian drug trafficking cartel based in Medellín, founded in the late 1990s by Gerardo Santana Garza and Luis Mendez. It is a breakaway group from the Juárez Cartel and traffics cocaine, heroin, MDMA, fentanyl, marijuana, and pink cocaine. The cartel operates in Colombia, Mexico, and other regions, and has been involved in conflicts with former Juárez Cartel members.

country_links.evidence_quote: Territory: Medellín, Bogotá, parts of the Amazon natural region, Ciudad Juárez, Chiapas
country_links.context: The organization has territory in Ciudad Juárez and Chiapas, Mexico.

La Familia Michoacana.description: Mexican drug cartel and organized crime syndicate based in Michoacán, founded in the 1980s by Carlos Rosales Mendoza. Known for producing large amounts of methamphetamine. Originally allied with the Gulf Cartel and Los Zetas, it split off in 2006. After the death of leader Nazario Moreno González, several factions split to form the Knights Templar Cartel and La Nueva Familia Michoacana.

country_links.evidence_quote: used the port city of Lázaro Cárdenas, Michoacán to import narcotics from Peru and Colombia

La Línea.description: La Línea is the main faction of the Juárez Cartel, originally formed as an enforcement unit composed of former police and military personnel. Based in Ciudad Juárez, Mexico, it was founded in 2008 by Juan Pablo Ledezma. The group is involved in drug trafficking, extortion, and kidnappings, and has been responsible for numerous massacres in Ciudad Juárez. It has formed alliances with the CJNG and Los Chapitos to combat the Sinaloa Cartel.

country_links.evidence_quote: In the early 2010s the DEA estimated that about 70% of the cocaine that enters the United States flows through the El Paso–Juárez border.

La Mano con Ojos.description: Mexican criminal organization dedicated to drug trafficking and methamphetamine production, formed as a remnant of the Beltrán Leyva Cartel and Los Valencia. Founded in 2010 by Eznel Cortés Jiménez and Óscar Osvaldo García Montoya, it operated primarily in Mexico City and the State of Mexico. The group was involved in homicide, kidnapping, extortion, and other crimes. It was dismantled by 2016.

country_links.evidence_quote: Los miembros del grupo están parcialmente entrenados en Guatemala, donde Montoya sirvió en el ejército.
country_links.context: The organization's members are partially trained in Guatemala, where one of its leaders served in the army.

La Nueva Familia Michoacana.description: Mexican criminal organization specializing in drug trafficking, illegal mining, and extortion. Formed in 2011 as a splinter group after the original La Familia Michoacana lost power. Led by brothers Johnny and José Alfredo Hurtado Olascoaga. Operates primarily in Michoacán, Guerrero, and the State of Mexico, and is involved in distributing cocaine, fentanyl, and methamphetamine to the United States. Designated as a foreign terrorist organization by the U.S. State Department in 2025.

country_links.evidence_quote: the organization is primarily involved in the distribution of cocaine, fentanyl, and methamphetamine to the United States

country_links.context: The organization distributes cocaine, fentanyl, and methamphetamine into the United States.

La Raza Nation.description: La Raza Nation is a street gang founded in Chicago in 1973, primarily composed of Hispanic members of Mexican or Central American origin. Its colors are green, white, and red, and its symbols include the Mexican flag, cross, and six-point star. The gang is affiliated with the Folk Nation and has been involved in conflicts with various other gangs. It has expanded from Chicago to other states including Illinois, Wisconsin, Ohio, Florida, and Georgia.

La Unión Tepito.description: Mexican criminal organization founded in 2009 in Tepito, Mexico City, under the tutelage of Édgar Valdez Villarreal. It engages in drug trafficking, kidnapping, extortion, murder, money laundering, and other crimes. The group operates primarily in Greater Mexico City and several Mexican states, and is known for using minors in criminal activities. It remains active as of 2021.

Lanzino.description: The Lanzino 'ndrina is a criminal clan of the 'Ndrangheta based in Cosenza, Calabria, Italy. It is allied with the Alvaro clan. The organization has been involved in extortion, public contract rigging, and vote-buying, with operations spanning from the 1980s to the present. Key members include Ettore Lanzino, who died in prison in 2024.

Lashkar-e-Taiba.description: Pakistani Islamist jihadist militant organization founded in 1985–1986 by Hafiz Saeed and others with funding from Osama bin Laden. Its primary objective is to merge Kashmir with Pakistan and seeks destruction of India, Hinduism, and Judaism through jihad. Designated as a terrorist group by the UN and many countries, it has carried out major attacks in India including the 2008 Mumbai attacks. It is supported by Pakistan's ISI and operates primarily in Kashmir.

Latella 'ndrina.description: The Latella 'ndrina is a clan of the 'Ndrangheta, a mafia-type organization based in Reggio Calabria, Italy. Founded in the 1980s by Pasquale Latella, it controls the Ravagnese and Croce Valanidi quarters and is allied with the Ficara, De Stefano, and Pelle 'ndrine. The clan has been involved in feuds and alliances, notably during the Second 'Ndrangheta war, and was investigated in 2013 for monopolizing the construction sector. It remains active.

Latin Counts.description: The Latin Counts is an Indigenous Latino American street gang based in Chicago, Illinois, with a significant branch in Detroit, Michigan. Founded in 1955 by Tejano youth in the Pilsen neighborhood, it is a member of the People Nation alliance. The gang is involved in drug trafficking, racketeering, and other criminal activities.

Latin Eagles.description: The Latin Eagles are a Puerto Rican street gang founded in Chicago, Illinois in 1964. Originally formed as a club to protect against white greaser gangs, it evolved into a criminal organization. The gang is known for spawning the Young Lords political group in the late 1960s. They are aligned with the Folk Nation and have been active continuously since their founding.

Latin Kings.description: The Latin Kings is a predominantly Hispanic street and prison gang founded in Chicago in 1954 by Puerto Ricans. It operates under two main factions: the King Motherland Chicago (KMC) and the Bloodline, with a total membership estimated between 22,000 and 42,500. The gang is involved in drug trafficking, assault, burglary, homicide, identity theft, and money laundering, with primary income from street-level narcotics distribution. It has a presence in 31 U.S. states and several other countries.

Lenox Avenue Gang.description: Early 20th-century New York City street gang based in Harlem, founded in the early 1900s by Harry Horowitz. It consisted mostly of pickpockets and burglars, allied with the Eastman Gang. The gang was involved in muggings, robberies, and murder, notably the assassination of gambler Herman Rosenthal in 1912. After the execution of its leaders in 1914, the gang disbanded.

Lenox Street Boys.description: One of the oldest and most dangerous street gangs in Boston, Massachusetts, originating in the Lenox Street Projects in Roxbury possibly dating back to the 1950s. The gang has been active since at least the 1980s, involved in drug trafficking, robbery, and murder. They have engaged in long-standing feuds with rival gangs such as the Columbia Point Dawgs. Law enforcement raids in 2011 and 2016 resulted in numerous arrests.

Libertadores del Vichada.description: Colombian drug trafficking neo-paramilitary group involved in the Colombian armed conflict. It was one of the most important drug trafficking organizations in eastern Colombia, formed from the remnants of ERPAC. The group was led by Martín Farfán Díaz González, alias 'Pijarbey', and was completely dismantled after the capture of its last leader in September 2017.

Liga da Justiça.description: Brazilian militia faction based in Rio de Janeiro, founded in 1995 by Ricardo Teixeira Cruz (Batman) and Aldemar Almeida dos Santos (Robin). It is the largest and most well-known militia group in Rio, involved in assassinations, extortion, and terrorist activities. The group has been led by Toni Ângelo de Souza Aguiar (Robin) after Batman's imprisonment.

Live Oak Boys.description: Irish-American street gang based in New Orleans, formed in 1858 by 'Red' Bill Wilson. Named after their oaken clubs, they dominated the city during the 1860s and 1870s, engaging in assault, arson, and vandalism for hire. Internal conflicts and law enforcement pressure led to their decline by 1880.

Lo Russo clan.description: The Lo Russo clan was a Neapolitan Camorra clan operating in the Miano area of Naples, formed in the late 1970s by the Lo Russo brothers. It was a member of the Nuova Famiglia and later the Secondigliano Alliance, involved in drug trafficking, extortion, and other crimes. The clan was considered overthrown after the arrests of its leaders and affiliates.

Locale di Piscopio.description: Italian 'Ndrangheta organization based in the Piscopio district of Vibo Valentia, founded between 2009 and 2010. It engages in drug trafficking and extortion, with connections to other 'Ndrangheta clans in Calabria and Turin. The group was involved in the Stefanaconi feud (2011-2012) and has been targeted by multiple police operations.

Logan Heights Gang.description: The Logan Heights Gang is a Sureño street gang based in Southeast San Diego, California, founded in the 1970s from the unification of several Mexican-American gangs. It is composed of five main subsets and has spread to other U.S. cities and Tijuana, Mexico. The gang is involved in drug trafficking, murder, kidnapping, and human smuggling, and has alliances with the Tijuana Cartel and Mexican Mafia.

Lone Legion Brotherhood.description: An outlaw motorcycle club based in Blenheim, New Zealand, established in the 1970s. It controlled the town as its exclusive territory until around 2007. The club was involved in a fatal shooting in 2007 and later demolished its clubhouse. In 2019, it patched over to the Outlaws MC.

Loners Motorcycle Club.description: International outlaw motorcycle club founded in Woodbridge, Ontario, Canada in 1979 by Frank Lenti and Gennaro Raso. Operates chapters in Canada, Italy, the United States, and other countries. Known for its elaborate patch and involvement in conflicts with other biker gangs. Estimated to have 1,000 active members globally.

Loomis Gang.description: The Loomis Gang was a family of outlaws operating in Central New York during the mid-19th century. Founded by George Washington Loomis Sr. and his wife Rhoda Mallet, the gang specialized in horse theft, livestock rustling, counterfeiting, and burglary. They expanded into a multi-state syndicate under Wash Loomis in the 1840s, buying protection from authorities and cultivating local goodwill to avoid prosecution.

country_links.context: The Loomis Gang sold stolen horses in Canada.

Lopers 13.description: Lopers 13 is a Mexican American street gang founded in Santa Ana, California, in the late 1980s or early 1990s. It is the largest gang in Santa Ana by territory, controlling areas including Main Street, Minnie Street, First Street, and Edinger Avenue. The gang is involved in drug trafficking and has been targeted by law enforcement operations.

Los Angeles crime family.description: Italian American Mafia crime family based in Los Angeles, California, founded in the early 20th century by Joseph Ardizzone. It gained power through bootlegging during Prohibition and peaked under Jack Dragna in the 1940s-1950s. The family has declined since the 1980s due to RICO prosecutions and competition from other gangs, but remains the last Mafia family in California.

country_links.evidence_quote: the Canadian mobster and Musitano crime family associate Albert Iavarone was inducted into the Los Angeles family shortly before he was shot dead in Hamilton, Ontario on September 13, 2018.
country_links.context: The organization inducted Canadian mobster Albert Iavarone as a liaison between Canadian and American Mafia.

Los Ardillos.description: Los Ardillos is a Mexican criminal group based in the La Montaña region of Guerrero, founded around 2000 by Celso Ortega Rosas and his sons. It engages in drug trafficking, extortion, and kidnapping, and has been a major source of violence in the region, particularly targeting indigenous communities. The group was initially allied with the Beltrán Leyva Cartel and later became involved in a violent conflict with the Cártel de los Rojos. Despite the arrest and subsequent killing of its founder, the group remains active.

Los Cachiros.description: Honduran criminal organization dedicated to drug trafficking, founded in the early 1990s by cattle ranchers in Colón and Olancho departments. It became one of the largest transport groups in Honduras, accumulating a net worth of nearly one billion dollars. The group purchased cocaine from Colombian organizations and passed it to the Sinaloa Cartel and other Mexican groups. It had extensive business and political interests, including ties to the Honduran elite and government officials.

Los Caparrapos.description: Colombian narcoparamilitary group that emerged as dissidents of the Autodefensas Gaitanistas de Colombia/Clan del Golfo. Based in the Bajo Cauca region of Antioquia, they engaged in massacres, murders, extortion, forced displacement, drug trafficking, and illegal mining. The group was dismantled in 2021 after the death of its leader Robinson Gil Tapias.

Los Chapitos.description: Los Chapitos is a splinter faction of the Sinaloa Cartel in Mexico, formed around 2016 by the sons of Joaquín 'El Chapo' Guzmán. The group emerged after Guzmán's capture and extradition, taking control of large parts of the cartel's territory in Sinaloa and neighboring states. They are known for drug trafficking, violence, and conflicts with rival factions and government forces. The group remains active as of the article's last update.

Los Charlines.description: Galician drug trafficking clan founded in 1975 by Manuel Charlín Gama and his family. Based in Galicia, Spain, they engaged in smuggling of food, tobacco, hashish, and later cocaine and heroin. The clan was dismantled in Operation Nécora in 1990 but continued operations, with members serving prison sentences. They are considered one of the most important drug trafficking clans in Galicia.

Los Chone Killers.description: Ecuadorian criminal and narcoterrorist organization dedicated to drug trafficking, contract killing, and other crimes. Originally an armed wing of Los Choneros, it split off in 2020 after the assassination of its former leader Jorge Luis Zambrano. Based primarily in Guayas province with its center of operations in Durán. The group has been involved in prison massacres and terrorist attacks, and maintains a territorial dispute with the Latin Kings since 2023.

Los Choneros.description: Los Choneros is an organized crime syndicate from Ecuador, involved in drug trafficking, extortion, robbery, and other crimes. Originating in Manabí Province in the 1990s, it functions as the armed wing of the Sinaloa Cartel in Ecuador. The group has significant influence over security officials and politicians, and its leader José Adolfo Macías Villamar escaped prison in 2024, triggering an armed conflict. As of 2025, the group remains active with an estimated 12,000-20,000 members.

Los Ciclones.description: Los Ciclones, also known as the Facción Matamoros, is a Mexican criminal organization and one of the four main factions of the Gulf Cartel. Based in Matamoros, Tamaulipas, it was founded between 2010 and 2012 by Rafael Cárdenas Vélez. The group is engaged in drug trafficking, murder, kidnapping, extortion, and money laundering, and operates primarily in northeastern Mexico and the border area with Brownsville, Texas. It is currently active and in conflict with rival cartels such as the Cartel del Noreste and Los Metros.

Los Huistas.description: Los Huistas are a powerful Guatemalan criminal organization based in Huehuetenango, near the Mexican border. Founded in the late 1990s, they control a strategic drug trafficking route for cocaine, methamphetamine, and heroin from Central America to the United States. They have evolved from transporters to producers of methamphetamine and money launderers, infiltrating state institutions. The group maintains a centralized hierarchy and is led by Eugenio Darío Molina-López until his capture in 2026.

Los Lagartos.description: Ecuadorian narcoterrorist cartel based in Guayaquil, founded as 'Los Cubanos' and initially engaged in contract killings. It now handles international drug trafficking, micro-trafficking, extortion, and robbery, providing logistics and security for groups like the Jalisco New Generation Cartel. Considered the second most powerful criminal group in Ecuador after Los Choneros, with whom it fiercely competes for territory. The group recruits young people from marginalized neighborhoods and has operated within the prison system for at least a decade.

Los Lobos.description: Ecuadorian criminal and terrorist organization specializing in drug trafficking and contract killing. Formed in 2020 as a splinter group from Los Choneros after the death of Jorge Luis Zambrano. Operates primarily in Latacunga, Riobamba, Cuenca, Machala, and Pastaza province, with over 8,000 members. Involved in prison riots and political violence, including the assassination of presidential candidate Fernando Villavicencio.

Los Mazatlecos.description: Mexican criminal organization formerly the enforcer gang of the Beltrán Leyva Cartel, operating independently since 2017 under Fausto Isidro Meza Flores. Based in Guasave, Sinaloa, it engages in drug trafficking, murder, kidnapping, and extortion. The group is in a turf war with the Sinaloa Cartel and active in Sinaloa, Sonora, Durango, and Nayarit.

Los Metros.description: Los Metros is a Mexican criminal organization and a splinter faction of the Gulf Cartel, based in Reynosa, Tamaulipas. It was founded around 2005 by Samuel Flores Borrego, also known as 'Metro 3' or 'M3'. The group is one of five factions that emerged from the Gulf Cartel's internal fragmentation and is involved in drug trafficking, homicide, money laundering, and other crimes. It remains active and is allied with the Jalisco New Generation Cartel and the Gulf Cartel.

Los Mexicles.description: Los Mexicles is a Mexican and Mexican-American gang founded in 1987 in Ciudad Juárez, Chihuahua. It is an armed wing of the Sinaloa Cartel in the border region, involved in murder, extortion, drug trafficking, kidnapping, and vehicle theft. The gang operates primarily in several Mexican states and parts of Texas, and is known for using Nahuatl messages in U.S. prisons. Its members are mostly deportees or descendants of Mexicans, and leaving the gang is punishable by death.

country_links.context: Los Mexicles was founded in Texas and operates there, with territory in Texas.
