Los Negros.description: Los Negros was the main armed wing of the Beltrán Leyva Cartel in Mexico, formed in 2003 to support the Sinaloa Cartel against the Gulf Cartel and Los Zetas. After the split between the Beltrán Leyva brothers and Joaquín 'El Chapo' Guzmán, Los Negros allied with Los Zetas. Led by Édgar Valdez Villarreal 'La Barbie', the group was involved in drug trafficking, murder, and extortion across multiple Mexican states. Following Valdez's capture in 2010, the group fragmented into independent cells.

Los Ninis.description: Los Ninis are the main armed wing of the Los Chapitos faction of the Sinaloa Cartel, composed of young hitmen aged 20-35 trained in urban combat. They operate as security forces for Los Chapitos leaders, and are involved in torture, murder, drug trafficking, and controlling cartel territories. Based in Culiacán, Sinaloa, they were formed to maintain Los Chapitos' dominance over the Sinaloa Cartel.

mentioned_in.title: Bandas y grupos emergentes en Colombia

Los Paisas.description: Colombian criminal and narcoparamilitary organization based in Medellín, formed in 2008 from remnants of paramilitary groups demobilized during peace talks (2004-2006). It was founded by former members of the Oficina de Envigado after the extradition of Don Berna. The group engaged in drug trafficking, extortion, kidnapping, and murder. It was dissolved by Colombian security forces in 2014, with remaining members joining the Clan Úsuga.

mentioned_in.title: Bandas y grupos emergentes en Colombia

Los Pelones.description: Los Pelones is an enforcer gang originally part of the Sinaloa Cartel, founded in 2004 in Guerrero, Mexico. It distributed narcotics in tourist spots and later became independent after the Beltrán-Leyva split. The group allied with the Gulf Cartel in 2012 and later became independent again due to fragmentation. It is involved in drug trafficking, murder, and extortion.

Los Pepes.description: Colombian paramilitary group formed in 1992 to fight Pablo Escobar and the Medellín Cartel. Financed by the Cali Cartel and led by the Castaño brothers, they waged a small-scale war involving assassinations and bombings. The group disbanded after Escobar's death in 1993, with many members later joining the United Self-Defense Forces of Colombia (AUC).

Los Priscos.description: Colombian criminal group affiliated with the Medellín Cartel, active in the 1980s and early 1990s. Named after the four Prisco Lopera brothers, they functioned as the armed wing of the cartel, carrying out assassinations ordered by Pablo Escobar. The group was dismantled in 1991 when its leaders were killed by police.

Los Rastrojos.description: Colombian narcoparamilitary group formed by dissidents of the AUC after its demobilization in 2006. It became independent following the murder of its founder in Venezuela in 2008 and was one of Colombia's most important drug trafficking organizations. The group finances itself through cocaine, marijuana, and heroin trafficking, as well as illegal gold mining. It operated mainly in Valle del Cauca and Cali, with influence extending to other parts of Colombia and western Venezuela. By 2017, the group had fragmented into smaller factions.

Los Rojos.description: Los Rojos is a faction of the Gulf Cartel, formed in the late 1990s as an armed wing for security. Based in Reynosa, Tamaulipas, Mexico, it engaged in infighting with the Metros faction after the assassination of Samuel Flores Borrego in 2011. The group is involved in murder and kidnapping, and remains active but less powerful.

Los Solidos.description: Los Solidos is a street gang founded in the early 1990s by Lawrence Beauvais in Hartford, Connecticut. The gang formed from the merger of two other gangs to defend against larger rivals like the Latin Kings. It operates in Hartford, Springfield, Massachusetts, and other northeastern cities, involved in drug trafficking, weapons sales, and violent crimes. Despite leadership arrests, the gang remains active as of 2026.

Los Talibanes.description: Mexican criminal organization based in San Luis Potosí and Zacatecas, founded in 2012 by Iván Velázquez Caballero, a former member of Los Zetas. The group broke from Los Zetas and allied with the Gulf Cartel. Engaged in drug trafficking, particularly fentanyl, and migrant smuggling. Since 2019, they have fought alongside the Jalisco New Generation Cartel and Sinaloa Cartel for control of Zacatecas.

Los Tiguerones.description: Ecuadorian narcoterrorist and criminal organization specializing in drug trafficking, extortion, kidnapping, and murder. It split from Los Choneros in 2021 after the assassination of Los Choneros leader Jorge Luís Zambrano. Originating in Esmeraldas, it expanded to Guayaquil and Manta. The group gained notoriety for a violent takeover of TC Televisión in 2024.

Los Viagras.description: Los Viagras is a Mexican criminal group based in Michoacán, founded around 2014 as a self-defense group and later evolving into a drug trafficking organization. Led by Nicolás Sierra Santana, the group is involved in methamphetamine production and transportation, and has been in conflict with the Jalisco New Generation Cartel. They are known for using minors as human shields and generating violence in the Tierra Caliente region. As of 2024, they have allied with the CJNG.

Los Zetas.description: Los Zetas is a fractured Mexican criminal syndicate and designated terrorist organization, known for extreme violence including beheadings and torture. Originally formed in the late 1990s as the enforcement arm of the Gulf Cartel by deserters from the Mexican Army, they broke away in 2010 to become an independent cartel. They were once Mexico's largest cartel by territory but have fragmented since the mid-2010s, with many factions absorbed or eliminated. They are based in Nuevo Laredo, Tamaulipas, and engage in drug trafficking, extortion, kidnapping, and other illegal activities.

Los Ántrax.description: Los Ántrax is a large enforcer unit and hit squad for the Sinaloa Cartel, based in Culiacán, Sinaloa, Mexico. The group provides armed security to drug lord Ismael 'El Mayo' Zambada and is responsible for numerous homicides and violent attacks. It is considered the Sinaloa Cartel's largest and deadliest enforcer unit.

Lost Breed Motorcycle Club.description: Outlaw motorcycle club based in Nelson, New Zealand, founded in 1976. The club claimed opposition to methamphetamine and domestic violence, though police viewed these claims skeptically. It was shut down by the Hells Angels in December 2015, with some members joining a new Hells Angels chapter in Nelson.

Hells Angels MC criminal allegations and incidents in the United Kingdom

Loyal to Familia.description: Loyal to Familia is a Danish street gang established in Nørrebro, Copenhagen in 2013. It engaged in drug trafficking and had a membership of 225 in 2017. The gang was ordered dissolved by the Danish Supreme Court on September 1, 2021, for lacking a legal purpose, marking the first such ruling since 1924.

LRGP.description: LRGP (Lombard, Rother, Gibson, and Playter) was a gang based in the Broadway-Fillmore area of Buffalo, New York, founded in the 2000s. It was primarily involved in drug trafficking, including marijuana and crack cocaine, and engaged in violent conflict with the rival Bailey Boys. The gang was heavily targeted by law enforcement, leading to multiple arrests and its eventual disbandment by 2016.

mentioned_in.title: List of gangs in the Netherlands

Lucchese crime family.description: The Lucchese crime family is one of the Five Families of the American Mafia in New York City. Originating in the early 1920s, it was led by Tommy Gagliano and later Tommy Lucchese, becoming a powerful force in organized crime. The family controls rackets including gambling, loansharking, drug trafficking, and labor racketeering, primarily in New York and New Jersey. It is still active today.

country_links.evidence_quote: the New Jersey faction controlled a $2.2 billion illegal gambling, money laundering and racketeering ring based in New Jersey and Costa Rica.
country_links.context: The Lucchese family's New Jersey faction controlled a gambling, money laundering and racketeering ring based in Costa Rica.

Lucchese crime family Brooklyn faction.description: The Lucchese crime family's Brooklyn faction is a group of Italian-American mobsters within the Lucchese crime family that control organized crime activities in the New York metropolitan area, predominantly based in Brooklyn and Staten Island. It was created in the early 2000s by merging the Vario Crew and the 19th Hole Crew. The faction is involved in racketeering, bookmaking, loansharking, extortion, gambling, and other illegal activities. It remains active as part of the Lucchese family.

mentioned_in.title: Lucchese crime family New Jersey faction

Lucchese crime family New Jersey faction.description: A crew of Italian-American mobsters operating in Northern New Jersey, part of the Lucchese crime family. Founded in the 1920s, it was led by Anthony Accetturo and Michael Taccetta during the 1970s-1980s. A war with New York members in the late 1980s led to Accetturo becoming a government witness. Currently controlled by Joseph R. Perna.

own_sources.title: Lucchese crime family New Jersey faction

Lucerne Street Doggz.description: Street gang based in the Lucerne Street area of Mattapan, Boston, founded in 2003. Primarily African American, involved in drug trafficking, robbery, and murder. In 2006, the gang was responsible for 37 shootings, accounting for 10% of all shootings in Boston that year.

Lueders Park Piru.description: The Lueders Park Piru is a set of the Piru gang alliance, part of the larger Bloods alliance, based in Compton, California. Originating as the Lueders Park Hustlers, it was instrumental in forming the Bloods in 1972. The gang is involved in drug trafficking, robbery, and weapons sales, with approximately 140 members in 2005. It has ongoing rivalries with several Crips sets.

Luppino crime family.description: The Luppino crime family is an 'Ndrangheta organized crime family based in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada, founded in the 1950s by Giacomo Luppino. It is one of three centralized Mafia organizations in Hamilton, alongside the Musitano and Papalia families. The family has strong connections with the Buffalo crime family and has been involved in racketeering, drug trafficking, and other criminal activities. By 2018, the Violi family had increased its role, but both Violi brothers were imprisoned for drug offenses. The family is now believed to be the Buffalo family's Canadian crew.

country_links.evidence_quote: The Luppinos have had strong connections with the Buffalo crime family of Buffalo, New York .
country_links.context: The Luppino crime family has strong connections with the Buffalo crime family based in Buffalo, New York, and has fallen under its control, acting as its Canadian crew.

Lynwood Vikings.description: The Lynwood Vikings is a deputy gang within the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department (LASD), formerly based at the Lynwood station. Composed of sworn deputy sheriffs, it has been described as a neo-Nazi, white supremacist gang engaged in racially motivated hostility. Members have been involved in police brutality and corruption, with tattoos symbolizing officer-involved shootings. The gang rose to prominence in the 1990s amid misconduct litigation.

Lynx gang.description: The Lynx gang was a Birmingham-based gang originally composed of British Pakistani members, founded in the 1970s in the Sparkhill area to protect the local British Pakistani community from White power skinheads. It is known for having former member Moazzem Begg, who was part of an unofficial junior version of the gang.

Lyons Crime Family.description: The Lyons Crime Family is an organised crime group based in Glasgow, Scotland, involved in drug trafficking, money laundering, extortion, and violence. Founded in the 1990s by Eddie Lyons Snr, the group has been engaged in a deadly feud with the Daniel Crime Family since 2001. The family operates in the UK, Spain, and the UAE, and has ties to the Kinahan Organized Crime Group.

Maceo Organization.description: The Maceo Organization was a criminal syndicate that controlled Galveston, Texas, from the 1920s to the 1980s. Founded by brothers Sam and Rosario Maceo, it engaged in illegal gambling, prostitution, bootlegging, and racketeering. The organization wielded significant political influence, with ties to Texas Governor James V. Allred and other officials. It was eventually succeeded by the Fertitta Organization.

Mafia Capitale.description: Mafia Capitale is an organized crime organization based in Rome, Italy, founded in 1999 by Massimo Carminati and Salvatore Buzzi. It engaged in money laundering, racketeering, political corruption, and bid rigging, stealing funds from city services. The organization was dismantled following a major investigation in 2014, and in 2020 Italy's Supreme Court ruled that its acts did not constitute mafia association.

Mala del Brenta.description: Italian criminal organization based in Veneto, founded in the late 1970s by Felice Maniero. It engaged in kidnappings, robberies, drug and arms trafficking, money laundering, and murders. The group was heavily hit in the 1990s after Maniero's arrest and collaboration with authorities.

country_links.context: The organization trafficked cocaine from South America through Spain to Venice.

Mali Boys.description: Organised street gang based in Leyton and Walthamstow, East London, controlling the local drug trade with extreme violence. Emerged in 2015 after splintering from the Beaumont Crew. Known for county lines drug networks, child exploitation, and hundreds of violent attacks. Estimated 40-100 members, predominantly male and ethnically diverse.

Mallardo clan.description: The Mallardo clan is a Camorra crime clan based in Giugliano, Campania, Italy, founded in the late 1970s by Francesco Mallardo. It is a key member of the Secondigliano Alliance, considered the most powerful active Camorra group. The clan is involved in racketeering, smuggling, extortion, and drug trafficking, and has dominated the Neapolitan underworld since the 1990s. In 2011, Italian police seized assets worth €600 million from the clan.

Mamak Gang.description: The Mamak Gang is a notorious Malaysian gang active since the early 1990s, specializing in carjacking and robberies. They are most infamous for stealing RM 12 million worth of gold bars from the Malaysia Airlines cargo complex in 1994. Despite multiple arrests and preventive detention, they continued operations from prison until their last three members were arrested in December 2006.

mentioned_in.title: Hells Angels MC criminal allegations and incidents in the United Kingdom

Maniac Latin Disciples.description: Predominantly Hispanic street gang based in Chicago, Illinois, founded in 1966 as a Humboldt Park baseball club. They are part of the Folks Alliance and are involved in drug trafficking, assault, auto theft, robbery, homicide, money laundering, and weapons trafficking. The gang has an estimated 7,500-10,000 members and operates across multiple U.S. states.

Manitoba Warriors.description: Indigenous street gang based in Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada, founded in 1993 at Stony Mountain Institution to rival the Indian Posse. Engages in drug trafficking, auto theft, illegal firearms, gambling, and supports Hells Angels activities. Designated by CISC as indigenous-based organized crime. Active with approximately 300 members.

Manson Family.description: The Manson Family was a commune, gang, and cult led by Charles Manson, active in California from the late 1960s to early 1970s. The group consisted of approximately 100 followers who lived an unconventional lifestyle, using psychoactive drugs and radicalized by Manson's teachings. They committed at least nine murders, including the Tate–LaBianca murders, and other crimes. The group dissolved after Manson and other members were arrested.

Mara Mao Mao.description: A Salvadoran gang founded in the late 1990s by Carlos Alberto García. It is involved in drug trafficking, extortion, and territorial control, primarily in El Salvador. Smaller than MS-13 or Barrio 18, it maintains a hierarchical structure and engages in violent conflicts with rival gangs. The group remains active as of the present.

Mara Salvatrucha.description: International criminal gang originating in Los Angeles, California in the 1980s, initially formed to protect Salvadoran immigrants. It expanded through deportations to Central America and is active in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Central America. Engages in drug trafficking, murder, extortion, and other crimes. Designated as a terrorist organization by the US, Canada, and El Salvador.

March 23 Movement.description: The March 23 Movement (M23) is a Congolese rebel paramilitary group backed by Rwanda, based in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. It was founded in 2012 by former members of the National Congress for the Defence of the People (CNDP) who mutinied against the government. M23 captured Goma in 2012 but withdrew after negotiations, and resumed operations in 2022. It is the principal member of the Congo River Alliance.

country_links.evidence_quote: Makenga sought to recruit additional fighters from the DRC, Rwanda, and Uganda. Although he received some assistance from sympathetic Rwandan officials who facilitated recruitment in Rwanda...

country_links.context: M23 uses Uganda for recruitment, training, and meetings to coordinate operations.

Marginals.description: The Marginals, also known as the Paddy Irish gang, was a New York street gang active in the early 1900s. Based on the Lower West Side of Manhattan, they were involved in extortion and labor slugging. Under leader Thomas F. 'Tanner' Smith, they succeeded the Hudson Dusters in their territory. The gang's reign ended with Smith's murder in 1919.

Marielitos.description: Marielitos are Cuban immigrants who arrived in the United States during the 1980 Mariel boatlift, with a subset involved in organized crime. They are based in the United States, primarily Miami, and are known for drug and arms trafficking, gambling, and contract killing. The group emerged in the early 1980s and remains active, with alliances with the American Mafia and other cartels.

country_links.evidence_quote: Marielito gang activity isn't as endemic as it was in the 80s, but Marielito gangs are still active in Los Angeles, Washington and New York City (especially the South Bronx ).
country_links.context: Marielitos immigrated to and operate in the United States, with gang activity in Los Angeles, Washington, and New York City.

Market Street Commandos.description: The Market Street Commandos was an outlaw motorcycle club that participated in the 1947 Hollister incident alongside the Boozefighters and Pissed Off Bastards of Bloomington. The club merged with the Hells Angels in 1954 to become their San Francisco chapter.

Markham Gang.description: The Markham Gang was a 19th-century criminal organization based in Ontario, Canada, evolving from groups supporting the Upper Canada Rebellion of 1837. It engaged in petty theft and counterfeiting, using a courier network to transport stolen goods. The gang was broken up in 1846, with members imprisoned but later released.

Martinez Familia Sangeros.description: Puerto Rican criminal organization founded in the 1980s by Quitoni Martinez in Aguada, Puerto Rico. It operates as a mafia-style group with six crime families, involved in drug trafficking, racketeering, extortion, and money laundering. The organization has connections with Colombian cartels and other international crime groups, and maintains a presence in the United States, Mexico, Spain, and Panama.

Massa Carcerária.description: Brazilian criminal faction originating from the state of Ceará, founded in 2021 by former members of Comando Vermelho dissatisfied with the group's leadership. It expanded with defectors from Guardiões do Estado (GDE) and became the largest faction in Caucaia by 2022. Engaged in violent conflicts with rival factions, including massacres and forced evictions. As of 2023, it maintains an alliance with Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC).

Matsuba-kai.description: The Matsuba-kai is a yakuza organization based in Tokyo, Japan, founded in March 1953 from remnants of the Sekine-gumi and Fujita-gumi. It is a designated yakuza group with an estimated 280 active members as of 2024. The group is a member of the Kantō Hatsuka-kai federation and has been involved in drug smuggling, violent feuds, and protests.

country_links.evidence_quote: In the 1980s the gang was caught smuggling 12 kilos of heroin into Canada .
country_links.context: The Matsuba-kai smuggled heroin into Canada.

Mau Maus.description: A 1950s Puerto Rican street gang based in Brooklyn, New York City, formed in 1957 by youths from the Fort Greene Housing Project. Known for its violent activities including murder and drug trafficking, the gang gained notoriety through its leader Nicky Cruz, whose story was documented in the book and film 'The Cross and the Switchblade'. The gang was active until around 1962.

McCarthy-Dundon.description: The McCarthy-Dundon gang is a criminal organization based in Limerick City, Ireland, involved in drug dealing, extortion, and armed robbery. Founded in the 2000s by James McCarthy and Dessie Dundon, the gang has been a central player in the Limerick feud, which has claimed up to 13 lives. The gang has been responsible for high-profile murders of innocent people and has been largely inactive since 2010 after its leaders were imprisoned.

country_links.context: The gang conspired to import weapons from the UK, with undercover agents from the Serious Organised Crime Agency involved.

Median Empire Motorcycle Club.description: German outlaw motorcycle club founded in 2011 in Cologne with predominantly Kurdish membership. Led by Kawan Azad, a former member of the Mongols. Claims no involvement in organized crime, earning income from membership fees and providing bouncers. Has chapters in Germany, Dubai, and support clubs in Sweden.

Menace of Destruction.description: Menace of Destruction (MOD) is a Hmong street gang founded in 1988 in Fresno, California. Originally called Masters of Destruction, it is one of the oldest active Asian street gangs in Northern California and the largest Hmong gang in the United States. The gang is involved in murders, shootings, drug trafficking (marijuana and methamphetamine), and weapon trafficking. It is active in California, the Midwestern United States, and other areas with large Hmong communities.

They were born to Giuseppe Messina, who established brothels in Malta and Egypt. The brothers expanded their operations to London's Soho district, controlling a large network of prostitutes and bribing police. Their criminal activities declined after the 1950s.

Metz Gang.description: The Metz Gang was a drug ring founded by Glenn Metz and his brother Cordell Metz, active from 1985 to 1992 in New Orleans. It distributed approximately 1,000 kilograms of cocaine in the New Orleans metropolitan area and committed murders, attempted murders, and other violent crimes. The gang was dismantled after a 1993 conviction of its leaders.

Mexican Mafia.description: The Mexican Mafia, also known as La eMe, is a powerful criminal organization based in the United States, primarily composed of individuals of Mexican origin. Founded on November 15, 1957, by Luis "Huero Buff" Flores in a California youth prison, it is one of the oldest and most powerful prison gangs in the U.S. The organization controls illegal activities within prisons and on the streets, including drug trafficking, extortion, and murder. Despite its name, it has no origins in Mexico and operates almost exclusively in the United States.

Mexikanemi.description: Mexikanemi, also known as the Texas Mexican Mafia, is a Mexican-American prison and street gang established in the Texas state prison system in 1984. It operates independently from the California Mexican Mafia and engages in drug trafficking, loan sharking, money laundering, and other illegal activities. The gang has a formal written constitution and a hierarchical structure. It is based in Texas and remains active.

Miami Boys.description: The Miami Boys was a drug trafficking organization based in Liberty City, Miami, Florida, founded in 1982 by Issac Hicks and James Sawyer. Structured like organized crime with ranks and territories, it expanded into multiple cities across the South and Midwest. The gang was largely eliminated in Atlanta in 1996 and the last dealer in Jacksonville was arrested in 1999.

Mickey Cobras.description: The Mickey Cobras are an African American street gang based in Chicago, Illinois, founded in 1954 as the Egyptian Cobras by James Cogwell. The gang is part of the People Nation alliance and is involved in drug trafficking, robbery, extortion, and murder. It was renamed in honor of Henry "Mickey" Cogwell after his assassination in 1977. The gang remains active in Chicago and the Midwestern United States.

Milenio Cartel.description: The Milenio Cartel was a Mexican criminal organization based in Michoacán and later Jalisco, founded by the Valencia family in the late 1970s. It engaged in drug trafficking, money laundering, murder, and arms trafficking, producing marijuana and heroin. The cartel was a branch of the Sinaloa Federation until its leadership was captured in 2009-2010, leading to its dissolution and the emergence of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel.

Milwaukee crime family.description: The Milwaukee crime family was an Italian American Mafia crime family based in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, founded around 1918 by Vito Guardalabene. At its peak, it had over 50 made members and maintained links to other Midwestern Mafia families. The family was heavily involved in skimming revenue from Las Vegas casinos under boss Frank Balistrieri. After Balistrieri's death in 1993, the Chicago Outfit absorbed the family, and it ceased to exist as an independent organization by 2024.

Minore Mafia clan.description: Historical Sicilian Mafia clan originating from Castellammare del Golfo, founded in the 1910s. It led the Trapani Mafia family from the 1950s and controlled the mandamento of Trapani until a conflict with the Corleonesi led to the assassination of boss Totò Minore in 1982 and the clan's decline. The clan was involved in narcotics trafficking and money laundering.

Mkhedrioni.description: Georgian paramilitary group founded in 1989 by Jaba Ioseliani. Involved in the Georgian Civil War and War in Abkhazia, known for criminal activities such as banditry and extortion. Outlawed in 1995 after an assassination attempt on President Shevardnadze, leading to its dissolution.

Mob Piru.description: The Mob Piru is a set of the Piru gang alliance and a criminal organization, part of the larger Bloods alliance. Based in East Compton, California, it is primarily African American and involved in drug trafficking, robbery, and arms trafficking. Suge Knight, co-founder of Death Row Records, is an affiliate. The set split from Lueders Park Piru at some point.

Moccia clan.description: The Moccia clan is a powerful Camorra clan operating in the northeast area of the Metropolitan City of Naples, Italy, with a strong presence in Lazio. Founded in the 1960s by Gennaro Moccia, it is considered the oldest still active clan in the region. After Gennaro's death, his wife Anna Mazza led the clan, becoming the first woman convicted of Mafia-related crimes in Italy. The clan controls drug trafficking, money laundering, and political corruption, and is known for its vertical structure and lack of pentiti.

Molluso 'ndrina.description: The Molluso 'ndrina is a clan of the 'Ndrangheta based in Platì, Calabria, Italy, founded in the 1970s. It is involved in drug trafficking, money laundering, arms trafficking, extortion, corruption, gambling, and murder. The clan has a strong presence in the province of Milan, particularly in Buccinasco and Corsico, and is allied with the Barbaro and Papalia 'ndrine.

Mongrel Mob.description: The Mongrel Mob is a prominent organised crime group and prison gang based in New Zealand, founded in the 1960s by mainly Pākehā youths in Wellington and Hawke's Bay. It is the largest gang in New Zealand with over thirty chapters, also operating in Australia and Canada. The gang is known for its violent rivalry with Black Power and engages in drug trafficking, weapon trafficking, extortion, and other crimes. Members are identified by red and black colors, a bulldog patch, and facial tattoos.

Moran family.description: The Moran family is a Melbourne-based Australian criminal family involved in drug trafficking, corruption, money laundering, and debt collection. Founded by Lewis Moran in the 1970s, the family was heavily involved in the Melbourne gangland killings, a feud that resulted in over 30 deaths from 1998 to 2010. Key members include matriarch Judy Moran, who was convicted of murder in 2011. The family is allied with the Carlton Crew and rivals with the Williams Gang.

Morello crime family.description: One of the earliest crime families in New York City, based in Italian Harlem. Founded by Giuseppe Morello in the 1890s, it dominated the Italian underworld by defeating the Brooklyn Camorra. The family engaged in racketeering, counterfeiting, and murder, and was the predecessor of the Genovese crime family. It was active until 1931.

Motisi Mafia clan.description: Historical Sicilian Mafia clan from the Pagliarelli area in Palermo, founded in 1936. One of the oldest active Mafia clans in Palermo, it has been involved in the Sicilian Mafia Commission and allied with the Corleonesi. Members have been convicted for murders of anti-mafia judges and rival clan members. Currently led by Giovanni Motisi, a fugitive since 1993.

Muerte a Secuestradores.description: Colombian paramilitary group and private army formed in 1981 by drug cartels, politicians, and landowners to protect economic interests and fight kidnapping. It assassinated political opponents and community organizers, and waged counterinsurgency against guerrilla groups like FARC-EP and M-19. Supported by the Medellín Cartel and U.S. corporations, it was active through the 1990s.

Mullen Gang.description: The Mullen Gang was an Irish-American street gang operating in South Boston, Massachusetts, founded in the 1950s. Engaged in racketeering, armed robbery, auto theft, and burglary, it fought a decade-long war with the Killeen Gang for control of criminal rackets. In 1972, both gangs were consolidated under the Winter Hill Gang. The gang derived its name from a commemorative plaque to war hero John Joseph Mullen.

Mungiki.description: Mungiki is a banned ethnic organization in Kenya, originating in the late 1980s among Kikuyu youth. It promotes a return to traditional Kikuyu customs and resistance to Westernization, and has been involved in ethnic violence, anti-government resistance, and criminal activities such as protection racketeering. The group is secretive and operates through a cell structure, with a reported peak membership of 500,000. It was banned by the Kenyan government.

Murder, Inc..description: Murder, Inc. was an organized crime group active from 1929 to 1941 that served as the enforcement arm of the National Crime Syndicate. Composed of Jewish-American and Italian-American gangsters, it was based in New York City and responsible for hundreds of contract killings. The group was exposed in 1941 by former member Abe Reles, leading to convictions and executions of many members.

Musitano crime family.description: The Musitano crime family is a 'Ndrangheta organized crime family based in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada, with branches in Italy. Founded by Angelo Musitano in the 1940s, it engaged in racketeering, drug trafficking, and murder. The family was involved in a power struggle with rival Hamilton families, leading to the killings of Johnny Papalia and Carmen Barillaro in 1997. Key members Angelo and Pat Musitano were killed in 2017 and 2020, respectively.

Nacionalni stroj.description: Nacionalni stroj was a neo-Nazi organization based in the Vojvodina region of Serbia. It orchestrated several incidents from 2005 onward. In late 2005, charges were pressed against 18 leading members in Novi Sad, each facing up to eight years in prison. The organization was banned in Serbia in 2011.

Nakano-kai.description: The Nakano-kai was a yakuza gang based in Osaka, Japan, founded by Taro Nakano after World War II. It was known for its bellicosity and was an affiliate of the Yamaguchi-gumi until 1997, when it broke away violently. The gang disbanded after a high-profile assassination of a Yamaguchi-gumi leader led to a police crackdown.

Naserligan.description: Criminal organization primarily active in Gothenburg, Sweden, founded by Naser Dzeljilji around 2000. Involved in drug trafficking, illegal gambling, armed robbery, extortion, and protection racketing. Gained notoriety in 2001 during a violent conflict with the Original Gangsters over control of the illegal gambling market. Membership is diverse, including individuals of Albanian and Swedish descent.

National Liberation Army (Colombia).description: Colombian far-left guerrilla organization founded in 1964 by Fabio Vásquez Castaño and other rebels trained in Cuba. It advocates a composite ideology of Marxism–Leninism, Camilism, and liberation theology. The ELN has been involved in the Colombian conflict and is designated as a terrorist group by several countries. As of 2026, it has approximately 5,000 fighters.

Native Mob.description: The Native Mob is a Native American street gang founded in the 1990s in Minneapolis, Minnesota. It is one of the largest and most violent Native American gangs in the U.S., active in Minnesota, Wisconsin, Colorado, and South Dakota. The gang engages in drug trafficking, assault, robbery, and murder, with an estimated 200 members as of 2021. Members have been placed on the FBI most wanted list in 2025.

Nazi Lowriders.description: A white supremacist prison gang active in Southern California, especially Cypress, with small factions in Chicago and other states. Originated in the mid-1970s, recognized by California prison authorities in 1999. Known for extreme violence and a three-tier hierarchy. Allies include the Aryan Brotherhood and Public Enemy No. 1; rivals include Bloods, Crips, and Black Guerrilla Family.

Neighbors' Sons.description: The Neighbors' Sons was a New York street gang active in the early 1900s, operating in neighborhoods between Bleecker and Grove Streets. They were rivals of the Gopher Gang and the Hudson Dusters. The gang was involved in violent brawls and altercations with law enforcement, and was broken up during police campaigns against street gangs in 1916.

New Irish Republican Army.description: Irish republican paramilitary group formed in 2012 from a merger of the Real IRA, Republican Action Against Drugs (RAAD), and other small militant groups. It is the largest dissident republican group, active mainly in Northern Ireland, and has launched attacks against British security forces. The group is designated as a terrorist organization by the United States.

country_links.evidence_quote: In February 2014, the group sent seven letter bombs to British Army recruitment offices in south-east England; the first time republicans had struck in Britain since 2001.
country_links.context: The New IRA sent letter bombs to British Army recruitment offices in south-east England and attacked PSNI and British Army targets in Northern Ireland.

New Orleans crime family.description: Italian American Mafia crime family based in New Orleans, Louisiana, with a history dating back to the late 19th century. Engaged in racketeering, extortion, gambling, narcotics, and murder. Reached its height under Silvestro Carollo and Carlos Marcello. Declined after Marcello's imprisonment in the 1980s and death in 1993, though some elements may remain active.

country_links.evidence_quote: Territory: Primarily the New Orleans metropolitan area, with additional territory throughout Louisiana, Mississippi and Texas, as well as Las Vegas and Havana
country_links.context: The New Orleans crime family has territory in Havana, indicating it operates there.

New Springville Boys.description: The New Springville Boys was an Italian-American recruitment gang or farm team for the American Mafia, specifically the Bonanno and Colombo crime families. Based in Staten Island, New York, the gang operated from the 1980s to the 2000s, engaging in burglary, robbery, loan sharking, money laundering, drug trafficking, and hijacking. Members were indicted for burglarizing night-deposit boxes across the country and other crimes.

New York divorce coercion gang.description: A Haredi Jewish group based in the New York metropolitan area that kidnapped and tortured Jewish men to force them to grant their wives religious divorces. Founded by Rabbi Mendel Epstein in the mid-1980s, the group was broken up by the FBI in October 2013. Three of four prosecuted members were convicted in late 2015.

New Zealand Nomads.description: The New Zealand Nomads are a large organized criminal gang formed in Horowhenua, New Zealand in 1977 by Dennis Hines. Originally members of Black Power, they split to form their own gang. The gang is involved in drug dealing, theft, murder, and extortion, and has a long-standing rivalry with the Mongrel Mob. As of 2013, they had 103 members in prison.

Newton Gang.description: The Newton Gang was an outlaw group active from around 1919 to 1924, primarily engaged in train and bank robberies across the United States and Canada. Comprising four Newton brothers and an associate, they claimed to have robbed 75 banks and six trains without killing anyone. Their most famous heist was the 1924 Rondout train robbery in Illinois, netting $3 million. The gang's later years saw involvement with the Barrow Gang and continued criminal activity into the 1970s.

Norman Conks.description: Large Catholic sectarian street gang active in Glasgow, based in the Norman Street area of Bridgeton. Active from the 1880s to the 1960s, they evolved from a penny mob into an influential gang. Known for street fighting with the Protestant Billy Boys and friendly relations with the Catholic Calton Tongs. Included young women members.

Norteños.description: The Norteños are a Latino street gang primarily operating in Northern California, affiliated with the Bloods. They originated in 1968 in California prisons as a rival faction to the Sureños, aligning with Nuestra Familia. The gang is involved in drug trafficking and violent conflicts, and has been targeted by federal RICO investigations such as Operation Black Widow.

North Preston's Finest.description: A gang of pimps based in North Preston, Nova Scotia, Canada, founded in the mid-to-late 1980s. The gang is involved in pimping, weapons and drug trafficking, money laundering, and murder. It is the most prominent of approximately ten gangs in the Halifax Regional Municipality, with most members being Black Canadians from North Preston.

North Side Gang.description: The North Side Gang was a multi-ethnic criminal organization in Chicago during Prohibition, active from the early 1920s to the mid-1930s. It was the principal rival of the Chicago Outfit led by Al Capone. Founded by Dean O'Banion and Hymie Weiss, the gang controlled bootlegging, gambling, and robbery on Chicago's North Side. The gang was largely defunct by 1935 after a series of violent conflicts.

Nuestra Familia.description: Nuestra Familia is a Mexican American prison gang founded in 1965 at the Correctional Training Facility in Soledad, California. It operates primarily in Northern California and within prison systems, engaging in drug trafficking, extortion, and robbery. The gang is considered the leadership structure for the Norteños street gang and has a long-standing rivalry with the Mexican Mafia. It remains active with an estimated 250 members.

Nueva Plaza Cartel.description: Mexican criminal organization based in Jalisco, formed in 2018 as a split from the Jalisco New Generation Cartel. It operates primarily in the Guadalajara metropolitan area and disputes territory with CJNG. The group is involved in drug trafficking, money laundering, extortion, robbery, murder, and arms trafficking, and has received funding from the Sinaloa Cartel. Its founding leaders were Érick Valencia Salazar, Emilio Alejandro Pulido Saldaña, and Carlos Enrique Sánchez Martínez.

Numbers Gang.description: The Numbers Gang is a South African prison-based criminal organization founded in the late 1800s in KwaZulu-Natal. It operates through three main factions: the 26s (smuggling), 27s (enforcement), and 28s (protection). The gang is known for its complex rules, internal hierarchy, and secretive nature, and traditionally does not operate outside of prisons.

Nuova Camorra Organizzata.description: Italian Camorra criminal organization founded in the late 1970s by Raffaele Cutolo in Campania. It was a structured, hierarchical organization that became the strongest Camorra clan by 1981, providing a living for at least 200,000 people in the Neapolitan area. It was hostile to the Sicilian Mafia but allied with 'Ndrangheta clans. The organization was considered extinct in the late 1980s after many members were killed or imprisoned.

Nuova camorra pugliese.description: The Nuova camorra pugliese was a criminal organization based in Apulia, Italy, active from the early 1970s to the mid-1980s. It was founded by Raffaele Cutolo as an offshoot of the Nuova Camorra Organizzata. The group operated mainly in the provinces of Foggia and Taranto. It was eventually absorbed by the Sacra corona unita.

Nuova Famiglia.description: The Nuova Famiglia was an Italian Camorra confederation created in the late 1970s to oppose Raffaele Cutolo's Nuova Camorra Organizzata. It was headed by powerful Camorra bosses including Carmine Alfieri, the Nuvoletta brothers, Michele Zaza, Luigi Giuliano, and Antonio Bardellino. The organization was active primarily in Campania and had ties with the Sicilian Mafia. It engaged in various criminal activities such as drug trafficking, murder, and extortion until its dissolution in the 1990s.

Nuova Mala del Brenta.description: The Nuova Mala del Brenta is a mafia-type criminal organization based in the Veneto region of Italy, emerging in the late 1990s as a successor to the original Mala del Brenta. It is involved in drug trafficking, extortion, money laundering, and other crimes. The group is considered by Italian authorities to have all characteristics of a mafia organization under Article 416 bis-cp. It operates in Northeast Italy and has ties to Cosa Nostra and other Italian mafia groups.

Oaxaca Cartel.description: The Oaxaca Cartel was a smaller Mexican drug cartel operating in southern Mexico, particularly in Oaxaca and Chiapas. It focused on marijuana and cocaine trafficking and was allied with the Tijuana Cartel. Founded by Pedro Díaz Parada in the 1970s, the cartel was led by the Díaz-Parada brothers. It was active from 1980 to 2011.

Oda-gumi.description: The Oda-gumi is a yakuza organization founded in 1958 by Hideomi 'Joji' Oda in Osaka, Japan. It operates as a subsidiary of the Yamaguchi-gumi syndicate. The group has been involved in internal conflicts and leadership disputes, and has faced legal issues including arrests of its leaders. As of 2021, its future is uncertain due to leadership demotions and ongoing troubles.

Oficina de Envigado.description: Originally founded as an enforcement wing and debt collection service for Pablo Escobar's Medellín Cartel, Oficina de Envigado evolved into a major drug cartel and criminal organization based in Medellín and Envigado, Colombia. It controls extortion, gambling, and money laundering in the Valle de Aburrá and acts as a mediator and debt collector in drug trafficking disputes. By 2019, its activities shifted from direct drug trafficking to providing services to lower-level traffickers and mafia groups. It maintains connections with Colombian paramilitaries and guerrillas.

Okinawa-Kyokuryū-kai.description: The Okinawa-Kyokuryū-kai is a yakuza criminal organization based on the Okinawa island of Japan. Formed in 1990 after splitting from the Kyokuryu-kai, it is a designated yakuza group with an estimated 300 active members. It is the largest yakuza organization in Okinawa Prefecture, headquartered in Naha, and its official policy forbids drug trafficking.

Omega.description: Omega is a Singaporean prison gang turned organized crime group, founded in 1989 in Chia Keng Prison by Yan Bai. It is a monoethnic Malay Muslim secret society formed to protect Malay inmates from discrimination by Chinese-dominated gangs. The group evolved into a criminal enterprise involved in drug trafficking and other illegal activities, with networks extending beyond Singapore.

country_links.evidence_quote: it became heavily involved in the drug distribution trade from 1996 to the late 2000s, both within and across Singapore's borders into Malaysia.
country_links.context: Omega was involved in drug distribution across Singapore's borders into Malaysia.

On Leong Chinese Merchants Association.description: A tong society based in Chinatown, Manhattan, established in November 1893. It fought a violent war with the Hip Sing Tong for control of Chinatown's rackets and businesses. In recent years, it has been linked to the Ghost Shadows street gang. It has over 30,000 registered members, mostly with commercial or industrial backgrounds.

One Million Boys.description: Robbery gang known for notorious activities around Lagos, Nigeria. Originally formed in Ajegunle by about 20 boys to fight perceived injustice, but later hijacked into robbery, rape, and maiming. A 2014 movie titled '1 Million Boyz' was based on their crimes. In 2012, about 130 suspected members were arrested by Lagos State Police.

Orchard Park Trailblazers.description: A street gang based in the Roxbury area of Boston, Massachusetts, primarily active since the late 1980s. The gang is involved in drug trafficking, robbery, and murder, and has been engaged in a long-running feud with the Columbia Point Dawgs. Law enforcement crackdowns in the 1990s and 2000s led to multiple arrests and indictments.

Orekhovskaya gang.description: The Orekhovskaya gang was a powerful Russian criminal organization based in Moscow, active from the late 1980s to the early 2000s. Founded in 1988 by Sergey Timofeev, it consisted mainly of young former athletes. The gang engaged in extortion, racketeering, money laundering, and murder, and was responsible for thousands of killings. It eventually fragmented and was absorbed by the Solntsevskaya Bratva.

Organizacion de Narcotraficantes Unidos.description: Puerto Rican criminal organization based in Bayamón, founded in 1995 by José López Rosario. It unified drug dealers under one umbrella, becoming the most powerful drug trafficking organization in Puerto Rico by 2009. Involved in trafficking heroin, cocaine, marijuana, crack, Xanax, and Percocet. Declined after mass arrests in 2009-2010.

Ozone Park Boys.description: The Ozone Park Boys are a Gambino crime family Mafia crew based in Ozone Park, Queens, New York City. Founded in the 1980s, they are known for a wide range of criminal activities including a $30 million-a-year sports gambling enterprise, auto theft, murder, and drug trafficking. The crew operated under Ronald Trucchio during the 1990s and remains active.

Pagan's Motorcycle Club.description: Outlaw motorcycle club formed by Lou Dobkin in 1959 in Prince George's County, Maryland. Known for territorial conflicts with the Hells Angels and other clubs. Papalia crime family.description: The Papalia crime family is a 'Ndrangheta organized crime family based in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada, founded by Antonio Papalia in the 1940s. It is one of three centralized Mafia organizations in Hamilton, with strong connections to the Buffalo crime family. The family was decimated after the killings of boss Johnny Papalia and his lieutenant in 1997, ordered by the Musitano family. The last leader, Frank Papalia, died in 2014.

Parisi-Palermiti clan.description: The Parisi-Palermiti clan is a criminal organization originating from Bari, Italy, with its stronghold in the Japigia neighborhood. Founded in the 1980s by Savino Parisi and Eugenio Palermiti, it controls drug trafficking, extortion, and other illegal activities. The clan has infiltrated businesses and local politics, and has been involved in conflicts with rival groups. Despite the imprisonment of its founder, the organization remains active under the leadership of Eugenio Palermiti.

Patriarca crime family.description: Italian-American Mafia crime family operating in New England, with factions in Providence, Rhode Island and Boston, Massachusetts. Founded around 1916 by Gaspare Messina, it was led by Raymond Patriarca from 1954 to 1984. The family engages in illegal gambling, loansharking, extortion, and other rackets. As of 2024, it has approximately 30 made members.

PDC (gang).description: The PDC was a street gang based in Brixton, London, England, primarily active in the 1990s. They were involved in drug trafficking, robberies, and violence, and were the largest gang in the SW9 postcode. The gang later reformed as a music collective and label, while a faction broke off to form the 'Muslim Boys'.

Peaky Blinders.description: The Peaky Blinders were a street gang based in Birmingham, England, operating from the 1880s until the 1920s. They engaged in robbery, violence, racketeering, illegal bookmaking, and gambling control. The gang was known for their distinctive attire and held dominance in Birmingham until being overtaken by the Birmingham Boys in 1920.

aliases: Autodefensas Campesinas de Córdoba y Urabá
Peasant Self-Defenders of Córdoba and Ur.description: Colombian paramilitary group founded by the Castaño brothers in northwestern Colombia to retaliate against FARC-EP. It operated mainly in Antioquia and Córdoba departments, protecting members' farms and drug interests while eliminating left-wing sympathizers. It later became the core of the United Self-Defenders of Colombia (AUC).

Peckham Boys.description: Multi-generational gang based in Peckham, South London, founded in the 1990s. Known for popularising road rap music and involvement in drug trafficking, arms trafficking, robbery, and murder. The gang operates in Peckham, Walworth, and Camberwell, and is divided into subsets by age group. Active as of 2025.

Penny Mobs.description: The Penny Mobs was a street gang active in Glasgow, Scotland during the early 1870s. The name derived from the practice of collecting a penny per member to pay court fines, avoiding imprisonment. Formed by Irish immigrants fleeing the potato famines, the gang declined after courts stopped offering fines as an alternative to imprisonment.

People Nation.description: The People Nation is an American alliance of street gangs based in Chicago, founded in 1978 by leaders of the Vice Lords, Black P. Stones, and Latin Kings. It is a multiethnic coalition involved in drug trafficking, robbery, money laundering, and murder. The alliance is known for its rivalry with the Folk Nation and uses symbols such as a five-pointed star and left-sided identifiers.

People's Aman Committee.description: The People's Aman Committee was a Pakistani political party-affiliated militant group and organized crime gang based in Lyari, Karachi, founded in 2008 by Rehman Dakait. It engaged in drug trafficking, extortion, and gang wars, supporting the Pakistan People's Party. The group was officially banned in 2011 but continued de facto operations until the late 2010s.

It engages in extortion, money laundering, and other criminal activities, with influence in Corsica, mainland France, and abroad. Considered the most powerful criminal group in Corsica as of 2022, it has established political and economic networks. The group was founded in the 2000s and remains active.

Pettingill family.description: The Pettingill family is a Melbourne-based criminal family headed by matriarch Kath Pettingill. Members have convictions for drug trafficking, arms dealing, and armed robberies. The family was involved in the 1988 Walsh Street police shootings and the Melbourne gangland killings, suffering a major blow with the murder of Victor Peirce. Their power has been greatly weakened since.

Philadelphia crime family.description: Italian American Mafia crime family based in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, founded around 1911 by Salvatore Sabella. It operates throughout the Greater Philadelphia metropolitan area and South Jersey, known for violence and internal conflicts. The family experienced a peaceful era under Angelo Bruno (1959-1980) before a series of violent successions and wars. Currently active, with membership estimated at 50 made members and 100 associates as of 2004.

Philadelphia Greek Mob.description: The Philadelphia Greek Mob was a loose-knit Greek-American criminal faction operating in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, closely allied with the Italian-American Philadelphia crime family. Active primarily from the 1970s to the 1980s, it engaged in racketeering, drug trafficking, extortion, loansharking, and illegal gambling. The group was led by Chelsais "Steve" Bouras until his assassination in 1981, after which its influence declined.

Pietraperzia Mafia family.description: The Pietraperzia Mafia family is a crime family of the Sicilian Cosa Nostra based in Pietraperzia, a town in the province of Enna. It has deep historical roots dating back to at least 1900 and reemerged in the 1980s after a period of inactivity. The family is a close ally of the powerful Catania Mafia family and was involved in high-level mafia operations, including preparatory meetings for the 1992 Capaci bombing. It is currently active.

Ping On.description: Boston-based Chinese criminal organization founded in the 1970s by Stephen 'Sky Dragon' Tse, who had ties to the 14K Triad. It engaged in drug trafficking, arms trafficking, fraud, prostitution, human trafficking, illegal gambling, money laundering, extortion, murder, illegal immigration, and racketeering. The group declined after Tse's imprisonment in the 1980s and was linked to the Boston Chinatown massacre.

Pirus.description: The Pirus are a subset of the Bloods gang alliance, founded in 1969 in Compton, California by Sylvester Scott and Vincent Owens. They emerged as rivals to the Crips and are involved in drug trafficking, robbery, extortion, and murder. The gang remains active and influential in Los Angeles street gang culture.

Piserà 'ndrina.description: The Piserà 'ndrina is a clan of the 'Ndrangheta, a criminal organization based in Tropea, Calabria, Italy. Active since the 1980s, it is allied with the Mancuso 'ndrina and has been in a feud with the La Rosa 'ndrina since the 1990s. The clan has been involved in violence, including the killing of municipal councilor Pasquale Piserà in 1982.

Pissed Off Bastards of Bloomington.description: An outlaw motorcycle club founded in Bloomington, California in 1945 by Norman Briggs. The club participated in the 1947 Hollister riot, which inspired the film The Wild One. It is considered a precursor to the Hells Angels, as a former member founded that club. The club remains active in California, Nevada, and Utah.

Pittsburgh crime family.description: The Pittsburgh crime family, also known as the LaRocca crime family, was an Italian American Mafia crime family based in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Formed in the late 1880s under Salvatore Catanzaro, it rose to prominence during Prohibition and was led for decades by Sebastian LaRocca. The family engaged in racketeering, labor union infiltration, and drug trafficking, but became defunct after convictions and attrition, with the last known member dying in 2021.

country_links.context: The Pittsburgh crime family partnered with the Trafficante crime family to manage the Sans Souci casino in Havana.

Playboys (gang).description: American street gang founded in Los Angeles County, California in the mid-1950s, originally a car club. It has multiple cliques and is predominantly Hispanic, with an estimated 6,500 members. The gang is aligned with the Mexican Mafia (La EME) and engages in drug trafficking, assault, robbery, and other criminal activities. It remains active across several U.S. states and Mexico.

country_links.context: The Playboys gang has territory in Mexico.

Plug Uglies.description: The Plug Uglies were an American Nativist criminal street gang active in Baltimore, Maryland from 1854 to 1865. They were known for their involvement in election-day violence and street brawls, often using plug hats stuffed with wool as helmets. The gang participated in the 1856 Baltimore Know-Nothing Riot and the 1863 New York City Draft Riots. They were allied with the Know Nothing political party and rivaled Irish American gangs.

Polverino clan.description: The Polverino clan is a Neapolitan Camorra clan based in Marano di Napoli, Italy, founded by Giuseppe Polverino in the 1990s. It emerged as a ramification of the Nuvoletta clan and became independent, known for monopolizing hashish importation from Morocco to Italy via Spain. The clan operates in various Italian regions and has a strong presence in Spain, particularly in Barcelona, Málaga, and Alicante. It is considered one of the most powerful Camorra groups in Spain.

Popeye Moto Club.description: French-Canadian outlaw motorcycle club and criminal organization based in Quebec, founded in 1965 by Michel Langlois, Roger Calve, Yvon Bilodeau, and others. At their peak, they were the second-largest biker gang in Canada, known for drug trafficking, extortion, and violence. In 1977, they were absorbed by the Hells Angels and became the first Canadian Hells Angels charter.

It is the second-largest faction in the Palestine Liberation Organization, opposing Fatah's moderate stance and advocating a one-state solution. The group pioneered aircraft hijackings in the late 1960s and early 1970s and has been designated a terrorist organization by several countries. Its military wing is the Abu Ali Mustafa Brigades.

They terrorized the neighborhood and dominated Lower West Side Manhattan until the end of the 1890s, when they were displaced by the Hudson Dusters.

Primeiro Comando da Capital.description: Brazilian organized crime syndicate founded in 1993 by eight prisoners at Taubaté Penitentiary. Based in São Paulo, it is Latin America's largest drug gang with 40,000 lifetime members and 60,000 contractors. Active throughout South America, West Africa, and Europe, it controls over 50% of Brazil's drug exports to Europe and has a partnership with the 'Ndrangheta. Pruszków mafia.description: The Pruszków mafia was a Polish criminal organization originating from Pruszków in the 1990s, active in the Warsaw area. It engaged in car theft, drug trafficking, kidnapping, extortion, weapon trafficking, and murder. Law enforcement dealt a severe blow in 2000 after a key member became a crown witness, and the group has not been significantly active since.

Public Enemy No. 1.description: Public Enemy No. 1 (PEN1) is a street gang with prison presence formed in Long Beach, California, in the 1980s. Based in Orange County, it engages in identity theft, credit card fraud, and methamphetamine trafficking. The gang has ties to the Aryan Brotherhood and Nazi Lowriders. As of 2004, it had around 200 members statewide, with an estimated 400-500 members currently.

Puccio family.description: The Puccio family was an Argentine criminal family active in the early 1980s, based in San Isidro, Buenos Aires. The family, led by father Arquímedes Puccio, was convicted of four kidnappings and three murders. They targeted wealthy individuals for ransom, often killing victims despite payment. The family was arrested in 1985 after a police raid freed their last victim.

Pueblos Unidos.description: Mexican criminal group active in Michoacán, founded in 2021 as a self-defense group for avocado farmers but degenerated into a criminal racketeering organization. Possibly tied to La Resistencia. Led by José Artemio Maldonado, a major fuel thief involved in the Tula prison break.

Puente 13.description: Puente 13 is a Sureño street gang based in La Puente, California, founded around 1953 as the Bridgetown Gentlemen. It is affiliated with the Mexican Mafia and known for drug trafficking, fraud, murder, and assault. The gang claims the entire city of La Puente and operates in the San Gabriel Valley.

Puro Tango Blast.description: Puro Tango Blast is a loose affiliation of regionally based street and prison gangs of primarily Hispanic men from major Texas cities. Formed in the late 1980s within the Texas Department of Criminal Justice, it lacks a strict hierarchy and is classified as a security threat group. Members engage in drug trafficking, robbery, and other crimes. The organization remains active with an estimated 17,000–19,000 members.

Purple Gang.description: The Purple Gang was a Jewish-American criminal mob based in Detroit, Michigan, during the Prohibition era. They engaged in bootlegging, hijacking, extortion, and murder, becoming Detroit's dominant criminal gang in the 1920s. The gang was led by the Bernstein brothers and was known for its violence. Internal strife and infighting led to its collapse in the early 1930s.

country_links.evidence_quote: the Purple Gang enlisted “The Little Jewish Navy” to carry alcohol over the Detroit River from Canada before selling it themselves.
country_links.context: The Purple Gang enlisted 'The Little Jewish Navy' to carry alcohol over the Detroit River from Canada.

Quality Street Gang.description: The Quality Street Gang operated in Manchester, England, in the 1960s, 1970s and 1980s. Some senior police officers considered them instigators of major crime, but others maintain they were merely a social friendship group. No member was ever arrested or convicted, leading to doubts about their criminal nature. The group was named after a TV advertisement for Quality Street confectionery.

country_links.evidence_quote: carried out armed robberies together in Holland.
country_links.context: Members of the Quality Street Gang carried out armed robberies together with the Inter City Jibbers in Holland.

Ramacca Mafia family.description: The Ramacca Mafia family is a crime family of the Sicilian Cosa Nostra, operating primarily in the town of Ramacca, Sicily. Founded in the 1950s by Calogero 'Liddu' Conti, it engages in extortion, infiltration of public contracts, and political influence. The family has maintained control over local economic interests and alliances with powerful neighboring families. It remains active, with recent leadership transitions and ongoing criminal operations.

Ramashish Koeri gang.description: The Ramashish Koeri gang was a caste-based dacoit band active in the Kaimur plateau region of Bihar, India, during the 1980s. Led by Ramashish Koeri after the death of previous leader Mohan Bind, the gang was responsible for over a hundred murders in the region. It emerged from a context of extreme poverty and feudal repression by Rajput landlords, with members from Scheduled Castes and backward castes. The gang's activities declined after the death of Ramashish Koeri, but it was succeeded by leaders like Kameswar Koeri.

Rapid Support Forces.description: Sudanese paramilitary force originating from the Janjaweed militias used in the Darfur conflict. Formed in August 2013 under Muhammad Dagalo (Hemedti). Fights the Sudanese Armed Forces in a civil war since 2023, establishing a parallel government in 2025. Accused of war crimes, genocide, and human rights abuses.

country_links.evidence_quote: In June 2023, the UAE set a field hospital in Amdjarass, Chad with the stated goal of assisting Sudanese refugees. According to African officials, the hospital was treating wounded Rapid Support Forces fighters.
country_links.context: The RSF receives weapons and medical treatment for its fighters in Chad, and uses it as a base for attacks.

country_links.evidence_quote: In February 2025, RSF and its allies signed a charter in Nairobi, Kenya, to form a parallel " Government of Peace and Unity "

country_links.context: The RSF uses Libya as a supply line, procuring vehicles, oil, and weapons there, and its troops have entered and cooperated with Libyan forces.

country_links.evidence_quote: Gold mined in Sudan was sold and sent to Dubai in the United Arab Emirates, where RSF leader Hemedti kept most of his money... country_links.context: The RSF buys vehicles from UAE dealers, sends gold to Dubai, receives weapons and financial support from the UAE, and its fighters are treated in UAE hospitals.

Rasta City.description: Rasta City is a gang based in Trinidad and Tobago, originally formed after a split from Muslim City. It is currently led by 'Prezzi' and is involved in ongoing conflicts with rival gangs including Sixx and ABG. The gang has been active in gangland violence, with its former leader Akini 'Dole' Adams killed in a police raid in 2019. A peace deal with Sixx in 2023 was short-lived.

Rathkeale Rovers.description: The Rathkeale Rovers are a criminal group based in Ireland but operating internationally, composed of members of Ireland's Travelling Community. They engage in fraud, money laundering, drug smuggling, and art theft, notably stealing rhino horns and Chinese antiquities from museums. The group originated with Simon Quilligan and was later led by the O'Brien family. Europol and US authorities have investigated them, leading to multiple arrests.

country_links.evidence_quote: In October 2013, the New South Wales Fair Trading department issued a warning that the gang was operating on the Australian eastern seaboard.

country_links.context: The Rathkeale Rovers carried out museum thefts in the UK and had members still at large there.

Real Calton Tongs.description: A violent Scottish teenage gang active in the Calton area of Glasgow during the 1960s. The gang financed itself through a protection racket and marked its territory with the slogan 'Tongs Ya Bass'. The area they controlled was nicknamed Tongland.

Real Irish Republican Army.description: Dissident Irish republican paramilitary group formed in 1997 after a split from the Provisional IRA, aiming to create a united Ireland. It waged a campaign in Northern Ireland against British security forces and carried out bombings, most notably the 1998 Omagh bombing. Red Army (football firm).description: The Red Army is a hooligan firm associated with English football club Manchester United. Founded in the 1970s, it became one of the largest firms in British football, known for causing mayhem at away matches. The firm includes criminal sub-divisions involved in drug smuggling, armed robberies, and theft. Its activities have declined since the late 1980s.

Red Brigades.description: Italian far-left Marxist-Leninist militant group formed in 1970, seeking a revolutionary state through armed struggle. Responsible for numerous violent attacks during Italy's Years of Lead, including the kidnapping and murder of former prime minister Aldo Moro in 1978. The group was broken up in the 1980s but saw a resurgence in the late 1990s to 2000s.

Richardson Gang.description: The Richardson Gang was an English crime gang based in South London in the 1960s, known for extreme violence and torture. Founded by brothers Charlie and Eddie Richardson, they engaged in racketeering, narcotics, extortion, and other crimes. Their reputation for sadistic methods earned them the nickname 'Torture Gang'. The gang was eventually dismantled in the late 1960s.

Rinaldi clan.description: The Rinaldi clan is a Camorra clan based in San Giovanni a Teduccio, Naples, founded in 1989 after splitting from the Mazzarella clan. It is involved in murder, extortion, drug trafficking, racketeering, and counterfeiting. Since 2019, it has formed a powerful alliance with the De Luca Bossa and Aprea-Cuccaro clans, dominating eastern Naples. The clan is allied with the Secondigliano Alliance and remains active.

Rizzuto crime family.description: Italian Canadian crime family based in Montreal, Quebec, founded in the 1970s by Nicolo Rizzuto. It overtook the Cotroni crime family to become the preeminent Mafia organization in Montreal. The family is involved in racketeering, drug trafficking, illegal gambling, and murder. It is considered by the FBI as a faction of the Bonanno crime family, but recognized as independent by Canadian authorities.

Active until 2001, it served as a recruitment tool and enforcement arm for the Hells Angels during the Quebec Biker War, carrying out intimidation, assaults, and assassinations to control the illegal drug trade.

Rockford crime family.description: The Rockford crime family was an Italian American Mafia crime family based in Rockford, Illinois, founded around 1920 by Antonio Musso. It operated independently from the nearby Chicago Outfit, engaging in racketeering, gambling, loan sharking, and murder. The family was led by Joseph Zammuto from 1957 to 1974, then by Frank Buscemi until its decline in the early 2000s.

Rocks Push.description: A notorious larrikin gang that dominated The Rocks area of Sydney from the 1870s to the 1890s. Engaged in theft, murder, assault, and robbery, often using female members to lure victims. Leaders were determined through bare-knuckle boxing matches. Known for a distinctive dress style to appear unarmed while concealing razor blades.

ROD Gang.description: A small murderous drug ring that operated in New Orleans, primarily in the St. Roch neighborhood. Formed among teens in trailers after Hurricane Katrina, the gang sold crack, marijuana, and heroin from 2007 to 2013. Twelve members were indicted on murder and racketeering charges in 2013.

Rollin' 30s Harlem Crips.description: The Rollin' 30s Harlem Crips are a set of the Crips street gang alliance, formed by Belizean American Crips who moved from South Los Angeles to Belize and then to Harlem, New York. The gang is involved in drug trafficking, weapon trafficking, prostitution, murder, and robbery. It was established in New York City in the late 1980s or early 1990s by Dalmin "Diamond" Mayen and his associates. The gang remains active in Los Angeles, New York City, and Belize City.

Rollin' 60s Neighborhood Crips.description: The Rollin' 60s Neighborhood Crips is a set of the Crips street gang alliance based in Los Angeles, California, founded in 1976 from the Westside Crips. It is one of the largest gangs in the Los Angeles area with an estimated 1,600 members. The gang is involved in racketeering, murder, drug trafficking, and other crimes, and has spread to other U.S. cities.

Rollin' 90s Neighborhood Crips.description: The Rollin' 90s Neighborhood Crips are a set of the larger Crips gang alliance, based on the west side of South Los Angeles, California. Formed in the late 1970s or early 1980s, they are primarily African-American and engage in drug trafficking and murder. The gang has expanded to other U.S. cities and Canada, with a notable presence in Nashville and Montreal.

Romanian Constitutional Bar.description: A parallel, illegal bar association in Romania, established by Pompiliu Bota in 2002, lacking legal personality. It allowed unauthorized persons to practice law, violating Romanian criminal codes. The organization was never legally recognized and operated as a criminal group.

Rudaj Organization.description: The Rudaj Organization was an Albanian-American gang active in the New York City metro area, founded in 1993 by Alex Rudaj and Nardino Colotti. It engaged in extortion, illegal gambling, and murder, operating in Queens, The Bronx, and Westchester County. The organization was dismantled after a 2004 federal indictment that charged 22 members.

Ryno-Skachevsky gang.description: Russian racist serial killer group composed of young men, active in the 2000s, headed by Artur Ryno and Pavel Skachevsky. The gang targeted and murdered immigrants from the Caucasus and Central Asia in Moscow. Members were convicted in 2008 for multiple murders and hate crimes.

Sabaot Land Defence Force.description: The Sabaot Land Defence Force (SLDF) was a guerrilla militia operating in the Mount Elgon District of Kenya from 2005 to 2008. It drew members from the Sabaot people and was accused of killing over 600 people, committing atrocities such as murder, torture, and rape, and displacing more than 66,000 people. The group was led by Wycliffe Matakwei Komon and had a clear organizational structure with political, spiritual, and military wings. It was funded through unofficial taxation of local residents.

Sacra Corona Unita.description: Sacra Corona Unita is a Mafia-type criminal organization from the Apulia region in Southern Italy, founded in the early 1980s by Pino Rogoli. It is active in areas such as Brindisi, Lecce, and Taranto, and engages in cigarette smuggling, arms trafficking, drug trafficking, human trafficking, money laundering, extortion, and political corruption. The group was formed to counter the power of other mafia organizations in prisons and Apulian territory. After arrests and defections in the early 2000s, it no longer exists as a single viable organization.

country_links.evidence_quote: The organization has long been present in Albania, partly because of the proximity of Apulia and Albania and the diffusion of the Italian language. Albania is a point of arrival for huge quantities of smuggled cigarettes and drugs from Afghanistan.
country_links.context: The organization has long been present in Albania, using it as a point of arrival for smuggled cigarettes and drugs.

Sakaume-gumi.description: The Sakaume-gumi is a yakuza organization based in Osaka, Japan, founded by Umekichi Tobi. It is a small, old-established group focusing primarily on gambling, with relatively good relations with local police. It was registered as a designated yakuza group under the Organized Crime Countermeasures Law in May 1993.

Salakau.description: Salakau is a secret society and gang based in Singapore, founded in the early 1970s. The name means 'three six nine' in Hokkien, referencing the Eighteen Arhats. They are involved in drug trafficking, extortion, prostitution, and white-collar crime. The gang has a history of violent turf wars and has been targeted by the Singapore Police Force's Secret Societies Branch.

Sam Gor.description: Sam Gor is an international crime syndicate based in Asia-Pacific, primarily involved in drug trafficking. It is made up of members from five triads and is headed by Chinese-Canadian Tse Chi Lop, who was arrested in 2021. The group controls an estimated 40-70% of the Asia-Pacific methamphetamine market and earns at least $8 billion per year. It is believed to manufacture meth in the Golden Triangle region of Myanmar.

The family was involved in racketeering, gambling, loansharking, extortion, narcotics trafficking, and other illegal activities. Its membership peaked at 15-20 made men under boss James 'Jimmy the Hat' Lanza. The family was active from around 1928 until 2006.

Sangre Nueva Zeta.description: Mexican criminal syndicate formed in 2019 by former members of Los Zetas, founded by Roberto de los Santos de Jesús. Initially focused on fuel theft in Puebla's 'Red Triangle', it expanded into cocaine trafficking and extortion. The group allied with the Jalisco New Generation Cartel and is still active.

Santa.description: The Santa (or Società maggiore) is a high-level criminal organization within the 'Ndrangheta, founded in the mid-1970s. Members, called santisti, can interact with non-members including police, politicians, and Freemasons. The group has its own rituals and hierarchy, with a maximum of 33 members originally, later expanded. It is considered one of the highest ranks in the Calabrian mafia.

Santa Cruz Cartel.description: Bolivian drug cartel headquartered in Santa Cruz de la Sierra, one of the largest in the country. Active since the 1980s, it has been involved in narco-terrorist incidents including assassination attempts on DEA agents and bombings. Allied with Colombian, Brazilian, and Mexican trafficking organizations, it engages in turf wars with smaller gangs.

Santa Monica 13.description: Mexican-American street gang based in Santa Monica, California, founded in the late 1920s as the Santa Monica Tomato Patch Gang. They are a Sureño gang known for violence, drug trafficking, and other criminal activities. The gang's primary clique is Santa Monica 17th Street (SM17). They have been allied with the Mexican Mafia and Sureños.

Sarasota Assassination Society.description: A late 19th-century secret organization in Manatee County, Florida, founded in 1884 by Alfred Bidwell, Leonard Andrews, and Jason Alford. Composed of 20-22 former Confederate soldiers, it engaged in murder of political opponents, blackmail, and political intimidation. The group was responsible for the murders of Charles E. Abbe and Harrison T. Riley, leading to indictments and trials of its members. It was active from 1884 to 1892.

Satan's Choice Motorcycle Club.description: Canadian outlaw motorcycle club founded in 1965 in Oshawa, Ontario. It was the second largest outlaw motorcycle club in the world by 1970 with over 400 members. The club was involved in the first major outlaw biker conflict in Canadian history against the Popeyes from 1974 to 1976. It disbanded in 2000 when most chapters joined the Hells Angels, was briefly reactivated in 2017 and again in 2025.

Savage Nomads.description: The Savage Nomads were a mostly Puerto Rican and African American street gang founded in the South Bronx, New York City in 1970 by Benjamin Melendez. Active primarily in the 1970s, the gang engaged in small crimes and battles with rival gangs such as the Seven Immortals and Savage Skulls. After a period of dormancy, the gang resurfaced in 2017 with homicides linked to them.

Savage Skulls.description: The Savage Skulls are a mostly Puerto Rican and African American street gang founded in the Hunts Point area of the Bronx, New York, in the late 1960s. They gained popularity in the 1970s and declared war on drug dealers in Hunts Point. The gang was involved in conflicts with rival gangs and appropriated Nazi symbolism. They were featured in a 1979 documentary film.

Scarface gang.description: The Scarface gang was a criminal gang possibly from the Netherlands, active in the 2000s and early 2010s. It consisted of two to six men and sometimes a woman, responsible for a series of violent armed robberies in Belgium, the Netherlands, Germany, and France. The gang was named after the character Tony Montana from the film Scarface. Four members were arrested in December 2011, while two fled to Morocco and one disappeared.
