Scattered Spider.description: Scattered Spider is a hacking group mostly composed of teens and young adults from the United States and the United Kingdom, believed to be affiliated with the cybercriminal network 'The Com'. Founded around May 2022, the group gained notoriety for hacking and extorting Caesars Entertainment and MGM Resorts International in 2023. They have also targeted numerous other companies including Visa, Marks & Spencer, and Snowflake cloud storage customers. The group uses social engineering, SIM swapping, and multi-factor authentication fatigue attacks.

Sex Money Murder.description: Sex Money Murder is a set of the Bloods street gang operating on the East Coast of the United States, founded in the Soundview section of the Bronx, New York, on September 27, 1995, by Peter "Pistol Pete" Rollock. Originally a subset of the United Blood Nation, it later gained independence and is involved in drug trafficking, racketeering, armed robbery, assault, and murder. The gang has spread to the southern United States, particularly North Carolina and Georgia.

ShadowCrew.description: ShadowCrew was a cybercrime forum operating from 2002 to 2004, founded by Brett Johnson, Seth Sanders, and Kim Marvin Taylor. It facilitated credit card fraud, hacking, and other illegal activities, with around 4,000 members. The site was infiltrated by the US Secret Service through informant Albert Gonzalez, leading to its shutdown.

Shapiro Brothers.description: The Shapiro Brothers were a group of Jewish-American mobsters from New York City, based in Williamsburg, who led a faction in the garment industry. They were involved in a violent conflict with Jacob Shapiro and Louis Buchalter for control of the industry in Brooklyn. All three brothers were killed by rivals between 1931 and 1934.

Shiners.description: Gangs of Irish immigrants active in Bytown (later Ottawa) during the 1830s. Formed after the Rideau Canal's completion left many Irish unemployed, they used intimidation and violence to create jobs, sparking the Shiners' War. Engaged in street fights, robbery, and murder until armed patrols suppressed them in 1837.

Shining Path.description: Far-left political party and guerrilla group in Peru, founded in 1969 by Abimael Guzmán. It launched a 'people's war' in 1980 aiming to overthrow the government and establish a New Democracy through guerrilla warfare. The group is designated as a terrorist organization by Peru, the US, EU, Japan, and Canada. Since the capture of its leaders in the 1990s and 2012, its activity has declined, with remaining factions operating in the VRAEM region.

Shinwa-kai.description: The Shinwa-kai is a yakuza group based in Takamatsu, Kagawa, Japan, with an estimated 30 active members. It was renamed from the Takamatsu Shinwa-kai in 1971 and registered as a designated yakuza group in December 1992. It is the only designated yakuza group based in the Shikoku region and has been a member of the anti-Yamaguchi federation Gosha-kai since 1996.

Shirt Tails.description: The Shirt Tails were a mid-19th-century street gang based in the Five Points slum in Manhattan, New York City. They wore their shirts outside their pants as insignia and concealed weapons beneath. Active from the 1830s to the 1860s, they participated in the New York Draft Riots and disappeared shortly before the American Civil War.

Shower Posse.description: The Shower Posse is a Jamaican gang founded around 1981 by Lester Lloyd Coke and Vivian Blake, based in Tivoli Gardens, Kingston. It is involved in drug and arms smuggling, with branches in North America and the United Kingdom. The gang has ties to the Jamaica Labour Party and has been linked to CIA support. It remains active in drug trafficking, firearms trafficking, and other criminal activities.

It operates in Hong Kong, Macau, and Chinese communities abroad, engaging in extortion, loan sharking, narcotics, and control of nightclubs and gambling dens. It is the largest criminal group in the state, involved in drug trafficking, murders, robberies, extortion, and prison rebellions. Created as a reaction to the control of the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC), it has been in conflict with the PCC and other rival factions. The group remains active.

Sio Sam Ong.description: Sio Sam Ong is a leading Chinese triad in Malaysia, based in Penang and Selangor, with strong presence in northern states like Kedah and Perlis. Established in the 1940s-1950s, it is considered one of the most powerful triads in the country, primarily composed of Hokkien ethnic group. The organization is involved in international drug trafficking, kidnapping, murder, extortion, racketeering, and loansharking, and has been linked to multiple murders in Penang in the late 1980s and early 1990s.

Slaughter House Gang.description: A prominent street gang in New York's Fourth Ward during the late 1880s to the mid-1990s, known for violent muggings and murder. They lured victims into dive bars or used a bucket of ash to blind them before robbing and sometimes killing them. The gang was led by George Leese, a river pirate and illegal prize fight organizer. They dominated the Fourth Ward until police drove them out after the American Civil War.

Soai-kai.description: The Soai-kai is a yakuza organization based in Chiba, Japan, formed in 1945 by Toramatsu Takahashi. Originally an affiliate of the Sasada-ikka, it became independent in 1955. It is a designated yakuza group with an estimated 80 active members and is one of the three dominating yakuza groups in Chiba Prefecture.

Società di Polistena.description: The Società di Polistena is a 'ndrangheta criminal organization based in Polistena, Calabria, Italy, with influence in surrounding towns. It has been active since the late 19th century, with early recorded bosses including Pasquale Ferrara and Francesco Sergio. The group engaged in drug and arms trafficking, and was involved in reconstruction profiteering after the 1905 earthquake. It remains active, with historical ties to the Guerrisi and Mercuri families.

Società foggiana.description: The Società foggiana is a mafia-type criminal cartel operating in Foggia and its province, with infiltrations in other Italian regions. It emerged in the early 1980s as a splinter of Raffaele Cutolo's Nuova Camorra Organizzata and gained recognition in 1994. Known for its brutality, it lacks a single leader but is organized into family-based 'batteries' with a federal structure. It is considered one of the most violent Italian mafias.

Soldiers of Aryan Culture.description: A large white supremacist prison gang in the United States, founded in 1997 by Tracy David 'Tinman' Swena in Utah. The gang operates both inside and outside prison walls, engaging in drug trafficking, extortion, and violence. It has a paramilitary ranking structure and requires members to attack sex offenders and informants. The SAC has expanded across multiple states and the federal prison system.

Solid Wood Soldiers.description: Neo-Nazi prison gang and organized crime syndicate based in Texas, founded in 1990 at Snake River Correctional Institution in Oregon. Known for drug trafficking, assault, murder, and racketeering, with strong ties to other white supremacist groups. Uses distinctive tattoos and symbols, including the number four representing honor, courage, respect, and loyalty.

Solntsevskaya Bratva.description: Russian crime syndicate founded in the late 1980s in the Solntsevo District of Moscow by Sergei Mikhailov and Viktor Averin. It controls transport hubs and engages in racketeering, drug trafficking, money laundering, and other crimes. The group has expanded internationally and maintains alliances with various criminal organizations.

Solo Angeles.description: An outlaw motorcycle club formed in Tijuana, Mexico in 1959. The club's insignia is a chopper-style motorcycle. It conducts an annual charity run delivering toys to poor children in Tijuana.

Somali Outlaws.description: The Somali Outlaws are a Somali American street gang based in the Minneapolis–Saint Paul metropolitan area, active since the 2000s. The gang operates primarily around the Karmel Mall in south Minneapolis and the Cedar-Riverside neighborhood, with additional territory in Saint Paul and Nashville. Their activities include drug trafficking and human trafficking. The gang's leader, Mustafa Ali, was killed in 2019.

Sombra Negra.description: Death squad based in El Salvador, composed mainly of police and military personnel acting as vigilantes targeting criminals and gang members. Active since around December 1994, it was dismantled in 1996 but resurfaced in 2014. Known for targeting Mara Salvatrucha and Mara 18 gangs, often leaving victims blindfolded and shot in the head.

Sonora Cartel.description: The Sonora Cartel was a Mexican drug trafficking organization founded in 1987 by Miguel Caro Quintero and Rafael Caro Quintero, operating primarily in northern Mexico and the southwestern United States. It was considered one of the oldest and best-established cartels by the DEA, with direct links to Colombian cartels. The cartel was acquired by the Sinaloa Cartel by 2007 and reported defunct by 2010.

country_links.evidence_quote: The Sonora Cartel is believed to be one of the earliest cartels to begin shipping cocaine from Colombia, particularly from the Cali Cartel .

Sons of Samoa.description: Crips-affiliated street gang based in Long Beach, California, founded by the 1980s. Membership primarily consists of Samoan Americans and other Pacific Islanders. Involved in drug trafficking, robbery, burglary, and extortion. Operates in multiple U.S. states including Alaska, California, Missouri, Utah, and Washington.

Sons of Satan Motorcycle Club.description: One percenter outlaw motorcycle club based in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, founded in 1949 by returning WWII veterans. Originally a family-oriented club, it became a violent gang under John 'Satan' Marron, who later became National President of the Pagan's Motorcycle Club. The club is a brother club to the Pagans and wears a diamond 'P' patch to signify allegiance. Its clubhouse was destroyed by a pipe bomb in 2002, suspected to be by Hells Angels.

Sons of Silence.description: International outlaw motorcycle club founded in Niwot, Colorado in 1966 by Bruce Gale Richardson. Designated a criminal organization by the U.S. Department of Justice. Has over 250 members with 35 chapters in 12 U.S. states and Germany. Sixth-largest motorcycle club worldwide.

They are primarily African-American and known for their involvement in the murder of Tupac Shakur in 1996. The gang operated numerous drug houses during the crack epidemic and has ongoing rivalries with various Piru and Crips sets.

Spanish Cobras.description: The Spanish Cobras is a primarily Latino street gang founded in the 1970s in Chicago, Illinois, by former members of the Maniac Latin Disciples. It operates in multiple Midwestern states and has a strong presence on Chicago's north and west sides. The gang is part of the Folk Nation alliance and is known for its rivalry with People Nation gangs, including the Latin Kings.

Spanish Gangster Disciples.description: The Spanish Gangster Disciples is an Indigenous Latino American street gang originating in South Chicago, founded by Rudy Rios in the early 1980s. It is an offshoot of the Gangster Disciples and is part of the Folk Nation alliance. The gang is involved in drug trafficking, assault, robbery, and murder, and remains active.

Spook Hunters.description: White racist youth gang based in South Gate, California, active from the 1940s to the 1950s. Formed in reaction to the growing African American population in Los Angeles, the gang opposed integration and racial segregation, starting fights and intimidating black youths. Their activities prompted the formation of black protective gangs such as the Slausons.

St. Louis crime family.description: The St. Louis crime family was an Italian-American Mafia crime family based in St. Louis, Missouri, founded around the 1890s. It was involved in racketeering, gambling, drug trafficking, and other illegal activities. The family was active until approximately 2014, with ties to other Mafia families such as the Chicago Outfit and Detroit Partnership.

State Line Mob.description: The State Line Mob was an association of criminal elements operating in the 1950s and 1960s along the Mississippi–Tennessee state line. Involved in bootlegging, gambling, prostitution, robbery, and murder, it owned motels, restaurants, and clubs that served as centers for vice. The group gained national attention for its feud with Sheriff Buford Pusser, which inspired the film Walking Tall.

Stidda.description: The Stidda is a Sicilian Mafia-type criminal organization based in southern Sicily, founded in the early 1980s by former Cosa Nostra members expelled during the Second Mafia War. It operates primarily in rural areas and is known for its star tattoo. The Stidda engaged in a violent conflict with Cosa Nostra in the 1990s, resulting in over 300 deaths. It remains active, with an estimated 2,000 full members.

Stopwatch Gang.description: The Stopwatch Gang was a group of three Canadian bank robbers active from 1974 to 1980. They robbed over 140 banks in the United States and Canada, stealing approximately $15 million Canadian dollars. Known for meticulous planning and non-violent methods, they completed robberies in under two minutes. The gang was named by the FBI after a member wore a stopwatch during a heist.

Straight Satans Motorcycle Club.description: The Straight Satans Motorcycle Club was a one-percenter outlaw motorcycle gang based in Southern California, founded in July 1959 by three bikers known as Father Bill, Little Jerry, and Glick. It was among the earliest outlaw motorcycle clubs in the Los Angeles area, but remained localized without chapters beyond its original base. The club gained notoriety for its association with the Manson Family during the late 1960s, particularly around the Tate–LaBianca murders. It was implicated in criminal incidents including a sexual assault in 1972.

Strisciuglio clan.description: The Strisciuglio clan is a powerful and violent criminal organization based in Bari, Italy, founded in the late 1990s by Domenico Strisciuglio. It operates primarily in the northern area of Bari, engaging in murder, drug trafficking, money laundering, extortion, usury, and gambling. The clan has close ties with local politics and is currently active.

Suishin-kai.description: The Suishin-kai was a Japanese yakuza gang based in Nagasaki, affiliated with the Yamaguchi-gumi. It came to prominence in April 2007 when its former underboss, Tetsuya Shiroo, assassinated the mayor of Nagasaki, Iccho Itoh. The gang voluntarily disbanded shortly after the killing due to intense police scrutiny.

Sumiyoshi-kai.description: The Sumiyoshi-kai is the second-largest yakuza group in Japan, based in Tokyo. Founded in 1958 by Jusaku Abe, it operates as a confederation of smaller gangs with a loose chain of command. The group engages in protection rackets in upscale districts like Kabukichō and Ginza. As of 2020, it had an estimated 2,100 members.

Sun Yee On.description: Sun Yee On is one of the leading triads in Hong Kong and China, founded in 1919 by Heung Chin. It has over 25,000 members worldwide and is active in multiple countries including the UK, US, France, and Belgium. The triad is involved in racketeering, counterfeiting, extortion, drug trafficking, money laundering, murder, and illegal gambling. It remains active as of the present day.

Supreme Eiye Confraternity.description: The Supreme Eiye Confraternity (SEC) is a Nigerian confraternity founded in 1965 at the University of Ibadan. Originally a student group, it has evolved into a criminal organization involved in drug trafficking, passport forgery, money laundering, and sex trafficking. It operates internationally with cells called 'forums' and is outlawed under Nigerian law.

country_links.evidence_quote: In 2014, Italian police concluded an investigation into the SEC. They found that the group, along with the Black Axe, had been active in Italy since at least 2008, and had established an organized criminal network with connections in other European countries which was directly involved in trafficking of women from rural Nigeria into Europe.

Supreme Team.description: Organized crime syndicate based in South Jamaica, Queens, New York City, founded in 1981 by Kenneth 'Supreme' McGriff and his nephew Gerald 'Prince' Miller. Specialized in crack cocaine distribution, generating over $200,000 daily at its 1987 peak. Known for extreme violence and murder to control drug trade. Leaders were convicted and sentenced to life in prison.

Swamp Angels.description: The Swamp Angels were a New York City waterfront street gang active from the 1850s to the 1890s. Based in a rookery called Gotham Court on Cherry Street in Lower Manhattan, they used the sewers to raid East River dockyards and sell stolen cargo quickly. The gang was predominantly Irish and Irish-American. They eventually merged with rival gangs to form the White Hand Gang.

Sword Boys.description: Street gang in Perth, Western Australia, consisting mostly of Lebanese Australians, known to authorities since the mid-1990s. Members wear a miniature gold scimitar necklace. Involved in amphetamine and ecstasy distribution, and linked to car rebirthing. Members were convicted in 2016 for drug trafficking.

Sydney Ducks.description: The Sydney Ducks was a gang of criminal immigrants from Australia operating in San Francisco during the mid-19th century. They were blamed for an 1849 fire and rampant crime, leading to the formation of the first Committee of Vigilance in 1851. The vigilantes decimated the gang through lynchings and deportations. The area they clustered in became known as the Barbary Coast.

Södertälje mafia.description: Syriac-Aramean criminal organization based in Södertälje, Sweden, founded in the early 1980s. It is structured around family and kinship ties, with no single leader. The group is involved in drug trafficking, murder, welfare fraud, extortion, and other crimes. It has been confirmed by Swedish courts and continues to grow.

Taishu-kai.description: The Taishu-kai is a yakuza organization based in Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan, with an estimated 60 active members. It was formed around 1954 by Kuniharu Ota as the Ota Group, later renamed Ota-gumi, and finally Taishu-kai in 1973. It is one of five independent Fukuoka-based designated yakuza syndicates and a member of the anti-Yamaguchi-gumi federation Yonsha-kai.

mentioned_in.title: History of Libya under Muammar Gaddafi

Takumi-gumi.description: The Takumi-gumi is a Japanese yakuza syndicate based in the Kansai region, founded in 1967 by Masaru Takumi. It was originally part of the Yamaguchi-gumi, with Takumi serving as second-in-command. After Takumi's assassination in 1997, Tadashi Irie became the leader. The group withdrew from the Yamaguchi-gumi in 2015 to form the Kobe Yamaguchi-gumi, and later left that group in 2022. By 2023, membership had dwindled to about 20 members.

Taliban.description: The Taliban is an Afghan political and militant organization that emerged in 1994 during the Second Afghan Civil War. Founded by Mullah Omar, it ruled most of Afghanistan from 1996 to 2001, enforcing a strict interpretation of sharia law. Overthrown by a US-led invasion in 2001, it waged a 20-year insurgency before recapturing Kabul in 2021 and now controls all of Afghanistan. The group is designated as a terrorist organization by several countries and is widely condemned for human rights abuses.

Tanglewood Boys.description: The Tanglewood Boys was an Italian-American recruitment gang or farm team for the Lucchese crime family, operating from the Tanglewood Shopping Center in Yonkers, New York. Active from the 1990s to the 2000s, the gang was involved in murders, assaults, armed robbery, arsons, and bookmaking in Westchester County, the Bronx, and the Upper West Side. Many members were sons of made men. The gang's downfall followed high-profile murders and subsequent prosecutions.

TAP Boyz.description: Arab American street gang formed in Chicago in 1992 to protect the Arab-American community from racially motivated assaults after the Gulf War. They disbanded in 1999 after losing members to rival gangs. Their colors were white and red, and their symbol was a four-pointed star.

Taylor Street Jousters.description: The Taylor Street Jousters were a Chicago street gang originating in Little Italy, Chicago, in the 1950s or 1960s. They were primarily Italian and Mexican, known for their medieval knight symbols. The gang was allied with the Chicago Outfit and Gaylords, and rivaled the Gangster Disciples, Latin Kings, and Simon City Royals. They were active until 2005.

Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan.description: Deobandi jihadist militant organization primarily operating along the Afghanistan-Pakistan border. Founded by Baitullah Mehsud in 2007, it seeks to overthrow the Pakistani government and establish an Islamic state. Known for suicide bombings, sectarian violence, and attacks on security forces. Designated as a terrorist group by the UN and several countries.

country_links.evidence_quote: The Pakistani Taliban have previously assisted the Afghan Taliban in the 2001–2021 war... The TTP depends on the tribal belt along the Afghanistan–Pakistan border... In 2019, there were around 3,000 to 4,000 TTP militants in Afghanistan...

Temple Street gang.description: Street gang based in downtown Los Angeles, founded by Filipino and Mexican youths in the 1920s-1930s. Involved in murders, assaults, burglaries, drug and gun trafficking. Colors are blue and black. Allies include Sureños and Mexican Mafia; rivals include Norteños and 18th Street gang.

Tenth Avenue Gang.description: New York City street gang formed by Ike Marsh in 1860, later becoming the city's first train robbers. The gang committed a notable train robbery in 1868, stealing $5,000 in cash and bonds. By the early 1870s, the gang merged with the Hell's Kitchen Gang after several members were killed by railroad detectives.

Terceiro Comando.description: Brazilian criminal faction based in Rio de Janeiro, founded in 1988 to oppose the Comando Vermelho. It was formed by Jorge Zambi (Pianinho) and other former members of the Falange Vermelha. The group was involved in drug trafficking, murders, and prison rebellions. It was dissolved in the early 2000s after a rebellion led by Comando Vermelho leader Fernandinho Beira-Mar killed its main leaders.

Terceiro Comando Puro.description: Brazilian criminal organization based in Rio de Janeiro, founded in 2002 as a dissident faction of the Terceiro Comando. It is the second largest criminal faction in Rio de Janeiro and the third in Brazil, involved in drug trafficking, robberies, and murders. The group maintains a rivalry with Comando Vermelho and has expanded operations to several other Brazilian states.

Texas Syndicate.description: The Texas Syndicate is a mostly Texas-based street and prison gang with predominantly Mexican American membership, founded in 1978 at Folsom State Prison in California. It was established for self-protection against other prison gangs and later engaged in drug trafficking, extortion, prostitution, gambling, and contract murder. The gang has approximately 1,300 members and maintains a paramilitary structure. It operates primarily in Texas but also in prisons across the United States.

country_links.evidence_quote: Gang members smuggle multikilogram-quantities of powdered cocaine, heroin, and methamphetamine, and multiton-quantities of marijuana from Mexico into the U.S. for distribution inside and outside prison.

country_links.context: The Texas Syndicate smuggles drugs from Mexico into the United States.

Texis Cartel.description: Salvadoran criminal organization specializing in drug trafficking, founded in the 1990s by José Adán Salazar Umaña, Juan Umaña Samayoa, and Roberto Herrera. It transported drugs from Colombia through northern El Salvador to North America, bribing law enforcement and officials. The cartel was dismantled by Salvadoran authorities in 2018.

Thak Thak gang.description: The Thak Thak gang is a criminal group active in North India, especially the National Capital Region. It specializes in targeting parked vehicles and using deceptive tactics to distract victims before stealing cash and valuables. The group frequently changes location to evade arrest.

The Americans (gang).description: The Americans is a large street gang and organized crime group based in the Cape Flats area of Cape Town, South Africa. Founded in 1983 by Neville Harold (Jackie Lonte), it is a corporate body for many smaller gangs and is aligned with the 26 and 27 prison number gangs. The gang is involved in drug trafficking, extortion, abalone poaching, and other criminal activities. It has an estimated 30,000 members and its headquarters is called The White House.

The Base.description: The Base is an international neo-Nazi organization and paramilitary training network formed in 2018 by Rinaldo Nazzaro. It advocates accelerationist and white nationalist ideology, aiming to establish white ethnostates through terrorism and violent overthrow of governments. The group operates training camps and has links to other far-right extremist groups. It is designated as a terrorist organization in several countries.

The Brotherhood of Eternal Love.description: The Brotherhood of Eternal Love was an organization of drug users and distributors operating from the mid-1960s through the late 1970s in Orange County, California. Founded by John Griggs, it produced and distributed LSD and hashish with the goal of sparking a 'psychedelic revolution' in the United States. The group was known for the 'Orange Sunshine' LSD tablets and assisted Timothy Leary's escape from prison. Its activities largely ended after a 1972 drug raid, though some members were arrested as late as 2009.

The Carlton Crew.description: The Carlton Crew is a criminal organization based in Melbourne, Australia, founded in the 1970s by Gino Rosace. It is named after the Melbourne suburb of Carlton and has been involved in racketeering, murder, drug trafficking, and other crimes. The group played a significant role in the Melbourne gangland killings and has been a rival to Calabrian 'Ndrangheta groups. As of 2019, Tony Madafferi is the boss.

The Commission.description: The governing body of the American Mafia, formed in 1931 by Charles 'Lucky' Luciano after the Castellammarese War. It consists of the bosses of the Five Families of New York City, the Chicago Outfit, and occasionally other families. The Commission oversees Mafia activities in the United States and mediates conflicts between families. It was involved in the Apalachin meeting, a 1963 murder plot, and the 1985 Mafia Commission Trial.

The Company.description: Organized crime syndicate based in Hawaii, founded in 1969 by Wilford Pulawa. Controlled criminal activities in Hawaii from the late 1960s to the mid-1990s, involved in illegal gambling, prostitution, racketeering, extortion, and drug trafficking. Extended influence to mainland US states including California and Nevada.

country_links.evidence_quote: the wide-scale illegal trade in Chinese white heroin
country_links.context: The Company engaged in the wide-scale illegal trade in Chinese white heroin, sourcing it from China.

The Council.description: African-American organized crime syndicate in New York City that controlled the heroin trade in Harlem during the 1970s. Formed by Nicky Barnes in 1972, the seven-man organization handled local criminal disputes and drug distribution. It was heavily connected to the Italian-American Mafia, supplied by the Lucchese crime family. The Council dissolved in 1983 after Barnes became a federal informant.

country_links.evidence_quote: Council-manufactured heroin began to be distributed across New York State, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, as far west as Arizona, and even into Canada .
country_links.context: The Council distributed its heroin into Canada.

The Covenant, the Sword, and the Arm of.description: Far-right survivalist anti-government militia advocating Christian Identity, active in the United States during the 1970s and early 1980s. Developed from a Baptist congregation founded in 1971 in Pontiac, Missouri, and later operated a compound in northern Arkansas. Dissolved after a 1985 siege and arrest of its leaders.

The Extraditables.description: Narcoterrorist organization created by Colombian drug lords in the early to mid 1980s to oppose extradition to the United States. Its members were largely drawn from the Medellín Cartel, led by Pablo Escobar. The group engaged in bombings, assassinations, and kidnappings to pressure the Colombian government. It was active from 1984 until Escobar's death in 1993.

The Family.description: The Family was an African-American organized crime group based in Newark, New Jersey, founded by Akbar Pray in the early 1970s. It was primarily involved in drug trafficking, particularly cocaine, and at its height had over 300 members. The group collapsed after Pray was sentenced to life in prison in 1990, becoming fragmented.

The Firm.description: English organized crime group based in Bethnal Green, London, led by the Kray twins from the late 1950s until their arrest in 1968. Involved in murder, armed robbery, arson, protection rackets, gambling, and assaults. The twins were convicted in 1969 and sentenced to life imprisonment.

The Johnson Gang.description: A group of Romanichal criminals from Cheltenham, Gloucestershire, who specialized in stealing fine art and antiques from English country houses over 20 years. The gang stole goods worth an estimated £30-80 million and were sentenced to a total of 49 years in prison in August 2008. Members included Ricky Johnson, his sons Richard and Albi, nephew Daniel O'Loughlin, and Michael Nicholls.

The Order.description: Neo-Nazi organization active in the United States from September 1983 to December 1984. Founded by Robert Jay Mathews, the group raised funds through armed robbery and was involved in the murder of radio host Alan Berg. Inspired by The Turner Diaries, it aimed to overthrow the U.S. government and establish a white homeland. The group was dismantled after a shootout that killed Mathews.

The Westies.description: The Westies were an Irish criminal gang based in Blanchardstown, west Dublin, Ireland. They controlled the heroin trade in west Dublin during the late 1990s and early 2000s, and were known for extreme violence against drug addicts and rival dealers. The gang also engaged in armed robberies and extortion. The organization imploded after the murders of all its leaders.

The Yiddishers.description: The Yiddishers were a London street gang based in Whitechapel, led by Alfred Solomon. Active during the inter-war years, they opposed the growing fascist movement in Great Britain and participated in the Battle of Cable Street in 1936. The gang included future mobster Jack Spot among its members.

The Yogurt Connection.description: A drug smuggling ring based in Indianapolis, Indiana, operating in the late 1970s and early 1980s. Organized by Linda Leary and her sons Richard and Paul Heilbrunn, it smuggled an estimated 250,000 pounds of marijuana from Colombia, Jamaica, and Thailand into eleven midwestern states, valued at $50-100 million. The ring used a health-food business as a front and laundered money through offshore accounts.

Thief in law.description: A formal status of criminal authority in the Soviet Union and post-Soviet states, denoting a professional criminal who follows specific traditions and holds elite status within organized crime and prison environments. Originating in the early 20th century, thieves in law are 'crowned' through rituals and tattoos by consensus of existing Vory. They operate within a code that includes rejecting work and assisting authorities, and are drawn from various nationalities across post-Soviet states.

Tijuana Cartel.description: Mexican drug trafficking organization based in Tijuana, Baja California, founded in 1989 by the Arellano Félix brothers after the fragmentation of the Guadalajara Cartel. It was one of the largest and most violent cartels in Mexico during the 1980s and 1990s, but has been weakened by arrests and deaths of its leaders. Since 2014, it has allied with the Jalisco New Generation Cartel, effectively merging into the CTNG.

Tiny Rascal Gang.description: Primarily Cambodian-American street gang based in Long Beach, California, founded in 1981 by Cambodian youth refugees for protection. Engages in drug trafficking, murder, robbery, and weapons trafficking. Has an estimated 5,000-10,000 members and associates as of 2009. Active in the United States and Canada.

Toa-kai.description: The Toa-kai is a yakuza syndicate based in Tokyo, Japan, founded in 1948 by Zainichi Korean mob boss Hisayuki Machii as the Tosei-kai. Originally a far-right anti-communist organization, it became one of Tokyo's most powerful gangs during post-war economic growth. The group is a member of the Kanto Hatsuka-kai federation and has aligned with the Yamaguchi-gumi. As of the infobox, it has an estimated 20 members.

country_links.evidence_quote: he brokered deals between the Korean government and the yakuza that allowed Japanese criminals to set up rackets in Korea. Thanks to Machii, Korea became the yakuza's home away from home. Befitting his role as fixer between the underworlds of both countries, Machii was allowed to acquire the largest ferry service between Shimonoseki, Japan, and Busan, South Korea...

Tokyo Boyz.description: Japanese American gang founded in 1942 at Manzanar concentration camp during World War II. Initially formed by rebellious youths due to harsh internment conditions, the gang engaged in petty crimes like stealing rations. After release, members continued criminal activities in California, with membership growing post-internment. The gang was active until 1996.

Tongan Crip Gang.description: The Tongan Crip Gang is a Tongan American street gang and a subset of the Crips alliance, founded in Inglewood, California. It is active in California, Utah, Alaska, Washington, and parts of Auckland, New Zealand. The gang engages in a wide range of criminal activities including drug trafficking, robbery, extortion, and murder. It was involved in a 2007 federal indictment for a conspiracy to murder members of MS-13.

country_links.evidence_quote: The gang is active in the U.S. states of California, Utah and Alaska, Washington and parts of Auckland, New Zealand.
country_links.context: The Tongan Crip Gang is active in parts of Auckland, New Zealand.

Tonton Macoute.description: Haitian paramilitary and secret police force created in 1959 by dictator François Duvalier. Known for brutal state terrorism, assassinations, and human rights abuses, it suppressed political opposition through violence and intimidation. Formally disbanded in 1986, but members continued terrorizing the country.

Toonerville Rifa 13.description: Mexican-American street gang based in Atwater Village, Los Angeles County, founded in the 1930s. Engages in murder, assault, drug trafficking, racketeering, and other crimes. Allied with the Mexican Mafia and Sureños, and rivals several other gangs. Still active.

Tottenham Mandem.description: Organised street gang based in Tottenham, North London, originating on the Broadwater Farm estate in the 1970s. Involved in drug trafficking, weapon trafficking, armed robbery, kidnapping, and contract killing. Controlled much of the drug markets in North London during the 1990s. Splintered into various groups by the mid-2000s.

Trafficante crime family.description: The Trafficante crime family is an Italian American Mafia crime family based in Tampa, Florida, founded around 1920 by Ignacio Antinori. It was most notably led by Santo Trafficante Jr., who was involved with the CIA in assassination plots against Fidel Castro. After his death in 1987, Vincent LoScalzo controlled the family until his death in 2025. The family is still active.

Tree Top Piru.description: The Tree Top Piru is a set of the Piru gang alliance, part of the Bloods, founded in Compton, California in the 1970s. Named after tree-named streets in its territory, it has spread to other U.S. states including Tennessee, Texas, and Maryland. The gang is known for its connection to rappers such as DJ Quik and YG, and has been involved in violent crimes including murder.

Tren de Aragua.description: Transnational criminal organization originating from Venezuela, formed around 2007 in Aragua state. Initially involved in extortion linked to a railway construction union, it consolidated power from 2013 at the Tocorón prison under Héctor 'Niño' Guerrero. Engages in drug trafficking, human trafficking, extortion, illegal mining, and money laundering across Latin America, the US, and Spain. Designated as a terrorist group by several countries.

Tren del Llano.description: Venezuelan criminal organization founded by José Antonio Tovar Colina alias 'El Picure' in 2008, initially operating in Guárico and Aragua as a car theft gang. Known as one of the first megagangs, it engages in drug trafficking, extortion, homicide, and kidnapping. The group opposes Nicolás Maduro's rule and has threatened opposition leader María Corina Machado. It remains active with an estimated 700 members.

Tri-City Skins.description: Ontario-based white power group active from 1997 to 2012 in the Kitchener-Waterloo and Cambridge area. James Scott Richardson was its most visible member. The group engaged in intimidation, assault, vandalism, and property crimes, with some members arrested for weapons and drug trafficking.

Tribesmen Motorcycle Club.description: The Tribesmen are a prominent outlaw motorcycle club based in the North Island of New Zealand, founded in 1980 in Murupara. They are known for their yellow colors and middle finger salute, and have chapters in Ōtara, Northland, Rotorua, Murupara, and Christchurch. The club was one of the first organized groups to import and manufacture methamphetamine in New Zealand, but lost influence due to overindulgence in their own product. As of 2020, they are considered the dominant gang in Christchurch.

Trimboli 'ndrina.description: The Trimboli 'ndrina is a clan of the 'Ndrangheta based in Platì, Calabria, Italy, founded in the 1970s by the brothers Natale, Rocco, and Saverio Trimboli. It emerged as a branch of the Barbaro 'ndrina and expanded into Northern Italy, particularly Volpiano, and Australia. The clan is involved in drug trafficking, extortion, money laundering, and other criminal activities. It remains active, with members arrested as recently as 2010.

Velentzas Organization.description: Greek-American criminal organization operating in New York City, founded by Peter Kourakos in the 1950s. Venice 13.description: Mexican American street gang based in the Oakwood neighborhood of Venice, Los Angeles, California. Founded in the 1920s or 1930s, it is one of the earliest gangs in the city. Venice Shoreline Crips.description: The Venice Shoreline Crips is a set of the Crips gang alliance based in Venice, Los Angeles, California. Formed in the late 1960s in the Oakwood neighborhood, it became heavily involved in narcotics trafficking during the 1980s crack epidemic. The gang has been engaged in violent conflicts with rival gangs such as Culver City 13 and Venice 13. Despite law enforcement efforts, it maintains control over its territory with hundreds of members.

Weather Underground.description: American Marxist militant organization active from 1969 to 1977, originally a faction of Students for a Democratic Society. It sought to overthrow the U.S. government through a bombing campaign targeting government buildings and banks, with no fatalities from its bombings. West End Gang.description: The West End Gang is a powerful criminal organization based in Montreal, Quebec, active since the early 1900s. It is recognized as part of the Irish mafia, with close ties to the Winter Hill Gang in Boston and alliances with the Rizzuto and Musitano crime families. The gang engages in theft, robbery, kidnapping, fraud, arms trafficking, and drug dealing, notably controlling cocaine and hashish distribution in the 1970s. It was part of the Consorzio, a drug cartel with Italian-Canadian families and Hells Angels. Current membership is estimated at 100-150, and the gang remains active under boss Gerald Matticks.

Westies.description: The Westies were a New York City-based Irish-American organized crime gang operating from the early 1960s until 1988. They were involved in racketeering, drug trafficking, and contract killing, and were partnered with the Italian-American Mafia. Based in Hell's Kitchen, Manhattan, they were responsible for 60-100 murders between 1968 and 1986. The gang was founded by James Coonan and led by Mickey Spillane before Coonan took over.

Westmob.description: Westmob is a primarily African-American street gang based in San Francisco, California, active since at least 1999. It claims territory in the Hunters Point projects and is known for a long-running conflict with the rival Big Block gang. The gang has been linked to rap music and drug trafficking, and its rivalry was featured in the 2002 documentary Straight Outta Hunters Point.

Westside Locos.description: Predominantly Latino-American street gang based in San Fernando Valley, Glendale, with history dating back to the 1950s. They reside mainly in the Riverside Rancho neighborhood and are known for murder. Their main subset is Chicos Malos or Lake street. The gang is part of a larger Locos 13 alliance throughout Los Angeles County.

White Fence.description: White Fence is a predominantly Mexican American street gang based in Boyle Heights, East Los Angeles, claiming origins as early as 1900 but emerging in the 1910s as a sports team associated with La Purissima Church. It is one of the oldest gangs in Los Angeles, known for early use of firearms and a long-running rivalry with El Hoyo Maravilla. The gang has a structured barrio-based culture and is allied with the Mexican Mafia and Sureños.

White Hand Gang.description: The White Hand Gang was a collection of Irish American gangs on the New York City, Brooklyn, and Red Hook waterfronts from the early 1900s to 1925. They organized against the growing influence of Italian gangsters, choosing their name as a response to the Sicilian Black Hand gangs. Known for being virulently anti-Italian and particularly violent, the gang suffered from unstable leadership and internal killings, leading to its demise.

White Tigers.description: The White Tigers were a Chinese American street gang based in New York City's Flushing, Queens, and northern Chinatown. Formed in 1980 by Cantonese and Taiwanese immigrants and American-born Chinese, they engaged in extortion, kidnapping, drug trafficking, and murder. Active from the early 1980s to the mid-1990s, they fought turf wars with rival gangs like the Green Dragons.

White Uno Gang.description: Italian criminal organization active from 1987 to 1994, primarily in Emilia-Romagna and Marche. Composed largely of police officers with right-wing extremist ties, the gang committed 102 heists, resulting in 24 deaths and 102 injuries. Founded by the Savi brothers, it was known for using a white Fiat Uno. The gang was dismantled in 1994 after police investigations.

Whitney gang.description: The Whitney gang was a family-based criminal organization from the Anfield district of Liverpool, England, active from the 1980s until 2011. They were involved in drug trafficking, specifically conspiracy to supply Class A drugs. In November 2011, members and associates were sentenced to a total of 82 years in prison. The gang was led by the Whitney family, including Carol, Leslie, Lisa, Paul, Anthony, and Gary Whitney.

Whyos.description: The Whyos were a dominant street gang in New York City from the late 1860s to the early 1890s, formed from remnants of Five Points gangs after police crackdowns. They controlled much of Manhattan, engaging in street fighting, murder, robbery, and extortion. The gang was predominantly Irish and required members to have killed at least once. They were eventually defeated by the Monk Eastman Gang.

Wilmas 13.description: Wilmas 13 is a Mexican American street gang based in Wilmington, Los Angeles, California, controlled by the Mexican Mafia. It has four sub-gangs and is involved in drug trafficking, arms trafficking, murder, and extortion. The gang has been subject to federal racketeering indictments and civil injunctions. Its leadership includes members of the Mexican Mafia operating from California state prisons.

Winter Hill Gang.description: The Winter Hill Gang was a loose confederation of American organized crime figures based in the Boston area, primarily active from 1961 to 2000. Founded by James 'Buddy' McLean and Howard 'Howie' Winter, it was predominantly Irish-American and involved in racketeering, drug trafficking, gambling, and weapons smuggling. The gang was the second most powerful criminal organization in New England after the Patriarca crime family. It was taken over by James 'Whitey' Bulger in 1979 and eventually dissolved.

Wo Hop To.description: Wo Hop To is a triad group based in Wan Chai, Hong Kong, founded in 1908 in Sai Ying Pun as a secret political organization opposing the Qing dynasty. It specializes in protection rackets and is affiliated with the Sun Yee On triad. During the early 1990s, it expanded into the United States, particularly San Francisco, where it controlled Chinatown illegal activities. It is one of the Four Major Gangs of Hong Kong.

It is involved in extortion, drug trafficking, gambling, and prostitution. The group has expanded its influence from Tsuen Wan to other parts of Hong Kong and operates globally, including in China, Macau, and Europe. X-Team.description: X-Team is a gang associated with the Bandidos Motorcycle Club, founded in Denmark in 1997 after the Nordic Biker War. Members are not required to own a motorcycle and act as a street gang recruiting young criminals to carry out crimes such as debt collection and drug dealing on behalf of the Bandidos. The gang had approximately 350 members at its peak in 2002 and operated in multiple countries. The Danish branch was eventually disbanded after the Bandidos lost control.

Yamaguchi-gumi.description: Japan's largest yakuza organization, founded in 1915 by Harukichi Yamaguchi in Kobe. It engages in extortion, gambling, prostitution, arms and drug trafficking, real estate kickbacks, and other criminal activities. Membership has declined sharply from its 1960s peak to 3,100 active members by 2025. The group operates across Japan and overseas, with headquarters in Kobe.

country_links.context: The Yamaguchi-gumi has territory in Hawaii, United States.

Yamaken-gumi.description: The Yamaken-gumi is a yakuza gang based in Kobe, Japan, founded in 1961 by Kenichi Yamamoto. It was the largest affiliate of the Yamaguchi-gumi until 2015, when it withdrew to form the Kobe Yamaguchi-gumi. After a period of independence, it rejoined the Yamaguchi-gumi in 2021. The group has an estimated membership of around 800.

Yellow Henry Gang.description: The Yellow Henry Gang was a 19th-century New Orleans street gang active during the early 1870s and late 1880s. Originally led by Turpo, it was taken over by "Yellow" Henry Stewart after Turpo's arrest in 1877. The gang engaged in burglaries, armed robberies, and extortions, attracting many prominent criminals. It disbanded after leader Henry died in prison in 1886 and briefly reformed in 1888 before final dissolution in 1892.

Yiddish Black Hand.description: Criminal organization and extortion ring operating on New York's Lower East Side in the early 20th century, led by Jacob 'Johnny' Levinsky. It targeted Jewish immigrant businessmen, particularly pushcart vendors and ice cream manufacturers, using anonymous threat letters. The group also engaged in assault, theft, and murder for hire.

Young Boys Inc..description: Young Boys Inc. was a major African American drug organization based in Detroit, Michigan, founded in 1976 by Dwayne Davis, Bernard Boykins, Reginald Chestnut, and Charles Lindsey. It pioneered inner-city street-corner heroin sales using minors as couriers to avoid severe penalties. The group expanded to other cities like Boston and controlled up to 80% of Detroit's heroin trade until its leadership was indicted and convicted in 1982.

Yüksekova Gang.description: The Yüksekova Gang was an illegal organization based in the Yüksekova district of Hakkari Province, Turkey, accused of killing 16 people. It had apparent links to the Turkish Gendarmerie's JITEM unit and possible links to the Ergenekon organization. The gang smuggled drugs and weapons, and its activities were first revealed in 1996 after the Susurluk scandal. Legal cases against the gang were sent to the European Court of Human Rights.

Zemun Clan.description: The Zemun Clan is a Serbian mafia organization based in Zemun, a municipality of Belgrade. It rose to prominence between 2000 and 2003, becoming one of the most powerful criminal groups in Southeast Europe. The clan is involved in drug trafficking, arms smuggling, extortion, and contract killings. Its leaders included Dušan Spasojević and Milorad Ulemek, and it had ties to Serbian state security services. The group was heavily targeted after the assassination of Prime Minister Zoran Đinđić in 2003.
